STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r27.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r27.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r27.claim: The discussion returns to the Israelites' later disobedience and the future punishments they are said to suffer for it.
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r27.anchor: the Israelites’ later disobedience and the future punishments they are said to suffer as a result (vv. 159–71)

IBNMUJAHID:v1p297/r1.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p297/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو
IBNMUJAHID:v1p297/r1.claim: Abu Amr reads يمسكون and ولا تمسكوا with doubled consonants; he alone doubles ولا تمسكوا, while the others lighten it.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p297/r1.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو ﴿ يمسكون ﴾ ﴿ ولا تمسكوا ﴾ مضمومتى الياء والتاء مشددتين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215/r1.speaker: ابن السكيت
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215/r1.claim: Ibn al-Sikkīt allows خلف صدق and خلف سوء for a good or bad successor, with the same form for singular and plural; he cites poetry.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215/r1.anchor: وقال ابن السكيت: يقال هذا خلف صدق وهذا خلف سوء ويجوز هؤلاء خلف صدق وهؤلاء خلف سوء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215/r2.speaker: النضر بن شميل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215/r2.claim: Al-Naḍr says both vocalized and unvocalized forms occur in the Qurʾān for the bad successor, while the good form is only vocalized; most linguists agree, except al-Farrāʾ and Abū ʿUbayda.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215/r2.anchor:
وقال النضر بن شميل:
التحريك والإسكان معا في القرآن الردى وأما الصالح فبالتحريك لا غير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215/r3.speaker: ابن الأنباري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215/r3.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī parses خلف as a collective plural of خالف, like راكب/ركب; Abū Ḥayyān rejects this because it behaves like a singular, unlike a collective noun.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215/r3.anchor: وأما جمع خالف كراكب وركب وشارب وشرب قاله ابن الأنباري، وليس بشيء لجريانه على المفرد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215/r4.speaker: ابن عباس وابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn Zayd identify those who inherited the scripture as Jews.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس وابن زيد: هنا هم اليهود

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī specifies Jews living in the Prophet's time: they inherited the Torah, read its commands and prohibitions, but did not act on them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215/r5.anchor: قال الزمخشري: وهم الذين كانوا في زمان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: ورثوا الكتاب التوراة بقيت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215/r6.speaker: الطبري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215/r6.claim: Al-Ṭabarī identifies them as the descendants of the Jews.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215/r7.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215/r7.claim: Mujāhid also identifies them as Christians.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215/r8.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215/r8.claim: Another report from Mujāhid identifies them as this Muslim community.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215/r9.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215/r9.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads ورثوا with ḍamma on the wāw and a doubled rāʾ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215/r9.anchor:
وقرأ الحسن:
ورثوا بضم الواو وتشديد الراء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215/r10.claim: Depending on whom the inherited group represents, الكتاب may refer to the Torah, Gospel, or Qurʾān.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215/r10.anchor: وعلى الأقوال يتخرج الكتاب أهو التوراة أو الإنجيل والقرآن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215/r11.claim: عرض هذا الأدنى denotes bribes and corrupt earnings; عرض is transient property, so the phrase belittles these gains.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215/r11.anchor: وعرض هذا الأدنى هو ما يأخذونه من الرشا والمكاسب الخبيثة والعرض ما يعرض ولا يثبت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215/r12.claim: Knowing their scripture's warnings, they altered it for public gain; this echoes the condemnation in 2:79.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215/r12.anchor: وأنهم مع علمهم بما في كتابهم من الوعيد على المعاصي يقدمون لأجل العامة على تبديل الكتاب وتحريفه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215/r13.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215/r13.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī derives الأدنى from low status, baseness, and smallness, as an alternative to temporal nearness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215/r13.anchor: قال الزمخشري: وإما من دنو الحال وسقوطها وقلتها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215/r14.claim: He derives الأدنى primarily from nearness: the worldly gain is close at hand, short-lived, and soon gone.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215/r14.anchor: والأدنى من الدنو وهو القرب لأن ذلك قريب منقض زائل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215/r15.claim: Their claim “we will be forgiven” presumptuously assigns God forgiveness while they persist in sin; inheriting scripture should have taught them not to presume pardon.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215/r15.anchor: ويقولون سيغفر لنا قطع على الله بغفران معاصيهم أي لا يؤاخذنا الله بذلك والمناسب إذ ورثوا الكتاب أن يعلموا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215/r16.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215/r16.claim: Grammatically, لنا occupies the position of the passive clause's deputy subject; another analysis treats the hidden pronoun as the source noun of يأخذون.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215/r16.anchor: ولنا في موضع المفعول الذي لم يسم فاعله، وقيل ضمير مصدر يأخذون أي سيغفر هو أي الأخذ لنا.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r1.claim: The conditional clause is a fresh statement of their immersion in sin: whenever a similar corrupt gain comes, they take it again and persist despite the warning.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r1.anchor: الظاهر أن هذا استئناف إخبار عنهم بانهماكهم في المعاصي وإن أمكنهم الرشا والمكاسب الخبيثة لم يتوقفوا عن أخذها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r2.claim: He invokes an unattributed report that the wrongdoer follows desire and then presumes upon God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r2.anchor: كما جاء والفاجر من أتبع نفسه هواها وتمنى على الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r3.speaker: أبو عبيدة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r3.claim: Abū ʿUbayda takes عرض, with fatḥa on rāʾ, to mean worldly goods available to both the righteous and wicked.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r3.anchor: العرض بفتح الراء متاع الدنيا قاله أبو عبيدة، يقال: إن الدنيا عرض حاضر يأخذ

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r4.claim: With sukūn on rāʾ, عرض means silver and gold, the principal forms of capital and compensation for damaged property.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r4.anchor: والعرض بسكون الراء الدراهم والدنانير التي هي رؤوس الأموال وقيم المتلفات

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r5.speaker: السدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r5.claim: Al-Suddī says people reproached the judge, but when a reproacher took office, he accepted bribes.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r5.anchor: قال السدي: كانوا يعيرون القاضي فإذا ولى المعير ارتشى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r6.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r6.claim: Another account says they took a litigant's bribe and then overturned their first ruling when a second bribe came.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r6.anchor: وقيل كانوا لو أتاهم من الخصم الأجر رشوة أخذوها ونقضوا بالرشوة الثانية ما قضوا بالرشوة الأولى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r7.claim: A cited couplet jokes that a case turns toward whoever pours oil into the lamp, using bribery as its image.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r7.anchor:
وقال الشاعر:
إذا ما صب في القنديل زيت ... تحولت القضية للمقندل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r8.claim: Another poem depicts access to officials bought by a covered tray, avoiding the doorkeeper's obstruction.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r8.anchor:
وقال آخر:
لم يفتح الناس أبوابا ولا عرفوا ... أجدى وأنجح في الحاجات من طبق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r9.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says this verse applies substantially to the Muslim community as well.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r9.anchor: ولهذه الأمة من هذه الآية نصيب وافر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r10.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r10.claim: The Prophet predicts that this community will follow the ways of those before it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r10.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «لتسلكن سنن من قبلكم»

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r11.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r11.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī reads the wāw in وإن يأتهم as circumstantial: they hope for forgiveness while persisting and repeating the same conduct; only repentance permits forgiveness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r11.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: الواو للحال يعني في وإن يأتهم أي يرجون المغفرة وهم مصرون عائدون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r12.claim: Abū Ḥayyān favors his preceding reading of the clause; he says a conditional sentence can, in fact, function circumstantially, so that grammatical objection does not decide the issue.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r12.anchor: وجمله على جعل الواو للحال لا للعطف مذهب الاعتزال والظاهر ما قدمناه ولا يرد عليه بأن جملة الشرط لا تقع حالا لأن ذلك جائز.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r13.claim: The covenant in scripture rebukes them and establishes that they must not lie about God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r13.anchor: هذا توبيخ وتقرير لما تضمنه الكتاب من أخذ الميثاق أنهم لا يكذبون على الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r14.speaker: ابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r14.claim: Ibn Zayd says they ruled for a bribing claimant from God's book, but when the opposing wrongdoer bribed them they produced their own forged book and ruled for him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r14.anchor: قال ابن زيد: كان يأتيهم المحق برشوة فيخرجون له كتاب الله ويحكمون له به

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r15.claim: The covenant is not limited to their claim that they would be forgiven; it covers that and every other false claim made about God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r15.anchor: وقال بعضهم: هو قولهم سيغفر لنا ولا يتعين ذلك بل هو أعم من هذا القول وغيره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r16.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r16.claim: He parses أن لا يقولوا as a بدل of ميثاق الكتاب; al-Zamakhsharī instead calls it an explanatory apposition and understands it as the covenant stated in scripture.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r16.anchor: وأن لا يقولوا في موضع رفع على البدل من ميثاق الكتاب، وقال الزمخشري: هو عطف بيان لميثاق الكتاب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r17.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r17.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says asserting forgiveness without repentance violates the scriptural covenant and falsely attributes to God what is not true.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r17.anchor: وفيه أن إثبات المغفرة بغير توبة خروج عن ميثاق الكتاب وافتراء على الله تعالى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r18.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r18.claim: If the covenant refers back to an earlier one, أن لا يقولوا can be purposive, meaning “so that they would not say,” or explanatory as a prohibition against false speech.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p215#2/r18.anchor: وإن فسر ميثاق الكتاب بما تقدم ذكره كان أن لا يقولوا مفعولا له ومعناه لئلا يقولوا

NAHHAS:v2p160/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p160/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p160/r3.claim: A r is not assimilated into l because it vibrates; l may assimilate into r, as in bal rāna ʿalā qulūbihim.
NAHHAS:v2p160/r3.anchor: ولا يجوز إدغام الراء في اللام لأن فيها تكريرا ويجوز إدغام اللام في الراء نحو بل ران على قلوبهم

NAHHAS:v2p160/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p160/r4.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p160/r4.claim: In wa-in yaʾtihim the conditional verb is jussive, so its final yāʾ drops; yaʾkhudhuhu is the response.
NAHHAS:v2p160/r4.anchor: ( وإن يأتهم ) جزم بالشرط فلذلك حذفت منه الياء والجواب ( يأخذه )

NAHHAS:v2p160/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p160/r5.speaker: الكسائي
NAHHAS:v2p160/r5.claim: Al-Kisāʾī reports that Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān read wa-dārasū mā fīhi, assimilating tāʾ into dāl.
NAHHAS:v2p160/r5.anchor: قال الكسائي وقرأ أبو عبد الرحمن ( وادارسوا ما فيه ) فأدغم التاء في الدال

SAMIN-DURR:7:169/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:169/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:169/r1.claim: ورثوا is a nominative adjective describing خلف, while يأخذون is a circumstantial clause describing the subject of ورثوا.
SAMIN-DURR:7:169/r1.anchor: في محل رفع نعتا ل " خلف " و " يأخذون " حال من فاعل

SAMIN-DURR:7:169/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:169/r2.speaker: الفراء
SAMIN-DURR:7:169/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ distinguishes خلف with quiescent lām for a succeeding generation from خلف with open lām for one appointed as successor.

SAMIN-DURR:7:169/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:169/r3.speaker: الزجاج
SAMIN-DURR:7:169/r3.claim: Al-Zajjāj says خلف denotes a generation that comes after another.
SAMIN-DURR:7:169/r3.anchor: وقال الزجاج: يقال للقرن يجيء بعد القرن خلف

SAMIN-DURR:7:169/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:169/r4.speaker: ثعلب
SAMIN-DURR:7:169/r4.claim: Thaʿlab reports common usage: خلف صدق is a good successor and خلف سوء a bad one; the anonymous verse with في خلف witnesses the latter.
SAMIN-DURR:7:169/r4.anchor: وقال ثعلب: " الناس كلهم يقولون: " خلف صدق " للصالح و " خلف سوء " للطالح

SAMIN-DURR:7:169/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:169/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:169/r5.claim: A proverb and anonymous verse use خلف with open lām for a successor; other cited lines show disagreement over the vowels for good and bad successors.
SAMIN-DURR:7:169/r5.anchor: ويعزى هذا أيضا إلى الفراء وأنشدوا

SAMIN-DURR:7:169/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:169/r6.speaker: حسان
SAMIN-DURR:7:169/r6.claim: Ḥassān’s line uses خلف with quiescent lām for a good successor, contrary to the distinction that reserves that form for the bad.

SAMIN-DURR:7:169/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:169/r7.speaker: النضر
SAMIN-DURR:7:169/r7.claim: Al-Naḍr allows both vowels for a bad successor but says the good takes open lām; most linguists agree, unlike al-Farrāʾ and Abū ʿUbayd, who allow quiescent lām for good.
SAMIN-DURR:7:169/r7.anchor: ولهذا قال النضر: " يجوز التحريك والسكون في الرديء، فأما الجيد فبالتحريك فقط "

SAMIN-DURR:7:169/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:169/r8.speaker: ابن الأنباري
SAMIN-DURR:7:169/r8.claim: The quiescent form may be a verbal noun, or a collective noun meaning خالف like ركب for راكب; the author says the latter is challenged because it inflects like a singular.
SAMIN-DURR:7:169/r8.anchor: اسم جمع خالف كركب لراكب وتجر لتاجر، قاله ابن الأنباري. وردوه عليه

SAMIN-DURR:7:169/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:169/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:169/r9.claim: The noun may derive from succession or from wine going bad; the same root describes changed mouth odor, as in the fasting hadith.
SAMIN-DURR:7:169/r9.anchor: واشتقاقه: إما من الخلافة، أي: كل خلف يخلف من قبله، وإما من خلف

SAMIN-DURR:7:169/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:169/r10.speaker: الحسن البصري
SAMIN-DURR:7:169/r10.claim: Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī reads ورثوا passively with a damma on wāw and doubled rāʾ; يأخذون may then begin a new sentence.
SAMIN-DURR:7:169/r10.anchor: وقرأ الحسن البصري: " ورثوا " بضم الواو وتشديد الراء مبنيا

SAMIN-DURR:7:169#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:169#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:169#2/r1.claim: ويقولون coordinates with يأخذون under either parsing, and سيغفر is its predicate.
SAMIN-DURR:7:169#2/r1.anchor: نسق على " يأخذون " بوجهيه و " سيغفر " معموله

SAMIN-DURR:7:169#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:169#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:169#2/r2.claim: The passive’s نائب فاعل may be لنا or an implied taking inferred from يأخذون: the taking of low worldly gain will be forgiven.

SAMIN-DURR:7:169#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:169#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:169#2/r3.claim: The conditional clause may be independent with no syntactic position, or the wāw may introduce a circumstantial clause.
SAMIN-DURR:7:169#2/r3.anchor: أحدهما: وهو الظاهر أنها مستأنفة لا محل لها من الإعراب

SAMIN-DURR:7:169#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:169#2/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:7:169#2/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī takes the wāw as circumstantial: they expect forgiveness while persisting in wrongdoing without repentance, which he says precludes forgiveness.
SAMIN-DURR:7:169#2/r4.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " الواو للحال، أي: يرجون المغفرة وهم مصرون

SAMIN-DURR:7:169#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:169#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:169#2/r5.claim: Zamakhsharī’s condition that forgiveness requires repentance reflects Muʿtazilī doctrine; Sunnis allow forgiveness without repentance because the agent is free.
SAMIN-DURR:7:169#2/r5.anchor: وأما أهل السنة فيجوز مع عدم التوبة لأن الفاعل مختار

SAMIN-DURR:7:169#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:169#3/r1.speaker: أبو عبيدة
SAMIN-DURR:7:169#3/r1.claim: With open rāʾ, عرض denotes all transient worldly goods other than the two currencies; with quiescent rāʾ it means dirhams and dinars.
SAMIN-DURR:7:169#3/r1.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: " العرض بالفتح جميع متاع الدنيا غير النقدين

SAMIN-DURR:7:169#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:169#3/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:169#3/r2.claim: On the broad meaning, the present world is transient property consumed by both the righteous and the wicked.
SAMIN-DURR:7:169#3/r2.anchor: وعلى الأول قيل: الدنيا عرض حاضر يأكل منها البر والفاجر

SAMIN-DURR:7:169#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:169#3/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:169#3/r3.claim: أن لا يقولوا may be a بدل from ميثاق because speaking truth is the covenant, or an explanatory apposition close in meaning.
SAMIN-DURR:7:169#3/r3.anchor: محله رفع على البدل من " ميثاق " لأن قول الحق هو ميثاق الكتاب

SAMIN-DURR:7:169#3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:169#3/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:7:169#3/r4.claim: If ميثاق الكتاب means the Torah’s rule that a grave sinner is forgiven only through repentance, أن لا يقولوا is a purpose clause meaning so that they not say.
SAMIN-DURR:7:169#3/r4.anchor: كان " أن لا يقولوا " مفعولا من أجله، ومعناه: لئلا يقولوا

SAMIN-DURR:7:169#3/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:169#3/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:169#3/r5.claim: أن may explain the covenant as a statement; on that analysis لا is prohibitive and makes the verb jussive, while the other analyses take لا as negative and أن as a subjunctive particle.
SAMIN-DURR:7:169#3/r5.anchor: و " أن " مفسرة لميثاق الكتاب لأنه بمعنى القول

SAMIN-DURR:7:169#3/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:169#3/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:169#3/r6.claim: الحق may be a direct object or cognate accusative; ميثاق is annexed to الكتاب because the covenant is mentioned in the book.
SAMIN-DURR:7:169#3/r6.anchor: يجوز أن يكون مفعولا به وأن يكون مصدرا

SAMIN-DURR:7:169#3/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:169#3/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:7:169#3/r7.claim: The most apparent parsing coordinates درسوا with ألم يؤخذ: the rhetorical question asserts that they took the covenant and studied, like 26:18.
SAMIN-DURR:7:169#3/r7.anchor: أظهرها ما قال الزمخشري وهو كونه معطوفا على قوله " ألم يؤخذ "

SAMIN-DURR:7:169#3/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:169#3/r8.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:7:169#3/r8.claim: Another analysis coordinates درسوا with ورثوا, with ألم يؤخذ as an intervening parenthesis; al-Baqāʾ reports that earlier authorities including al-Ṭabarī held it.
SAMIN-DURR:7:169#3/r8.anchor: قال أبو البقاء: " ويكون قوله " ألم يؤخذ " معترضا بينهما

SAMIN-DURR:7:169#3/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:169#3/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:169#3/r9.claim: A third analysis supplies قد before درسوا, making it circumstantial: they claim forgiveness while studying the book’s ban on bribes, or take the gain while studying it.
SAMIN-DURR:7:169#3/r9.anchor: والتقدير: وقد درسوا. قلت: وهو على هذا منصوب على الحال

SAMIN-DURR:7:169#4/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:169#4/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:169#4/r1.claim: Under either preceding syntactic analysis, the interrogative is parenthetical.

SAMIN-DURR:7:169#4/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:169#4/r2.speaker: الجحدري
SAMIN-DURR:7:169#4/r2.claim: Al-Jahdari reads the clause with second-person address; the author calls this a pleasing shift in person.
SAMIN-DURR:7:169#4/r2.anchor: وقرأ الجحدري: " أن لا تقولوا " بتاء الخطاب وهو التفات حسن

SAMIN-DURR:7:169#4/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:169#4/r3.speaker: علي وأبو عبد الرحمن السلمي
SAMIN-DURR:7:169#4/r3.claim: Ali and Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami read وادارسوا with a doubled dal, derived from تدارسوا like فادارأتم.
SAMIN-DURR:7:169#4/r3.anchor: وقرأ علي رضي الله عنه وأبو عبد الرحمن السلمي " وادارسوا " بتشديد الدال والأصل: تدارسوا

SAMIN-DURR:7:169#4/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:169#4/r4.speaker: ابن عامر ونافع وحفص
SAMIN-DURR:7:169#4/r4.claim: Ibn Amir, Nafi, and Hafs read تعملون in address; the other readers use third-person الغيبة.
SAMIN-DURR:7:169#4/r4.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر ونافع وحفص " تعملون " بالخطاب والباقون بالغيبة

SAMIN-DURR:7:169#4/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:169#4/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:169#4/r5.claim: The address reading may shift from third person while retaining the same referents for the pronouns.
SAMIN-DURR:7:169#4/r5.anchor: أحدهما: أنه التفات من الغيبة إلى الخطاب، والمراد بالضمائر حينئذ شيء واحد

SAMIN-DURR:7:169#4/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:169#4/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:169#4/r6.claim: Alternatively, the address is to this community: do you not understand and marvel at the earlier people's condition?
SAMIN-DURR:7:169#4/r6.anchor: والثاني: أن الخطاب لهذه الأمة، أي: أفلا تعقلون أنتم حال هؤلاء وما هم عليه

SAMIN-DURR:7:169#4/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:169#4/r7.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:7:169#4/r7.claim: The Shaykh assigns the third-person reading to Abu Amr and the Meccans, and the address reading to the remaining readers.
SAMIN-DURR:7:169#4/r7.anchor: ونقل الشيخ أن قراءة الغيبة لأبي عمرو وأهل مكة، وقراءة الخطاب للباقين

ZAJJAJ:v2p388/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p388/r1.speaker: قوم
ZAJJAJ:v2p388/r1.claim: One view says the heirs of scripture took bribes for unjust judgments.
ZAJJAJ:v2p388/r1.anchor: قيل إنهم كانوا يرتشون على الحكم، ويحكمون بجور

ZAJJAJ:v2p388/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p388/r2.speaker: قوم
ZAJJAJ:v2p388/r2.claim: A second view says they took bribes even when rendering just judgments; either way the gain was paltry.
ZAJJAJ:v2p388/r2.anchor: وقيل إنهم كانوا يرتشون ويحكمون بحق، وكل ذلك عرض خسيس

ZAJJAJ:v2p388/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p388/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p388/r3.claim: They expected forgiveness without repenting after taking bribes; taking another similar gain shows they persisted, although forgiveness for grave sins is promised with repentance.
ZAJJAJ:v2p388/r3.anchor: دليل على إصرارهم على الذنب، والله جل وعز وعد بالمغفرة في العظائم

ZAJJAJ:v2p388/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p388/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p388/r4.claim: They knew the covenant of scripture because they had studied what it contained.
ZAJJAJ:v2p388/r4.anchor: أي فهم ذاكرون لما أخذ عليهم

ASAD-NOTES:7:169#n135/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:7:169#n135/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:7:169#n135/r1.claim: Their expectation of forgiveness despite pursuing worldly gain reflects a persistent belief that descent from Abraham guarantees divine forgiveness and grace regardless of their conduct.
ASAD-NOTES:7:169#n135/r1.anchor: no matter what they do, His forgiveness and grace are assured to them by virtue of their being Abraham's descendants.

ASAD-NOTES:7:169#n136/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:7:169#n136/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:7:169#n136/r1.claim: Asad reads the claim of forgiveness as an erroneous belief that pardon can be gained without sincere repentance.
ASAD-NOTES:7:169#n136/r1.anchor: A reference to their erroneous idea that God's forgiveness could be obtained without sincere repentance.

ASAD-NOTES:7:169#n136/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:7:169#n136/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:7:169#n136/r2.claim: The divine writ referred to twice in this passage is the Bible.
ASAD-NOTES:7:169#n136/r2.anchor: The divine writ mentioned twice in this passage is obviously the Bible.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p96/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p96/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p96/r1.claim: Bint al-Shati rejects modern scientific readings that project atoms, spacecraft, gravity, Earth's rotation, or engineering onto the Quran; the first Muslims recognized its inimitable humanly unmatched Arabic expression.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p96/r1.anchor: لا أعرض هنا للذين خاضوا حديثاً فيما سموه "الإعجاز العلمي" وتأولوا فيه آيات قرآنية في اختراع الذرة وسفن الفضاء وقانون الجاذبية

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p96/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p96/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p96/r2.claim: She objects to unqualified interpreters importing modern science without linguistic or Islamic evidence, producing readings unsupported by specialists or the Quran's wording and spirit.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p96/r2.anchor: المحنة أن يؤلَّف فيه من ليسوا من أهل الاختصاص، وتروج في البيئة الإسلامية أقاويل وتأويلات مقحمة على القرآن نصاً وروحاً

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p96/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p96/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p96/r3.claim: She says no sound report has the Prophet teaching companions such scientific interpretations for them to understand or explain.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p96/r3.anchor: ولا شيء من هذا صح في أي خبر أن الرسول عليه الصلاة والسلام قاله لتلاميذه الصحابة لكي يفهموا هذا الإعجاز العلمي

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p75/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p75/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p75/r2.claim: The omitted preposition before “that they not say” can be fī, lām, ʿalā, or bāʾ, bringing four meanings together through ellipsis.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p75/r2.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون (في) (ألم يؤخذ عليكم ميثاق الكتاب في ألا تقولوا على الله إلا الحق)

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p121/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p121/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p121/r1.claim: He counts nine possible construals: four supplied prepositions, no deletion with the clause as apposition or substitution, مصدرية or تفسيرية “أن,” and negative or prohibitive “لا”; several meanings may be intended together.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p121/r1.anchor: إذن هناك تسعة احتمالات في هذه الآية الواحدة إحتمال حذف حرف الجر (الباء، في، على، اللام)

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p526/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p526/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p526/r1.claim: Omitting the preposition before the clause permits readings with bi-, li-, fī, or ʿalā, gathering their meanings and broadening the expression.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p526/r1.anchor: لذا فهذا التعبير يحتمل كل معاني الباء واللام وفي وعلى للتوسع في المعنى أي أنه جمع أربع معاني في معنى واحد بحذف الحرف

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p266/r10.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p266/r10.speaker: السلمي وعباس عن الضبي عن الأعمش
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p266/r10.claim: Al-Sulamī reads وادارسوا ما فيه, while ʿAbbās from al-Ḍabbī from al-Aʿmash reads وادكروا ما فيه; no argument is supplied here.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p266/r10.anchor: ومن ذلك قراءة السلمي: "وادارسوا ما فيه"4، وعباس عن الضبي عن الأعمش: "وادكروا ما فيه".

NASHR:v1p122/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p122/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p122/r1.claim: ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn ʿUmar died in 349 AH, aged over seventy; the author calls him an eminent, trustworthy reciter, grammarian, and authority, unmatched after Ibn Mujāhid.
NASHR:v1p122/r1.anchor: (وتوفي) عبد الواحد بن عمر في شوال سنة تسع وأربعين وثلاثمائة، وقد جاوز السبعين فيه، وكان إماما جليلا ثقة نبيلا

NASHR:v1p122/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p122/r2.speaker: الخطيب البغدادي
NASHR:v1p122/r2.claim: Al-Khaṭīb al-Baghdādī describes ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn ʿUmar as reliable and trustworthy.
NASHR:v1p122/r2.anchor: قال الخطيب البغدادي كان ثقة أمينا

NASHR:v1p122/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p122/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p122/r3.claim: Ibn Mujāhid, born in 245 and deceased in 324 AH, became the leading reading authority of his era; his circle had 300 senior readers and 84 deputies, and he was the first to canonize seven readings.
NASHR:v1p122/r3.anchor: وكان إليه المنتهى في زمانه في القراءة، وبعد صيته في الأقطار ورحل إليه الناس من البلدان وازدحم الناس عليه

NASHR:v1p122/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p122/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p122/r4.claim: Abū Aḥmad al-Sāmirī, born around 295–296 and deceased in 386 AH, was a reciter, linguist, and leading transmitter.
NASHR:v1p122/r4.anchor: وكان مقرئا لغويا مسند القراء في زمانه

NASHR:v1p122/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p122/r5.speaker: الداني
NASHR:v1p122/r5.claim: Al-Dānī calls al-Sāmirī famous, precise, trustworthy, and dependable, but says his long life weakened his memory and led to errors in his final years.
NASHR:v1p122/r5.anchor: قال الداني: مشهور ضابط ثقة مأمون غير أن أيامه طالت فاختل حفظه ولحقه الوهم

NASHR:v1p122/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p122/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p122/r6.claim: Although al-Sāmirī and al-Naqqāsh were criticized, the author accepts al-Dānī’s validation of both, their inclusion in al-Taysīr, and the community’s acceptance of their transmissions.
NASHR:v1p122/r6.anchor: وقد تكلم فيه وفي النقاش، إلا أن الداني عدلهما وقبلهما وجعلهما من طرق التيسير وتلقى الناس روايتهما بالقبول

NASHR:v1p122/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p122/r7.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p122/r7.claim: Ṣāliḥ died around 380 AH and was a skilled, prominent master reciter with a high chain of transmission.
NASHR:v1p122/r7.anchor: (وتوفي) صالح في حدود الثمانين وثلاثمائة، وكان مقرئا متصدرا حاذقا عالي السند مشهورا

NASHR:v1p122/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p122/r8.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p122/r8.claim: Ibn Shanabūdh, who died in 328 AH, was a celebrated, precise, upright imam who traveled widely and gathered an unusually large body of readings.
NASHR:v1p122/r8.anchor: وكان إماما شهيرا وأستاذا كبيرا ثقة ضابطا صالحا، رحل إلى البلاد في طلب القراءات واجتمع عنده منها ما لم يجتمع عند غيره

NASHR:v1p122/r9.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p122/r9.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p122/r9.claim: Ibn Shanabūdh permitted any soundly transmitted reading even when it conflicted with the written muṣḥaf; the issue was disputed but did not damage his reliability or integrity.
NASHR:v1p122/r9.anchor: وكان يرى جواز القراءة بما صح سنده، وإن خالف الرسم، وعقد له في ذلك مجلس كما تقدم وهي مسألة مختلف فيها

NASHR:v1p122/r10.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p122/r10.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p122/r10.claim: Qāḍī Abū Faraj died aged 85 in 390 AH and was a trustworthy imam, reciter, and jurist.
NASHR:v1p122/r10.anchor: (وتوفي) القاضي أبو فرج سنة تسعين وثلاثمائة عن خمس وثمانين سنة، وكان إماما مقرئا فقيها ثقة

NASHR:v1p122/r11.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p122/r11.speaker: الخطيب البغدادي
NASHR:v1p122/r11.claim: Al-Khaṭīb al-Baghdādī calls Qāḍī Abū Faraj the most learned of people.
NASHR:v1p122/r11.anchor: قال الخطيب البغدادي سألت البرقاني عنه فقال: كان أعلم الناس

NASHR:v1p122/r12.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p122/r12.speaker: أبو محمد عبد الباقي
NASHR:v1p122/r12.claim: Abū Muḥammad ʿAbd al-Bāqī says that all the sciences were present when Qāḍī Abū Faraj attended, and that he deserved a bequest for the world's most learned person.
NASHR:v1p122/r12.anchor: وعن أبي محمد عبد الباقي، إذا حضر القاضي أبو الفرج فقد حضرت العلوم كلها

NASHR:v1p268/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p268/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p268/r1.claim: Optional recitation forms authorize the reader to use any one of them; they do not require combining every form at the same location, including pause forms and alternatives at two silent letters.
NASHR:v1p268/r1.anchor: إنما المقصود بها معرفة جواز القراءة بكل منها على وجه الإباحة لا على وجه ذكر الخلف، فبأي وجه قرئ منها جاز

NASHR:v1p268/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p268/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p268/r2.claim: Some verifiers use only the strongest form and regard other forms as permitted; others let the reader choose, while some vary choices across locations to demonstrate the full oral transmission.
NASHR:v1p268/r2.anchor: وكذلك كان بعض المحققين لا يأخذ منها إلا بالأصح الأقوى، ويجعل الباقي مأذونا فيه، وبعض لا يلتزم شيئا

NASHR:v1p268/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p268/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p268/r3.claim: Combining every variant at every location is an uninformed strain; combining Hamza’s rare stop forms can train beginners, but is not required of proficient readers.
NASHR:v1p268/r3.anchor: أما من يأخذ بجميع ذلك في كل موضع فلا يعتمده إلا متكلف غير عارف بحقيقة أوجه الخلاف

NASHR:v1p268/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p268/r4.speaker: مشايخ الأندلس
NASHR:v1p268/r4.claim: Some Andalusian teachers use only one of Qālūn’s two plural-mīm forms, either sukūn or ṣila, following the clear wording that leaves him a choice.
NASHR:v1p268/r4.anchor: بلغني عن جلة مشيخة الأندلس - حماها الله - أنهم لا يأخذون في وجهي الإسكان والصلة من ميم الجمع لقالون

NASHR:v2p195/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p195/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p195/r1.claim: Traditional teachers allowed combined readings only after a student separately completed each reading and mastered its routes; combining too early was driven by impatience and a wish to advance quickly.
NASHR:v2p195/r1.anchor: ولم يكن أحد من الشيوخ يسمح به إلا لمن أفرد القراءات وأتقن معرفة الطرق والروايات، وقرأ لكل قارئ ختمة على حدة

NASHR:v2p195/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p195/r2.speaker: الكمال الضرير
NASHR:v2p195/r2.claim: Al-Kamāl al-Ḍarīr read al-Shāṭibī’s seven readings over nineteen full cycles, separating al-Bazzī and Qunbul before combining them; al-Shāṭibī later directed him to combine Abū al-Ḥārith with al-Dūrī.
NASHR:v2p195/r2.anchor: حتى أكمل القراءات السبع في تسع عشرة ختمة، ولم يبق عليه إلا رواية أبي الحارث وجمعه مع الدوري في ختمة

NASHR:v2p195/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p195/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p195/r3.claim: The author says his teachers required twenty-one separate cycles of the seven readings before combination, and likewise for the ten.
NASHR:v2p195/r3.anchor: فلم أعلم أحدا قرأ على التقي الصائغ الجمع إلا بعد أن يفرد السبعة في إحدى وعشرين ختمة وللعشرة كذلك

NASHR:v2p195/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p195/r4.speaker: عبد الوهاب القروي الإسكندري
NASHR:v2p195/r4.claim: ʿAbd al-Wahhāb al-Qarawī read the seven readings according to al-Iʿlān in forty full cycles with al-Qawṣī.
NASHR:v2p195/r4.anchor: وقرأ شيخنا عبد الوهاب القروي الإسكندري على شيخه الشهاب أحمد بن محمد القوصي بمضمن الإعلان في السبع أربعين ختمة

NASHR:v2p195/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p195/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p195/r5.claim: More lenient teachers allowed one cycle per reader, except that Nāfiʿ’s Qālūn and Warsh transmissions and Ḥamza’s Khalaf and Khallād transmissions each required a separate cycle.
NASHR:v2p195/r5.anchor: وكان الذين يتساهلون في الأخذ يسمحون أن يقرءوا لكل قارئ من السبعة بختمة سوى نافع وحمزة فإنهم كانوا يأخذون ختمة لقالون ثم ختمة لورش

NASHR:v2p195/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p195/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p195/r6.claim: The author recounts that he had completed Abū ʿAmr and Ḥamza separately with Ibn al-Sallār, but was denied general combination because he had not individually studied all readings; only Nāfiʿ and Ibn Kathīr could be combined.
NASHR:v2p195/r6.anchor: فلم يأذن لي، وقال: لم تفرد على جمع القراءات، ولم يسمح بأكثر من أن أذن لي في جمع قراءة نافع وابن كثير فقط

NASHR:v2p195/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p195/r7.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p195/r7.claim: Once a student has individually mastered and combined readings with a recognized teacher and been authorized, no further individual cycles are required before combining in one cycle; al-Qalānisī read al-Kāmil in one cycle with al-Hudhalī.
NASHR:v2p195/r7.anchor: فأراد أن يجمع القراءات في ختمة على أحدهم لا يكلفونه بعد ذلك إلى إفراد لعلمهم بأنه قد وصل إلى حد المعرفة والإتقان

NASHR:v2p438/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p438/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p438/r1.claim: When connecting the final sūra to the tahlīl, retain the final word’s original vowel or sukūn; assimilate tanwīn, as in «لخبير لا إله إلا الله».
NASHR:v2p438/r1.anchor: إذا وصل القارئ التهليل بآخر السورة أبقى ما كان من أواخر السور على حاله، سواء كان متحركا أو ساكنا إلا أن يكون تنوينا فإنه يدغم

NASHR:v2p438/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p438/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p438/r2.claim: Lengthening «لا إله إلا الله» is allowed as a devotional magnification; some teachers always lengthened it as remembrance, while most readers shortened it in keeping with their rule for separated madd, and both are accepted.
NASHR:v2p438/r2.anchor: ويجوز إجراء وجه مد " لا إله إلا الله " عند من أجرى المد للتعظيم كما قدمنا في باب المد

NASHR:v2p438/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p438/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p438/r3.claim: If takbīr belongs to the end of a sūra, pronounce it before stopping and begin the next sūra with basmala alone; if it belongs to the beginning, stop without it and pronounce it at the next sūra’s start.
NASHR:v2p438/r3.anchor: فمن قال: إن التكبير لآخر السورة كبر، وقطع القراءة

NASHR:v2p438/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p438/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p438/r4.claim: That end-versus-beginning distinction also governs the extra takbīr at prostration in the final sūra of al-ʿAlaq and at the transition to bowing in prayer.
NASHR:v2p438/r4.anchor: حتى لو سجد في آخر العلق فإنه يكبر أولا لآخر السورة، ثم يكبر للسجدة على القول بأن التكبير للآخر

NASHR:v2p438/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p438/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p438/r5.claim: If using Ḥamza’s takbīr between sūras according to those who permit it, the reader must include basmala by intending to stop at the previous sūra and begin a new one.
NASHR:v2p438/r5.anchor: لو قرأ القارئ بالتكبير لحمزة بين السورتين على رأي بعض من أجازه له فلا بد له من البسملة معه

NASHR:v2p27/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p27/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p27/r1.claim: Some reciters call assimilation with retained ghunna into wāw/yāʾ, and in some transmissions into lām/rāʾ, incomplete; without ghunna they call it complete.
NASHR:v2p27/r1.anchor: الإدغام بالغنة في الواو والياء، وكذلك في اللام والراء عند من روى ذلك هو إدغام غير كامل من أجل الغنة الباقية معه

NASHR:v2p27/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p27/r2.speaker: أبو الحسن السخاوي
NASHR:v2p27/r2.claim: Al-Sakhāwī argues that what is called assimilation while ghunna remains is actually concealment, with only a slight doubling.
NASHR:v2p27/r2.anchor: فقال: واعلم أن حقيقة ذلك إخفاء لا إدغام، وإنما يقولون له إدغام مجازا

NASHR:v2p27/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p27/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p27/r3.claim: The author prefers incomplete assimilation: retained ghunna is like the remaining emphatic sound in «أحطت» and «بسطت», and the audible shadda proves assimilation because concealment does not take shadda.
NASHR:v2p27/r3.anchor: (قلت) : والصحيح من أقوال الأئمة أنه إدغام ناقص من أجل صوت الغنة الموجودة معه

NASHR:v2p27/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p27/r4.speaker: الحافظ أبو عمرو
NASHR:v2p27/r4.claim: Abū ʿAmr defines complete assimilation as leaving no trace of the merged letter; retained nūn or tanwīn ghunna therefore resembles concealment, whereas removing it changes the letter fully into the following sound.
NASHR:v2p27/r4.anchor: قال الحافظ أبو عمرو: فمن أبقى غنة النون والتنوين مع الإدغام لم يكن ذلك إدغاما صحيحا في مذهبه

NASHR:v2p27/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p27/r5.speaker: أبو عمرو الداني
NASHR:v2p27/r5.claim: Al-Dānī restricts retained ghunna before lām to cases where the nūn remains in the written form; he omits it when the muṣḥaf omits that nūn, as in the cited Hūd and al-Kahf examples.
NASHR:v2p27/r5.anchor: وهذا اختيار الحافظ أبي عمرو الداني، وغيره من المحققين، قال في جامع البيان: واختار في مذهب من يبقي الغنة مع الإدغام عند اللام

QIRAAT-ER:7:169:47#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:7:169:47#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:7:169:47#1/r1.claim: The third-person plural they reason shifts the ending from a direct second-person challenge to commentary about the narrated group.
QIRAAT-ER:7:169:47#1/r1.anchor: shifts from direct audience challenge to third-person comment about the narrated group

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p240/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p240/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p240/r1.claim: Qatada says they take worldly gain whether lawful or unlawful, and whenever another such gain appears, lawful or unlawful, they take it.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p240/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ يأخذون عرض هذا الأدنى ﴾ قال يأخذونه إن كان حلالا وإن كان حراما

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p240#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p240#2/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p240#2/r1.claim: Saʿid b. Jubayr says they commit sins and tell themselves they will be forgiven.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p240#2/r1.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير في قوله تعالى ﴿ يأخذون عرض هذا الأدنى ﴾ قال يعملون بالمعاصي ويقولون سيغفر لنا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210#2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210#2/r1.claim: The book stipulates repentance for forgiveness; Abū Ḥayyān says the determinist doctrine on this point is precisely the Jewish doctrine.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210#2/r1.anchor: ودرسوا ما فيه أي ما في الكتاب من اشتراط التوبة في غفران الذنوب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210#2/r2.speaker: مالك بن دينار
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210#2/r2.claim: Mālik ibn Dīnār warns that people may fall short of commands yet presume forgiveness, while even their best compromise; such Muslims resemble those condemned in the verse.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210#2/r2.anchor: وقال مالك بن دينار رحمه الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210#2/r3.claim: Abū Ḥayyān characterizes the preceding account as following the Muʿtazilite approach.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210#2/r4.claim: The qualification إلا الحق shows they spoke falsely while taking worldly gain.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210#2/r4.anchor: وقوله: إلا الحق دليل على أنهم كانوا يقولون الباطل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210#2/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210#2/r5.claim: Abū Ḥayyān prefers connecting ودرسوا to the reproachful question ألم يؤخذ: they had studied and repeated the book, understood its warning, yet still lied.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210#2/r5.anchor: ودرسوا معطوف على قوله ألم يؤخذ وفي ذلك أعظم توبيخ وتقريع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210#2/r6.speaker: الطبري وغيره
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210#2/r6.claim: Al-Ṭabarī and others connect ودرسوا to ورثوا الكتاب; Abū Ḥayyān considers this unlikely.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210#2/r6.anchor: وقال الطبري وغيره: هو معطوف على قوله ورثوا الكتاب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210#2/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210#2/r7.claim: A third parse supplies an omitted قد, yielding وقد درسوا ما فيه; Abū Ḥayyān prefers the reproachful-question connection instead.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210#2/r7.anchor: وقيل هو على إضمار قد أي وقد درسوا ما فيه وكونه معطوفا على التقرير هو الظاهر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210#2/r8.speaker: الجحدري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210#2/r8.claim: Al-Jaḥdarī reads أن لا تقولوا with second-person address.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210#2/r8.anchor: وقرأ الجحدري أن لا تقولوا بتاء الخطاب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210#2/r9.speaker: علي والسلمي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210#2/r9.claim: ʿAlī and al-Sulamī read وادارسوا, from an original وتدارسوا, like فادارأتم from تدارأتم; this supports studying and repeatedly reviewing the book.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210#2/r9.anchor: وقرأ علي والسلمي: وادارسوا وأصله وتدارسوا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210#2/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210#2/r10.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects the sense that درسوا means they erased the book by abandoning its teaching: Arabic calls worn traces ربع دارس, not ربع مدروس.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210#2/r10.anchor: وهذه القراءة توضح أن معنى ودرسوا ما فيه هو التكرار لقراءته والوقوف عليه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210#2/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210#2/r11.claim: The afterlife reward is better than the vile, base bribe that brings disgrace in this life and the next; the God-fearing avoid God's prohibitions.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210#2/r11.anchor: أي ولثواب دار الآخرة خير من تلك الرشوة الخبيثة الخسيسة المعقبة خزي الدنيا والآخرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210#2/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210#2/r12.speaker: أبو عمرو وأهل مكة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210#2/r12.claim: Abū ʿAmr and the Meccans read يعقلون in the third person, matching the prior pronouns.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210#2/r12.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو وأهل مكة يعقلون بالياء جريا على الغيبة في الضمائر السابقة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210#2/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210#2/r13.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210#2/r13.claim: The majority read تعقلون as direct address, either turning to the Jews or addressing the Muslim audience to reflect on their conduct.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210#2/r13.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور بالخطاب على طريقة الالتفات إليهم أو على طريق خطاب هذه الأمة

ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r1.claim: The successors came after the people just mentioned, or after the righteous predecessors.

ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r2.claim: Khalaf with open lām means a bad successor, a verbal noun used adjectivally or a collective noun, and commonly denotes evil; an Arabic saying illustrates it.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r2.anchor: أي بدل سوء مصدر نعت به ولذلك يقع على الواحد والجمع

ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r3.claim: Khalf with sukūn on lām is often used for a good successor; some say it is specifically positive, while others treat the forms as synonymous for any successor.

ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r4.speaker: حسان
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r4.claim: Ḥassān’s verse uses khalf in praise of successors who follow in obedience to God.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r4.anchor: حسان : لنا القدم الأولى إليك وخلفنا لا ولنا في طاعة الله تابع

ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r5.speaker: لبيد
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r5.claim: Labīd’s verse uses khalaf in blame for the wretched company that remained.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r5.anchor: لبيد : ذهب الذين يعاش في أكنافهم وبقيت في خلف كجلد الأجرب

ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r6.speaker: البصريون
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r6.claim: The Basrans allow both vocalizations for bad successors but only open-lām for good ones; most linguists agree, except al-Farrāʾ and Abū ʿUbayda.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r6.anchor: عن البصريين أنه يجوز التحريك والسكون في الردى وأما الجيد فبالتحريك فقط

ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r7.claim: The word may derive from succession or corruption and change, as in the altered breath of a fasting person.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r7.anchor: اشتقاقه إما من الخلافة أو من الخلوف وهو الفساد والتغيير

ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r8.speaker: أبو حاتم
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r8.claim: Abū Ḥātim says khalf with sukūn means offspring, singular and plural alike, while khalaf with fatḥa is replacement, child or stranger.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r8.anchor: أبو حاتم : الخلف بالسكون الأولاد الواحد والجمع فيه سواء

ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r9.claim: Most identify the successors as contemporaries of the Prophet; they are apparently Jews, since they cannot be believers in him.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r9.anchor: الأكثرون على أن المراد بهؤلاء الخلف الذين كانوا في عصر رسول الله

ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r10.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r10.claim: Mujāhid identifies the successors as Christians, a view al-Ālūsī considers unsound.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r10.anchor: وعن مجاهد أنهم النصارى وليس بذاك

ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r11.claim: The book is the Torah; inheritance is figurative because successors possessed it and knew its contents after forebears.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r11.anchor: أي التوراة والوراثة مجاز عن كونها في أيديهم

ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r12.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r12.claim: Al-Hasan reads the verb as passive, with ḍamma and shadda.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r12.anchor: الحسن ( ورثوا ) بالضم والتشديد مبنيا لما لم يسم فاعله

ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r13.claim: The clause may independently describe what they did with the book after inheriting it; Abū al-Baqāʾ and others parse it as circumstantial to ‘they inherited.’
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r13.anchor: إستئناف مسوق لبيان ما يصنعون بالكتاب بعد وراثتهم إياه

ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r14.claim: ʿAraḍ denotes transient property and worldly chattels; theologians borrowed it for an accident as opposed to substance.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r14.anchor: والعرض مالا ثبات له ومنه إستعار المتكلمون العرض لمقابل الجوهر

ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r15.speaker: أبو عبيدة
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r15.claim: Abū ʿUbayda uses the vowelled form for worldly goods other than gold and silver, and the unvowelled form for money and value.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r15.anchor: أبو عبيدة : هو غير النقدين من متاعها وبالسكون المال والقيم

ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r16.claim: Al-adnā modifies an omitted ‘thing’ and means worldly life near relative to the afterlife, rather than the less likely sense ‘lowly.’
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r16.anchor: ( الأدنى ) صفة لمحذوف أي الشيء الأدنى

ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r17.claim: The worldly gain refers specifically to bribes in judgments and taking payment for distorting scripture.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r17.anchor: المراد بهذا العرض ما يأخذونه من الرشا في الحكومات

ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r18.claim: They claim God will pardon and overlook their sin; this clause coordinates with what precedes rather than being circumstantial.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r18.anchor: ولا يؤاخذنا الله تعالى بذلك ويتجاوز عنا والجملة عطف على ما قبلها

ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r19.claim: The passive verb may be construed with the prepositional phrase as complement, or with an implicit pronoun referring to them.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r19.anchor: والفعل مسند إلى الجار والمجرور وجوز أن يكون مسندا إلى ضمير يأخذون

ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r20.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r20.claim: The final clause may be circumstantial to ‘they say,’ understood as belief: they claim forgiveness while persisting in and repeating the same sin without repentance.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95#2/r20.anchor: في موضع الحال قيل من ضمير يقولون والقول بمعنى الاعتقاد

ALUSI-FULL:v9p96/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p96/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p96/r1.claim: The conditional clause can be circumstantial; that reading sharpens the rebuke because they hope for forgiveness while acting contrary to it.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p96/r1.anchor: إلا أن الحالية أبلغ لأن رجاءهم المغفرة في حال يضادها أوفق بالإنكار عليهم

ALUSI-FULL:v9p96/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p96/r2.speaker: الحلبي والسفاقسي
ALUSI-FULL:v9p96/r2.claim: They take the sentence as a new statement, not because a conditional clause cannot be circumstantial, but because that analysis has a Muʿtazilite tendency.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p96/r2.anchor: واختار الحلبي والسفاقسي أن الجملة مستأنفة لا لأن الجملة الشرطية لا تقع حالا

ALUSI-FULL:v9p96/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p96/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p96/r3.claim: The covenant is the one in the Torah: the annexation may mean a covenant contained in the Book or a covenant belonging to it; al-kitāb is definite by prior reference.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p96/r3.anchor: أي الميثاق المذكور في التوراة فالإضافة على معنى في ويجوز أن تكون إختصاصية

ALUSI-FULL:v9p96/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p96/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p96/r4.claim: The clause may explain the covenant, replace it, state its purpose, or attach to it through an implied preposition; أن may be infinitival or explanatory and لا prohibitive or negative.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p96/r4.anchor: عطف بيان للميثاق وقيل : بدل منه وقيل : إنه مفعول لأجله

ALUSI-FULL:v9p96/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p96/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p96/r5.claim: The heirs are rebuked for asserting that God must forgive them while they persist in sins and repeatedly return to them without repentance.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p96/r5.anchor: أنهم وبخوا على إيجابهم على الله تعالى غفران ذنوبهم التي لا يزالون يعودون إليها ولا يتوبون منها

ALUSI-FULL:v9p96/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p96/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v9p96/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says they were reproached for making forgiveness of their recurring, unrepented sins obligatory upon God.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p96/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما أنهم وبخوا على إيجابهم على الله تعالى غفران ذنوبهم

ALUSI-FULL:v9p96/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p96/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p96/r7.claim: The future particle س conveys emphatic certainty in their claim of forgiveness, as the authorities state.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p96/r7.anchor: وجاء البت من السين فإنها للتأكيد كما نص عليه المحققون

ALUSI-FULL:v9p96/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p96/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v9p96/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhshari accuses Sunnis of sharing the Jews’ view that sin may be forgiven without repentance, and says the Torah conditions forgiveness of grave sins on repentance.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p96/r8.anchor: عرض الزمخشري عامله الله تعالى بعدله في تفسير هذه الآية بأهل السنة وزعم أن مذهبهم هو مذهب اليهود

ALUSI-FULL:v9p96/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p96/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p96/r9.claim: Alusi rejects the comparison: Jews assert forgiveness categorically, while Sunnis do not guarantee it even for the obedient, much less sinners against God or other people.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p96/r9.anchor: فهل ما ادعاه إلا من قبيل ما جاء في المثل

ALUSI-FULL:v9p96/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p96/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p96/r10.claim: If al-Zamakhshari derived the Torah claim from this verse, it supports only that Torah distortions included altering prophetic descriptions, the stoning rule, and other laws for bribes and favors.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p96/r10.anchor: إلا على تحريفهم ما في التوراة من نعت النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم وآية الرجم

ALUSI-FULL:v9p96/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p96/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p96/r11.claim: Alusi notes that al-Zamakhshari himself accepts a comparable divine promise in the Quranic phrase about God forgiving some sins.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p96/r11.anchor: وقد سلم هو نحوا منه قوله سبحانه

ALUSI-FULL:v9p97/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p97/r1.speaker: شداد بن أوس
ALUSI-FULL:v9p97/r1.claim: Shaddad ibn Aws transmits the Prophet’s saying that the prudent person holds himself accountable and works for the afterlife, while the helpless follows desire and merely hopes in God; no grading is given.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p97/r1.anchor: عن شداد بن أوس أن رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم قال : الكيس من دان نفسه وعمل

ALUSI-FULL:v9p97/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p97/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p97/r2.claim: Their wrongdoing includes consuming people’s wealth unjustly, following desire, presuming on God’s mercy, and changing divine rulings to sell them for worldly gain.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p97/r2.anchor: ذموا بأكلهم أموال الناس بالباطل وإتباع أنفسهم هواها وتمنيهم على الله سبحانه

ALUSI-FULL:v9p97/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p97/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p97/r3.claim: They had studied the covenant to speak only the Torah’s truth, yet ruled against it, falsely attributed the ruling to God, and sought a small price.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p97/r3.anchor: فلم حكموا بخلافه وقالوا : هو من عند الله وما هو من عند الله ليشتروا به ثمنا قليلا

ALUSI-FULL:v9p97/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p97/r4.speaker: الجحدري
ALUSI-FULL:v9p97/r4.claim: Al-Jahdari reads أن لا قولوا with a second-person address, using a shift of address.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p97/r4.anchor: الجحدري ( أن لاقولوا ) بالخطاب على الإلتفات

ALUSI-FULL:v9p97/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p97/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p97/r5.claim: درسوا means they read the Book and therefore remember its contents.

ALUSI-FULL:v9p97/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p97/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p97/r6.claim: The clause most naturally coordinates by meaning with the covenant question: the covenant was taken and they studied the Book, despite the difference between declarative and interrogative forms.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p97/r6.anchor: وهو عطف على ( ألم يؤخذ ) من حيث المعنى وإن اختلفا خبرا وإنشاءا

ALUSI-FULL:v9p97/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p97/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p97/r7.claim: Other parses coordinate it directly with لم يؤخذ under the confirming question, with ورثوا while the question is parenthetic, or make the whole intervening question parenthetic.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p97/r7.anchor: وجوز كونه عطفا على ( لم يؤخذ ) والإستفهام التقريري داخل عليهما

ALUSI-FULL:v9p97/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p97/r8.speaker: الطبرسي
ALUSI-FULL:v9p97/r8.claim: Al-Tabarsi cites an interpretation of درسوا as abandoning and neglecting the Book when the clause is coordinated with ورثوا; Alusi finds it remote.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p97/r8.anchor: الطبرسي نقل عن بعضهم تفسير درسوا على هذا الوجه من العطف بتركوا وضيعوا وفيه بعد

ALUSI-FULL:v9p97/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p97/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p97/r9.claim: A further proposal makes the clause circumstantial of the subject of يقولوا, with an implied قد; Alusi considers this strained.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p97/r9.anchor: وقيل : إن الجملة في موضع الحال من ضمير يقولوا بإضمار قد

ALUSI-FULL:v9p97/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p97/r10.speaker: السلمي
ALUSI-FULL:v9p97/r10.claim: Al-Sulami reads ادارسوا with a doubled د and following alif, from تدارسوا after assimilation of ت into د and insertion of a connecting hamza.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p97/r10.anchor: وقرأ السلمي ( ادارسوا ) بتشديد الدال وألف بعدها

ALUSI-FULL:v9p97/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p97/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p97/r11.claim: The afterlife is better for those who fear God and His punishment and avoid the heirs’ conduct.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p97/r11.anchor: والدار الآخرة خير للذين يتقون ( الله تعالى ويخافون عقابه

ALUSI-FULL:v9p98/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p98/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p98/r1.claim: Addressing the covenant breakers who take worldly gain as believers intensifies the rebuke; another view addresses believers without a shift of address.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p98/r1.anchor: وهو خطاب لأولئك المأخوذ عليهم الميثاق الآخذين لعرض هذا الأدنى وفي الإلتفات تشديد للتوبيخ

ALUSI-FULL:v9p98/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p98/r2.speaker: نافع وابن عامر وابن ذكوان وأبو جعفر وسهل ويعقوب وحفص
ALUSI-FULL:v9p98/r2.claim: Some readers use third-person ياء; Nafi, Ibn Amir, Ibn Dhakwan, Abu Jafar, Sahl, Yaqub, and Hafs use second-person تاء.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p98/r2.anchor: وقرأ جمع بالياء على الغيبة وبالتاء وقرأ نافع وابن عامر وابن ذكوان وأبو جعفر

ALUSI-FULL:v9p98/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p98/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p98/r3.claim: The verse plainly rebukes their taking; some locate the reproach in their claim instead, yielding a paired, folded distribution of the two censures.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p98/r3.anchor: هذه الآية ظاهرة في التوبيخ على الأخذ

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295#2/r1.claim: Khalaf here means the generation that came after the people described earlier.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295#2/r1.anchor: والخلف: القرن الذي يجيء بعد قرن

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295#2/r2.speaker: أبو حاتم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295#2/r2.claim: With a still lām, khalaf means offspring, singular or plural; with a vowel, khalaf means a replacement, whether child or stranger.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295#2/r2.anchor: قال أبو حاتم: الخلف بسكون اللام الأولاد، الواحد والجمع فيه سواء، والخلف بفتح اللام: البدل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295#2/r3.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295#2/r3.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrābī says the form with fatḥa means righteous, while the form with sukūn means wicked.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295#2/r3.anchor: وقال ابن الأعرابي: الخلف بالفتح: الصالح، وبالجزم: الطالح

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295#2/r4.speaker: النضر بن شميل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295#2/r4.claim: Al-Naḍr says both vocalized and unvocalized forms can describe a bad generation, but only the vocalized form describes a good one.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295#2/r4.anchor: وقال النضر بن شميل: الخلف بتحريك اللام وإسكانها في القرن السوء واحد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295#2/r5.speaker: محمد بن جرير
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295#2/r5.claim: Ibn Jarīr says praise most often uses fatḥa and blame sukūn, though the reverse usages also occur.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295#2/r5.anchor: وقال محمد بن جرير: أكثر ما جاء في المدح بفتح اللام، وفي الذم بتسكينها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295#2/r6.claim: The later generation inherited the Torah from their forefathers.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295#2/r6.anchor: {ورثوا الكتاب} أي: انتقل إليهم الكتاب من آبائهم وهو التوراة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295#2/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295#2/r7.claim: ʿAraḍ means the goods of worldly life.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295#2/r7.anchor: فالعرض متاع الدنيا، والعرض، بسكون الراء، ما كان من الأموال

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295#2/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295#2/r8.claim: With a still rāʾ, ʿaraḍ denotes property other than dirhams and dinars.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295#2/r8.anchor: والعرض، بسكون الراء، ما كان من الأموال سوى الدراهم والدنانير

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295#2/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295#2/r9.claim: Al-adnā refers to this transient world, described as the perishing abode.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295#2/r9.anchor: وأراد بالأدنى العالم، وهو هذه الدار الفانية، فهو تذكير الدنيا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295#2/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295#2/r10.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295#2/r10.claim: The Jews inherited and read the Torah but neglected its commands, violated its rulings, took bribes in judgment, and altered God's words.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295#2/r10.anchor: وهؤلاء اليهود ورثوا التوراة فقرؤوها وضيعوا العمل بما فيها، وخالفوا حكمها، يرتشون في حكم الله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295#2/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295#2/r11.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295#2/r11.claim: They wish for forgiveness while persisting in wrongdoing, making a false presumption about God.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295#2/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295#2/r12.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295#2/r12.claim: The Prophet calls prudent the one who reckons with himself and works for the afterlife, and helpless the one who follows desire and merely hopes for God's pardon; the report is traced through Shaddād ibn Aws.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295#2/r12.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p296/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p296/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p296/r1.claim: Their greed and persistence mean they seize any similar worldly gain, lawful or unlawful, then again expect forgiveness.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p296/r1.anchor: إذا أشرف لهم شيء من الدنيا أخذوه حلالا كان أو حراما، ويتمنون على الله المغفرة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p296/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p296/r2.speaker: السدي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p296/r2.claim: Al-Suddī says Israelite judges took bribes; each excused himself by expecting forgiveness, then a successor who had criticized him did likewise.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p296/r2.anchor: وقال السدي: كانت بنو إسرائيل لا يستقضون قاضيا إلا ارتشى في الحكم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p296/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p296/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p296/r3.claim: The Torah covenant required them to speak only truth about God, forbidding their false claim that persistent sin would be forgiven.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p296/r3.anchor: أخذ عليهم العهد في التوراة أن لا يقولوا على الله الباطل، وهي تمني المغفرة مع الإصرار

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p296/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p296/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p296/r4.claim: The Torah contains no promise that sins committed in persistent disobedience will be forgiven.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p296/r4.anchor: وليس في التوراة ميعاد المغفرة مع الإصرار

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p296/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p296/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p296/r5.claim: Studying the book means reading it and reflecting on it repeatedly.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p296/r5.anchor: ودرس الكتاب: قراءته وتدبره مرة بعد أخرى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p296/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p296/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p296/r6.claim: They had read the covenant and remembered it; had they reasoned, they would have worked for the afterlife.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p296/r6.anchor: قرأوا ما فيه، فهم ذاكرون لذلك، ولو عقلوه لعملوا للدار الآخرة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p296/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p296/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p296/r7.claim: The afterlife is better for those who fear God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p296/r7.anchor: والدار الآخرة خير للذين يتقون أفلا تعقلون

BURSEVI:v3p205#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p205#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p205#2/r1.claim: The bad successors are Jews of the Prophet’s era, following earlier scattered Jewish communities that included both righteous and lesser people.
BURSEVI:v3p205#2/r1.anchor: من بعد المذكورين {خلف} أي : بدل سوء وهم الذين كانوا في عصر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم الذين

BURSEVI:v3p205#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p205#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p205#2/r2.claim: Khalaf is a verbal noun used adjectivally, so it can describe either one person or a group; here it means a bad replacement.
BURSEVI:v3p205#2/r2.anchor: والخلف : مصدر نعت به ولذلك يقع على الواحد والجمع

BURSEVI:v3p205#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p205#2/r3.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
BURSEVI:v3p205#2/r3.claim: Ibn al-Arabi distinguishes khalaf with fatḥa as a righteous successor and khalaf with sukūn as a bad one.
BURSEVI:v3p205#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن الأعرابي : الخلف بفتح اللام الصالح وبإسكان اللام الطالح

BURSEVI:v3p205#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p205#2/r4.speaker: محمد بن جرير
BURSEVI:v3p205#2/r4.claim: Ibn Jarir says praise usually uses fatḥa and blame sukūn, though either vowel can occur; he derives blame usage from milk left to sour, and compares spoiled breath and corrupt people.
BURSEVI:v3p205#2/r4.anchor: وقال محمد بن جرير : أكثر ما جاء في المدح بفتح اللام وفي الذم بتسكينها وقد يحرك في الذم ويسكن في المدح

BURSEVI:v3p205#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p205#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p205#2/r5.claim: Both vocalizations can denote good or evil, although good usage more often has fatḥa.
BURSEVI:v3p205#2/r5.anchor: والحاصل أن كليهما يستعملان في الشر والخير إلا أن أكثر الاستعمال في الخير بالفتح

BURSEVI:v3p205#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p205#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p205#2/r6.claim: They inherited the Torah from their forebears, reading it and knowing its contents.
BURSEVI:v3p205#2/r6.anchor: أي : التوراة من أسلافهم يقرؤونها ويقفون على ما فيها

BURSEVI:v3p205#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p205#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p205#2/r7.claim: “This lower thing” means worldly chattel: adnā can mean near and immediate, or low and base; here it refers to bribes in judgments and distorting scripture.
BURSEVI:v3p205#2/r7.anchor: يعني الدنيا وهو من الدنو ، أي القرب سميت هذه الدار وهذه الحياة دنيا لدنوها وكونها عاجلة

BURSEVI:v3p205#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p205#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p205#2/r8.claim: The worldly gains they took were bribes for judgments and for altering scripture’s words.
BURSEVI:v3p205#2/r8.anchor: والمراد ما كانوا يأخذونه من الرشى في الحكومات وعلى تحريف الكلام.

BURSEVI:v3p205#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p205#2/r9.speaker: الحدادي
BURSEVI:v3p205#2/r9.claim: Al-Haddadi says worldly goods are called “offered” because they pass quickly, like a cloud appearing and vanishing; he cites 46:24.
BURSEVI:v3p205#2/r9.anchor: قال الحدادي : سمي متاع الدنيا عرضا لقلة بقائه كأنه يعرض فيزول قال الله تعالى : {هاذا عارض ممطرنا} (الأحقاف : 24)

BURSEVI:v3p205#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p205#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p205#2/r10.claim: They assume God will not hold them to account but will cover and pardon their sin.
BURSEVI:v3p205#2/r10.anchor: لا يؤاخذنا الله بذلك ويتجاوز عنه يقال غفر الله له ذنبه غطى عليه وعفا عنه

BURSEVI:v3p205#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p205#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p205#3/r1.claim: The subject of “will forgive” may be the following prepositional phrase “for us,” or the implied pronoun may refer to taking the worldly gains, as in 5:8.
BURSEVI:v3p205#3/r1.anchor: قوله : سيغفر إما مسند إلى الجار والمجرور بعده وهو لنا وإما إلى ضمير الأخذ في يأخذون كقوله : {اعدلوا هو أقرب}

BURSEVI:v3p205#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p205#3/r2.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v3p205#3/r2.claim: The lower self exploits divine gifts and spiritual unveilings to gain wealth, rank, and pleasures, then deludedly claims its spiritual station licenses its sins, as antinomians do.
BURSEVI:v3p205#3/r2.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : من شأن النفوس أن يجعلوا المواهب الربانية والكشوف الروحانية ذريعة العروض الدنيوية

BURSEVI:v3p205#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p205#3/r3.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v3p205#3/r3.claim: Alternatively, they mean that God will forgive them after repentance, but they seek forgiveness only with the tongue, not the heart.
BURSEVI:v3p205#3/r3.anchor: وفيه معنى آخر وهو أنهم يقولون : سيغفر لنا إذا استغفرنا منها وهم يستغفرون باللسان لا بالقلب.

BURSEVI:v3p205#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p205#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p205#3/r4.claim: The clause “if a like gain comes” is circumstantial to the subject of “they say.”
BURSEVI:v3p205#3/r4.anchor: حال من فاعل يقولون ، أي : يأخذون الرشى في الأحكام وعلى تحريف الكلم للتسهيل على العامة

BURSEVI:v3p205#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p205#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p205#3/r5.claim: They claim God overlooks their worldly taking while remaining set on it, taking the same kind again without repentance.
BURSEVI:v3p205#3/r5.anchor: والحال إنهم مصرون على أخذه عائدون إلى مثله غير تائبين عنه

BURSEVI:v3p206/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p206/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p206/r1.claim: The covenant of the Book is the covenant stated in the Torah.
BURSEVI:v3p206/r1.anchor: ألم يؤخذ عليهم ميثاق الكتاب} أي : العهد المذكورة في التوراة.

BURSEVI:v3p206/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p206/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p206/r2.claim: The clause explains the covenant by apposition: they must not fabricate claims about God, such as certainty of forgiveness while persisting in sin.
BURSEVI:v3p206/r2.anchor: عطف بيان للميثاق ، أي : لا تفتروا على الله مثل القطع على المغفرة مع الإصرار على الذنب.

BURSEVI:v3p206/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p206/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p206/r3.claim: The Persian gloss says they read the Book yet did not find this ruling in it.
BURSEVI:v3p206/r3.anchor: (وخوانده اند آنه دروست واين حكم دروى نديده اند)

BURSEVI:v3p206/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p206/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p206/r4.claim: “They studied its contents” can attach by meaning to the assertive question, or directly to “was not taken”; the confirmatory question may govern both.
BURSEVI:v3p206/r4.anchor: وهو معطوف على ألم يؤخذ من حيث المعنى فإنه تقرير ، أي : أخذ عليهم ميثاق الكتاب ودرسوا ما فيه

BURSEVI:v3p206/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p206/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p206/r5.claim: The afterlife is better for those who avoid sins, associating partners with God, unlawful gain, and lying about God.
BURSEVI:v3p206/r5.anchor: للذين يتقون} المعاصي والشرك وأكل الحرام والافتراء على الله تعالى.

BURSEVI:v3p206/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p206/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p206/r6.claim: The rebuke asks whether they understand that they should not trade the lowly world, which brings punishment, for lasting bliss.
BURSEVI:v3p206/r6.anchor: تعلمون ذلك فلا تستبدلوا الأدنى المؤدي إلى العقاب بالنعيم المخلد.

DURR-FULL:v3p594/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p594/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v3p594/r1.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says they committed sins while assuring themselves they would be forgiven.
DURR-FULL:v3p594/r1.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير في قوله {يأخذون عرض هذا الأدنى ويقولون سيغفر لنا} قال: كانوا يعملون بالذنوب

DURR-FULL:v3p594/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p594/r2.speaker: عطاء
DURR-FULL:v3p594/r2.claim: Ata says they took whatever worldly gain came their way, then claimed they would seek forgiveness and repent.
DURR-FULL:v3p594/r2.anchor: عن عطاء في قوله {يأخذون عرض هذا الأدنى ويقولون سيغفر لنا} قال: يأخذون ما عرض لهم من الدنيا

DURR-FULL:v3p594/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p594/r3.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v3p594/r3.claim: Al-Suddi says Israelite judges took bribes in their judgments and excused themselves by saying they would be forgiven.
DURR-FULL:v3p594/r3.anchor: عن السدي قال: كانت بنو إسرائيل لا يستقضون قاضيا إلا ارتشى في الحكم

DURR-FULL:v3p594/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p594/r4.speaker: أبو الجلد
DURR-FULL:v3p594/r4.claim: Abu al-Jald warns of people whose hearts lose the Qur’an’s sweetness: they invoke forgiveness to excuse neglecting commands and violating prohibitions, live on hope without fear, and conceal wolf-like hearts beneath sheep skins; their best are self-indulgent.
DURR-FULL:v3p594/r4.anchor: عن أبي الجلد قال: يأتي على الناس زمان تخرب صدورهم من القرآن وتتهافت

DURR-FULL:v3p594/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p594/r5.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v3p594/r5.claim: Al-Hasan says believers accept God’s word as true, excel in deeds, and remain afraid even after giving a mountain of wealth; growing in piety makes them ask if they will be saved.
DURR-FULL:v3p594/r5.anchor: عن الحسن قال: المؤمن يعلم أن ما قال الله كما قال الله والمؤمن أحسن عملا

DURR-FULL:v3p594/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p594/r6.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v3p594/r6.claim: Al-Hasan contrasts the hypocrite, who thinks the crowd is large and forgiveness assured, so does evil while presuming upon God.
DURR-FULL:v3p594/r6.anchor: عن الحسن قال: المؤمن يعلم أن ما قال الله كما قال الله والمؤمن أحسن عملا

DURR-FULL:v3p594/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p594/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p594/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says their breach was claiming that God would forgive sins they repeatedly returned to without repenting.
DURR-FULL:v3p594/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس {ألم يؤخذ عليهم ميثاق الكتاب أن لا يقولوا على الله إلا الحق} فيما يوجهون على الله

DURR-FULL:v3p594/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p594/r8.speaker: ابن زيد
DURR-FULL:v3p594/r8.claim: Ibn Zayd says they had studied what was in the Book and therefore did not act from ignorance.
DURR-FULL:v3p594/r8.anchor: عن ابن زيد في قوله {ودرسوا ما فيه} قال: علموا ما في الكتاب

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1606#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1606#2/r1.speaker: ابن سعيد الخدري
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1606#2/r1.claim: Ibn Sa'id al-Khudri says the successors appeared sixty years later.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1606#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن سعيد الخدري في هذه الاية فخلف من بعدهم خلف قال : الخلف من بعد ستين سنة

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1606#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1606#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1606#2/r2.anchor: عن قتادة فخلف من بعدهم خلف اي والله لخلف سوء

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1606#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1606#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1606#2/r3.claim: Mujahid identifies these successors as this Muslim community.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1606#2/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد فخلف من بعدهم خلف قال : هذه الامة

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1606#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1606#2/r4.speaker: مجاهر
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1606#2/r4.claim: The report calls this community successors who follow one another like cattle, fearing no one in heaven and feeling no shame before people on earth.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1606#2/r4.anchor: عن مجاهر فخلف من بعدهم خلف قال : هم هذه الامة يترادفونه في الطرق كما ترادف الانعام

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1606#2/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1606#2/r5.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1606#2/r5.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the successors as Israelites and their counterparts among this community, the Murji'a.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1606#2/r5.anchor: عن السدي في قوله : فخلف من بعدهم خلف ورثوا الكتاب قال : هم من بني اسرائيل واشباههم من هذه الامة المرجئة

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1606#2/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1606#2/r6.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1606#2/r6.claim: Mujahid identifies the successors as Christians.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1606#2/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد فخلف من بعدهم خلف قال : النصارى

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1606#2/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1606#2/r7.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1606#2/r7.claim: Qatada identifies them as Jews and Christians.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1606#2/r7.anchor: عن قتادة فخلف من بعدهم خلف يعني اليهود والنصارى

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1606#2/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1606#2/r8.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1606#2/r8.claim: Qatada says they inherited scripture and its covenant from their prophets and messengers.
