IBNABIHATIM:v5p1606#2/r8.anchor: عن قتادة فخلف من بعدهم خلف اي والله لخلف سوء ورثوا الكتاب بعد انبيائهم ورسلهم

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1606#2/r9.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1606#2/r9.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1606#2/r9.claim: Ibn Zayd says Jews wrote a book opposing God's Book, called al-Mathna, in which the Torah's true and false were reversed.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1606#2/r9.anchor: سمعت ابن زيد في قوله : فخلف من بعدهم خلف ورثوا الكتاب قال : هؤلاء اليهود كتبوا كتابا ضادوا به كتاب الله يقال له المثناة

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1607/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1607/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير وإبراهيم
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1607/r1.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Ibrahim gloss the worldly gain they take as sins.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1607/r1.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير وابراهيم قالا : ياخذون عرض هذا الادنى قالا : الذنوب

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1607/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1607/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1607/r2.claim: Mujahid says they take whatever worldly thing tempts them each day, lawful or unlawful, then hope for forgiveness and take the same again when it appears.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1607/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد قوله : ياخذون عرض هذا الادنى قال : ما اشرف لهم في اليوم من شئ في الدنيا حلال أو حرام

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1607/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1607/r3.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1607/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak says the gain they take is unlawful.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1607/r3.anchor: عن الضحاك في قوله : ياخذون عرض هذا الادنى من الحرام

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1607/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1607/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1607/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd gives a different gloss, identifying the worldly gain as the books in their possession.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1607/r4.anchor: سمعت عبد الحرمن بن زيد يقول في قول الله : ياخذون عرض هذا الادنى قال : الكتاب الذين في ايديهم

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1607/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1607/r5.speaker: عطاء
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1607/r5.claim: Ata says they take whatever worldly thing is offered and say they will seek God's forgiveness and repent.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1607/r5.anchor: عن أبيه عطاء في قوله : ياخذون عرض هذا الادنى ويقولون سيغفر لنا ياخذون ما عرض لهم من الدنيا

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1607/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1607/r6.speaker: إبراهيم وسعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1607/r6.claim: Ibrahim and Sa'id ibn Jubayr explain a similar gain as sins, for which the sinners again expect forgiveness.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1607/r6.anchor: عن إبراهيم ، وعن سعيد بن جبير وان ياتهم عرض مثله ياخذوه قالا : الذنوب يقولون سيغفر لنا

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1607/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1607/r7.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1607/r7.claim: Mujahid says that when a similar worldly temptation appears the next day, they take it again, whether lawful or unlawful.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1607/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد قوله : وان ياتهم عرض مثله ياخذوه قال : ان وجدوا الغد مثله ياخذوه

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1608/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1608/r1.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1608/r1.claim: Al-Hasan says this covenant not to speak about God except the truth applied to the believers among them.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1608/r1.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله : الم يؤخذ عليهم ميثاق الكتاب ان لا يقولوا على الله الا الحق قال : هي لاهل الايمان منهم

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1608/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1608/r2.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1608/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak glosses the phrase as knowing what the Book contained.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1608/r2.anchor: عن الضحاك ودرسوا ما فيه قال : علموا ما فيه

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1608/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1608/r3.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1608/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd says they knew the Book and did not act from ignorance; he cites the wording 'you learned' in 6:105.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1608/r3.anchor: سمعت عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن اسلم في قوله : ودرسوا ما فيه قال : علموا ما في الكتاب لم ياتوه بجهالة

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1608/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1608/r4.speaker: الربيع
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1608/r4.claim: Al-Rabi glosses the phrase as reading what the Book contains and notes a lightened form.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1608/r4.anchor: عن الربيع ودرسوا ما فيه يعني فاقروا ما فيه يعني مخففة

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1608/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1608/r5.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1608/r5.claim: Al-Hasan says the promise that the Hereafter is better for the God-fearing is for the believers among them.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1608/r5.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله : والدار الاخرة خير للذين يتقون افلا تعقلون قال : هي لاهل الايمان منهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p160/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p160/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p160/r1.claim: خلف is a verbal noun used for an agent, meaning someone who succeeds or differs; its image comes from what is behind rather than in front.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p160/r1.anchor: وهو مصدر أريد به اسم الفاعل أي خالف ، والخلف مأخوذ من الخلف ضد القدام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p160/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p160/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p160/r2.claim: The successor group is not limited to one generation or century; context can make it extend through descendants, as in the later successors described at 19:59.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p160/r2.anchor: ولا حد لآخر الخلف ، بل يكون تحديده بالقرائن ، فلا ينحصر في جيل ولا في قرن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p160/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p160/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p160/r3.claim: “Inherited” is metaphorical for taking another’s place; the phrase means succeeding others in possession of Scripture, a reading that works whichever group is meant.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p160/r3.anchor: و { ورثوا } مجاز في القيام مقام الغير كما تقدم في قوله تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p160/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p160/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p160/r4.claim: The taking clause is circumstantial and condemns the successors; mentioning that they inherited Scripture first shows their misconduct was knowing and therefore worse.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p160/r4.anchor: ومهد لذلك بأنهم ورثوا الكتاب ليدل على أنهم يفعلون ذلك عن علم لا عن جهل ، وذلك أشد مذمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p160/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p160/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p160/r5.claim: Taking may be metaphorical for becoming involved in wrongdoing or literal for taking a thing into one’s possession.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p160/r5.anchor: ومعنى الأخذ هنا الملابسة والاستعمال فهو مجاز أي : يلابسونه ، ويجوز كونه حقيقة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p160/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p160/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p160/r6.claim: With both first vowels open, عرض means something transient and impermanent; it can refer to wealth or to available desires and benefits.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p160/r6.anchor: والعرض بفتح العين وفتح الراء الأمر الذي يزول ولا يدوم . ويراد به المال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p160/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p160/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p160/r7.claim: الأدنى literally means nearer in place but here means worldly life; the demonstrative hints at contempt for the gain, as in Qays ibn al-Khatim’s verse.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p160/r7.anchor: والأدنى الأقرب من المكان ، والمراد به هنا الدنيا ، وفي اسم الإشارة إيماء إلى تحقير هذا العرض

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p160/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p160/r8.speaker: سعيد بن جبير ومجاهد وقتادة والطبري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p160/r8.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, Qatada, and al-Tabari take the worldly gain as involvement in sins broadly, with taking used metaphorically for any manner of indulging in sin.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p160/r8.anchor: وبذلك فسر سعيد بن جبير ، ومجاهد ، وقتادة ، والطبري ، فيشمل كل ذنب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p160/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p160/r9.speaker: السدي ومعظم المفسرين
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p160/r9.claim: Al-Suddi and most commentators understand the gain as bribes and “taking” literally; Ibn Ashur says this better fits the next clause about similar gain coming to them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p160/r9.anchor: وقيل عرض الدنيا هو الرشا وبه فسرالسدي ، ومعظم المفسرين ، فيكون الأخذ مستعملا في حقيقته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p161/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p161/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p161/r1.claim: The claim may be spoken to people reproaching their sins, or may be inward self-talk that reassures them when a sense of restraint arises.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p161/r1.anchor: والقول في : { ويقولون } هو الكلام اللساني ، يقولون لمن ينكر عليهم ملابسة الذنوب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p161/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p161/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p161/r2.claim: The passive leaves God implicit as the known agent and generalizes the claim; the omitted object means “that” or “our sins.”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p161/r2.anchor: وبناء فعل ( يغفر ) على صيغة المجهول لأن الفاعل معروف ، وهو الله ، إذ لا يصدر هذا الفعل إلا عنه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p161/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p161/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p161/r3.claim: They presumptuously expect all their sins to be forgiven without repentance, as in their claim that the Fire would touch them only for a few days.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p161/r3.anchor: لأنهم يحسبون أن ذنوبهم كلها مغفورة { وقالوا لن تمسنا النار إلا أياما معدودة }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p161#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p161#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p161#2/r1.claim: لنا cannot be the passive subject: غفر takes one direct object, while the lām phrase expresses cause; compare شرح لك in 94:1, where لك could not become the نائب الفاعل either.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p161#2/r1.anchor: وقوله { لنا } لا يصلح للنيابة عن الفاعل ، لأنه ليس في معنى المفعول ، إذ فعل المغفرة يتعدى لمفعول واحد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p161#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p161#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p161#2/r2.claim: The claim of forgiveness is coordinated with their taking because both reports condemn them, and their combination intensifies the blame.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p161#2/r2.anchor: وجملة : { ويقولون سيغفر لنا } معطوفة على جملة ، { يأخذون } لأن كلا الخبرين يوجب الذم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p161#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p161#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p161#2/r3.claim: If عرض means money, its coming pictures an offer; if it means forbidden pleasures, its coming pictures the desire arising in them, though “coming” better suits concrete things.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p161#2/r3.anchor: واستعير إتيان العرض لبذله لهم إن كان المراد بالعرض المال ، وقد يراد به خطور شهوته في نفوسهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p161#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p161#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p161#2/r4.claim: They sin, assert their sins are forgiven, and continue sinning rather than desist.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p161#2/r4.anchor: والمعنى : أنهم يعصون ، ويزعمون أن سيئاتهم مغفورة ، ولا يقلعون عن المعاصي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p161#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p161#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p161#2/r5.claim: The question refutes their assertion by exposing its implication that God promised forgiveness; it is an aside addressed to the Prophet to use in argument against them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p161#2/r5.anchor: وجملة : { ألم يؤخذ عليهم ميثاق الكتاب } جواب عن قولهم : { سيغفر لنا } إبطالا لمضمونه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p161#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p161#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p161#2/r6.claim: The interrogative demands acknowledgment in order to rebuke them, since their own Scripture makes the covenant explicit.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p161#2/r6.anchor: والاستفهام للتقرير المقصود منه التوبيخ ، وهذا التقرير لا يسعهم إلا الاعتراف به

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p161#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p161#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p161#2/r7.claim: The Torah forbids adding to or subtracting from God's commands; it teaches repentance, not unearned forgiveness, so their claim falsely attributes a promise to God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p161#2/r7.anchor: ولا يجدون في الكتاب أنهم يغفر لهم ، وإنما يجدون فيه التوبة كما في الإصحاح من سفر التثنية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p162/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p162/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p162/r1.claim: The covenant is Moses’ testament, which he conveyed from God in many places; the Book is the Torah of Moses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p162/r1.anchor: والميثاق : العهد ، وهو وصية موسى التي بلغها إليهم عن الله تعالى في مواضع كثيرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p162/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p162/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p162/r2.claim: The genitive in “covenant of the Book” can mean a covenant within the Book or one known through it; أن may follow an omitted باء or explain the covenant in apposition.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p162/r2.anchor: وإضافة الميثاق إلى الكتاب على معنى ( في ) أو على معنى اللام أي الميثاق المعروف به

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p162/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p162/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p162/r3.claim: درسوا coordinates with يؤخذ, which has past force after لم; the implied sense is “was not a covenant taken and did they not study,” asserting their study rather than merely reporting it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p162/r3.anchor: وفعل { درسوا } عطف على { يؤخذ } ، . لأن يؤخذ في معنى المضي ، لأجل دخول لم عليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p162/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p162/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p162/r4.claim: The covenant and their study of the Book together establish the charge against them, since they knew what they had promised not to say about God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p162/r4.anchor: والمعنى : أنهم قد أخذ عليهم الميثاق بأن لا يقولوا على الله إلا الحق ، وهم عالمون بذلك الميثاق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p162/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p162/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p162/r5.claim: This clause is circumstantial: they knowingly violate Scripture while the afterlife is better than immediate gain, showing their choice was deliberate rather than careless.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p162/r5.anchor: وفي جعل الجملة في موضع الحال تعريض بأنهم يعلمون ذلك أيضا فهم قد خيروا عليه عرض الدنيا قصدا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p162/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p162/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p162/r6.claim: The reproach follows from the superiority of the afterlife; their preference for worldly gain treats them as irrational.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p162/r6.anchor: وقرينة ذلك قوله : { أفلا تعقلون } المتفرع على قوله : { والدار الآخرة خير للذين يتقون }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p162/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p162/r7.speaker: نافع وابن عامر وابن ذكوان وحفص عن عاصم ويعقوب وأبو جعفر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p162/r7.claim: Nafi, Ibn Amir, Ibn Dhakwan, Hafs from Asim, Yaqub, and Abu Ja'far read the verb with second-person tā’, shifting from narration to direct reproach; the remaining readers use third-person yā’ for indirect rebuke.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p162/r7.anchor: وقد قريء بتاء الخطاب ، على الإلتفات من الغيبة إلى الخطاب . ليكون أوقع في توجبه التوبيخ إليهم مواجهة ، وهي قراءة نافع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p163/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p163/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p163/r1.claim: Calling the afterlife better implies that the offenders lost its good by taking worldly gain, and calling it better for the God-fearing implies the gain-takers are not pious; the phrase compresses these meanings with miraculous eloquence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p163/r1.anchor: وهذه معان كثيرة جمعها قوله : { والدار الآخرة خير للذين يتقون أفلا تعقلون } وهذا من حد الإعجاز العجيب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r1.claim: Khalafa means a successor came after them; khalaf with still lām is usually blameworthy, though it can praise.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r1.anchor: خلف معناه حدث خلفهم وبعدهم خلف بإسكان اللام يستعمل في الأشهر في الذم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r2.speaker: لبيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r2.claim: Labid's line uses khalaf with a still lām in a blameworthy sense.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r2.anchor: ذهب الذين يعاش في أكنافهم ... وبقيت في خلف كجلد الأجرب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r3.speaker: حسان
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r3.claim: Hassan's verse shows that khalaf with a still lām can also be used approvingly.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r3.anchor: لنا القدم الأولى إليك وخلفنا ... لأولنا في طاعة الله تابع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r4.speaker: أبو عبيدة والزجاج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r4.claim: Abu Ubayda and al-Zajjaj say khalaf with fatḥa on lām is usually praiseworthy but can also be blameworthy.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r4.anchor: والخلف بفتح اللام يستعمل في الأشهر في المدح، قال أبو عبيدة والزجاج: وقد يستعمل في الذم أيضا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r5.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r5.claim: Mujahid identifies the khalaf here as Christians; al-Tabari rejects this identification.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r5.anchor: فخلف من بعدهم خلف ورثوا الكتاب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r6.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r6.claim: The majority read warithū al-kitāb in the ordinary form.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r7.speaker: الحسن البصري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r7.claim: Hasan al-Basri reads the verb with ḍamma on wāw and a doubled rāʾ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r7.anchor: وقرأ الحسن بن أبي الحسن البصري «ورثوا الكتاب» بضم الواو وشد الراء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r8.claim: The transient worldly gain refers to bribes and corrupt earnings; ʿaraḍ is passing and al-adnā points to worldly life.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r8.anchor: وقوله: يأخذون عرض هذا الأدنى إشارة إلى الرشا والمكاسب الخبيثة و «العرض» ما يعرض ويعن ولا يثبت،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r9.claim: Their claim of forgiveness is condemned because they knew the scriptural threat yet persisted and would repeat the sin for another gain.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r9.anchor: وقوله: ويقولون سيغفر لنا ذم لهم باغترارهم وقولهم: سيغفر مع علمهم بما في كتاب الله من الوعيد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r10.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r10.claim: The Prophet calls incapable the person who follows desire and merely wishes for forgiveness from God.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r10.anchor: كما قال صلى الله عليه وسلم: والعاجز من أتبع نفسه هواها وتمنى على الله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r11.claim: Only someone who has stopped sinning and repented should say he will be forgiven; these people presume forgiveness while persisting.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r11.anchor: فهؤلاء قطعوا بالمغفرة وهم مصرون وإنما يقول سيغفر لنا من أقلع وندم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r12.claim: The covenant requires truthful speech about God in rulings and judgments, and forbids bribes from turning judges toward falsehood.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r12.anchor: تشديد في لزوم قول الحق على الله في الشرع والأحكام بين الناس وأن لا تميل الرشا بالحكام إلى الباطل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r13.claim: The Book is the Torah, and its covenant refers to its stern instructions on this subject.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r13.anchor: والكتاب يريد به التوراة وميثاقها الشدائد التي فيها في هذا المعنى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r14.claim: The falsehood may mean unjust judgments or their claim God would forgive them despite knowing the prohibition.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r14.anchor: يمكن أن يريد بذلك قولهم الباطل في حكومة مما يقع بين أيديهم، ويمكن أن يريد قولهم سيغفر لنا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r15.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r15.claim: The majority read yaqūlū with yāʾ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r15.anchor: ألم يؤخذ عليهم ميثاق الكتاب أن لا يقولوا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r17.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r17.claim: Wa-darasū is coordinated with alam yuʾkhadh in the past sense, asserting the covenant was taken and they studied the Book.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r17.anchor: وقوله: ودرسوا معطوف على قوله: ألم يؤخذ الآية بمعنى المضي، يقدر: أليس قد أخذ عليهم ميثاق الكتاب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r18.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r18.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r18.claim: The Hereafter is better for those who fear God.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r19.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r19.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r19.claim: The majority read afalā taʿqilūn with tāʾ.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r20.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r20.speaker: أبو عمرو وأهل مكة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r20.claim: Abu Amr and the Meccans read yaʿqilūn with yāʾ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p472/r20.anchor: والدار الآخرة خير للذين يتقون أفلا تعقلون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p473/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p473/r1.speaker: الطبري وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p473/r1.claim: Al-Tabari and others coordinate wa-darasū with warithū al-kitāb.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p473/r1.anchor: وقال الطبري وغيره، قوله: ودرسوا معطوف على قوله: ورثوا الكتاب.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p473/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p473/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p473/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya finds that coordination unlikely because it removes the proof conveyed by the covenant question and weakens the admonition.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p473/r2.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: وفي هذا نظر لبعد المعطوف عليه لأنه قوله: ودرسوا يزول منه معنى إقامة الحجة بالتقدير

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p280/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p280/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p280/r1.claim: The later generation followed the people described earlier.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p280/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p280/r2.speaker: الجوني والجحدري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p280/r2.claim: Al-Jawnī and al-Jaḥdarī read خلف with fatḥa on the lām.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p280/r2.anchor: وقرأ الجوني والجحدري خلف بفتح اللام

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p280/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p280/r3.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p280/r3.claim: Abū ʿUbayda treats خلف and خلف as one word with the same meaning.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p280/r3.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة الخلف والخلف واحد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p280/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p280/r4.speaker: قوم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p280/r4.claim: Some distinguish the forms: lām with a vowel denotes the righteous, while a still lām denotes the unrighteous.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p280/r4.anchor: وقوم يجعلون المحرك اللام للصالح والمسكن لغير الصالح

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p280/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p280/r5.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p280/r5.claim: Ibn Qutayba says خلف means the inferior sort of people or speech, as in calling a statement خلف.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p280/r5.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة الخلف الرديء من الناس ومن الكلام

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p280/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p280/r6.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p280/r6.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī says Arabs usually use still-lām خلف for blameworthy things and vowelled-lām خلف for praiseworthy things, while allowing exceptions; this is the preferred distinction.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p280/r6.anchor: قال ابن الانباري أكثر ما تستعمل العرب الخلف باسكان اللام في الرديء المذموم وتفتح اللام في الفاضل الممدوح

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p280/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p280/r7.speaker: ابن عباس وابن زيد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p280/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn Zayd identify this later generation as the Jews.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p280/r7.anchor: أحدها أنهم اليهود قاله ابن عباس وابن زيد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p280/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p280/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p280/r8.claim: A second reported identification makes the later generation Christians.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p280/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p280/r9.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p280/r9.claim: Mujāhid is cited for identifying the later generation as Christians and, in another view, as people from Muhammad’s community.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p280/r9.anchor: والثالث أن الخلف من أمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم والقولان عن مجاهد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p280/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p280/r10.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p280/r10.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī explains the plural verb after singular خلف by taking خلف as the collective of خالف, as ركب is the collective of راكب.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p280/r10.anchor: أحدهما أن الخلف جمع خالف كما أن الركب جمع راكب والشرب جمع شارب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p280/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p280/r11.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p280/r11.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī’s second explanation is that خلف is a verbal noun usable for two or more, and for masculine or feminine; the passage also compares Maryam’s أضاعوا.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p280/r11.anchor: والثاني أن الخلف مصدر يكون للاثنين والجميع والمذكر والمؤنث

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p281/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p281/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p281/r1.claim: They received the Book as inheritance passing from predecessors to successors.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p281/r1.anchor: أي انتقل إليهم انتقال الميراث من سلف إلى خلف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p281/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p281/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p281/r2.claim: The inherited Book is variously identified as the Torah, Gospel, or Qurʾān.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p281/r2.anchor: فيخرج في الكتاب ثلاثة أقوال أحدها أنه التوراة والثاني الإنجيل والثالث القرآن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p281/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p281/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p281/r3.claim: The phrase means this worldly life and whatever worldly goods come within their reach.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p281/r3.anchor: أي هذه الدنيا وهو ما يعرض لهم منها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p281/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p281/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p281/r4.claim: Another explanation calls it عرض because it does not last long.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p281/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p281/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p281/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says they take whatever they desire, whether lawful or unlawful.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p281/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس يأخذون ما أحبوا من حلال أو حرام

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p281/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p281/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p281/r6.claim: A further view identifies the worldly gain as bribes in judicial decisions.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p281/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p281/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p281/r7.claim: Al-adnā is explained either as derived from nearness or as denoting baseness.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p281/r7.anchor: أحدهما أنه من الدنو والثاني أنه من الدناءة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p281/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p281/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p281/r8.claim: One explanation takes this as their false presumption that God will not hold them to account.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p281/r8.anchor: أن المعنى إنا لا نؤاخذ تمنيا على الله الباطل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p281/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p281/r9.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p281/r9.claim: Another explanation says they regard their sin as forgivable while hoping in God’s mercy.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p281/r9.anchor: أنه ذنب يغفره الله لنا تأميلا لرحمة الله تعالى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p281/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p281/r10.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p281/r10.claim: Al-Ḥasan says nothing satisfies them: they take more even when they have no need.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p281/r10.anchor: أن المعنى لا يشبعهم شيء فهم يأخذون لغير حاجة قاله الحسن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p281/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p281/r11.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p281/r11.claim: Mujāhid reads their repeated taking as persistence in sins.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p281/r11.anchor: أنهم أهل إصرار على الذنوب قاله مجاهد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p281#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p281#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p281#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says God bound them in the Torah to speak only truth about Him; they instead falsely presumed forgiveness for sins they would not repent of, though the Torah promises no forgiveness with persistence.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p281#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس وكد الله عليهم في التوراة أن لا يقولوا على الله إلا الحق فقالوا الباطل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p281#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p281#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p281#2/r2.claim: درسوا is coordinated with ورثوا; it means they read what the Book contained and so knowingly acted against it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p281#2/r2.anchor: معطوف على ورثوا ومعنى درسوا ما فيه قرؤوه فكأنه قال خالفوا على علم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p281#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p281#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p281#2/r3.claim: The Hereafter is better because of the reward it contains; the enduring is better than the passing for the God-fearing.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p281#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p281#2/r4.speaker: ابن عامر ونافع وحفص عن عاصم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p281#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir, Nāfiʿ, and Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim read the address with tāʾ; the other readers use yāʾ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p281#2/r4.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر ونافع وحفص عن عاصم بالتاء والباقون بالياء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p498#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p498#2/r1.speaker: السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p498#2/r1.claim: Al-Suddi says Israelite judges repeatedly took bribes despite a mutual covenant; each justified himself by saying God would forgive, while later appointees repeated the same practice.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p498#2/r1.anchor: وقال السدي [في] (4) قوله: {فخلف من بعدهم خلف} إلى قوله: {ودرسوا ما فيه} قال: كانت بنو إسرائيل لا يستقضون قاضيا إلا ارتشى في الحكم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p498#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p498#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p498#2/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir links the rebuke to the covenant requiring the People of the Book to make scripture clear and not conceal it, as in 3:187.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p498#2/r2.anchor: كقوله: {وإذ أخذ الله ميثاق الذين أوتوا الكتاب لتبيننه للناس ولا تكتمونه فنبذوه وراء ظهورهم واشتروا به ثمنا قليلا فبئس ما يشترون} [آل عمران:187]

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p498#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p498#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p498#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas explains their false claim that God would forgive as asserting forgiveness for sins they repeatedly commit without repenting.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p498#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن جريج: قال ابن عباس: {ألم يؤخذ عليهم ميثاق الكتاب أن لا يقولوا على الله إلا الحق} قال: فيما يوجبون على الله من غفران ذنوبهم التي لا يزالون يعودون فيها، ولا يتوبون منها.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p499/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p499/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p499/r1.claim: The afterlife and God’s reward are better for those who avoid prohibitions, resist their desires, and obey their Lord; the verse both encourages reward and warns of punishment.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p499/r1.anchor: يرغبهم تعالى في جزيل ثوابه، ويحذرهم من وبيل عقابه، أي: وثوابي وما عندي خير لمن اتقى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p499/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p499/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p499/r2.claim: The rebuke asks whether those trading the afterlife for worldly gain lack reason to restrain their foolishness and waste.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p499/r2.anchor: أفليس لهؤلاء الذين اعتاضوا بعرض الدنيا عما عندي عقل يردعهم عما هم فيه من السفه والتبذير؟

JISHUMI:v4p2765/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2765/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2765/r5.claim: The apparent reading درسوا means that they read the Scripture.
JISHUMI:v4p2765/r5.anchor: والقراءة الظاهرة: ودرسوا ما فيه يعني قرؤوا

JISHUMI:v4p2765/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2765/r6.speaker: السلمي
JISHUMI:v4p2765/r6.claim: Al-Sulami reads ادارسوا, meaning they studied together and read to one another, as in ادّاركوا.

JISHUMI:v4p2765/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2765/r7.speaker: الحسن
JISHUMI:v4p2765/r7.claim: The public reading has يعقلون in third person; al-Hasan reads تعقلون as direct address.

JISHUMI:v4p2765/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2765/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2765/r8.claim: Only the apparent, widely transmitted reading is admissible; anomalous forms may reflect a reading error, poor recitation, or belief that Quran may be read in all languages.
JISHUMI:v4p2765/r8.anchor: لا يجوز القراءة إلا بالظاهر والمستفيض

JISHUMI:v4p2765/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2765/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2765/r9.claim: If Quran means only the widely transmitted text, the objection about anomalous readings disappears.
JISHUMI:v4p2765/r9.anchor: القرآن هو المنقول المستفيض دون ما سواه، فلا شبهة فيه

JISHUMI:v4p2765/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2765/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2765/r10.claim: With a quiescent lām, خلف means a successor; with fatḥa, خلف is a replacement received for what was taken away.
JISHUMI:v4p2765/r10.anchor: الخلف بسكون اللام: من يجيء بعد، والخلف بفتحها

JISHUMI:v4p2765/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2765/r11.speaker: الفراء
JISHUMI:v4p2765/r11.claim: Al-Farra cites the expressions خلف سوء and خلف صدق as usage examples.
JISHUMI:v4p2765/r11.anchor: قال الفراء: يقال: خلف سوء، وخلف صدق

JISHUMI:v4p2765/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2765/r12.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
JISHUMI:v4p2765/r12.claim: Ibn al-Arabi reverses the usual distinction: fatḥa means righteous successor and sukūn means wicked successor.
JISHUMI:v4p2765/r12.anchor: وقال ابن الأعرابي: الخلف بالفتح: الصالح، وبالسكون: الطالح

JISHUMI:v4p2765/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2765/r13.speaker: لبيد
JISHUMI:v4p2765/r13.claim: Labid compares a خلف to the skin of a scabbed person as evidence for the term's usage.
JISHUMI:v4p2765/r13.anchor: قال لبيد: وبقيت في خلف كجلد الأجرب

JISHUMI:v4p2765/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2765/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2765/r14.claim: The sukūn form is more often blameworthy, perhaps deriving from milk left until spoiled; the fatḥa form is usually praise, though the forms can substitute for each other.
JISHUMI:v4p2765/r14.anchor: الأغلب على الخلف بالسكون أن يستعمل في الذم

JISHUMI:v4p2765/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2765/r15.speaker: علي بن عيسى
JISHUMI:v4p2765/r15.claim: Ali ibn Isa says the two forms may be used in place of each other.
JISHUMI:v4p2765/r15.anchor: قال علي بن عيسى: وقد يوضع أحدهما مكان الآخر

JISHUMI:v4p2765/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2765/r16.speaker: حسان
JISHUMI:v4p2765/r16.claim: Hassan's line uses خلفنا positively for a successor who follows the first generation in obeying God.

JISHUMI:v4p2765/r17.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2765/r17.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2765/r17.claim: An عرض is something that appears and does not remain long; the philosophical term for accident reflects that it appears in bodies without permanence, and clouds are also called عرض.

MUJAHID:v1p249#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p249#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p249#2/r1.claim: Mujahid identifies the later generation that inherited the Scripture as Christians.
MUJAHID:v1p249#2/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ فخلف من بعدهم خلف ﴾ يعني النصارى

MUJAHID:v1p249#2/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p249#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p249#2/r2.claim: They took any worldly gain that appeared to them, lawful or unlawful, whenever they desired it.
MUJAHID:v1p249#2/r2.anchor: ﴿ يأخذون عرض هذا الأدنى ﴾ يقول ما أشرف لهم من شيء من الدنيا حلالا كان أو حراما يشتهونه أخذوه

MUJAHID:v1p249#2/r3.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p249#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p249#2/r3.claim: They expected forgiveness and would take the same kind of worldly gain again if it appeared the next day.
MUJAHID:v1p249#2/r3.anchor: ويتمنون المغفرة وأن يجدوا الغد مثله يأخذوه

NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#4/r1.claim: The later generation is the people living in the time of the Messenger.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#4/r1.anchor: ﴿ فخلف من بعدهم ﴾ من بعد المذكورين ﴿ خلف ﴾ وهم الذين كانوا فى زمن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#4/r2.claim: Khalf with this form means a bad replacement, unlike khalaf, which means a righteous successor.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#4/r2.anchor: والخلفد البدل السوء بخلاف الخف فهو الصالح

NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#4/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#4/r3.claim: They inherited the Torah, knew its commands and prohibitions and its rules of permission and prohibition, but did not follow it.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#4/r3.anchor: التوراة ووقفوا على ما فيها من الأوامر والنواهى والتحليل والتحريم ولم يعملوا بها

NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#4/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#4/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#4/r4.claim: The lowly offering is worldly property and temporary benefit, near at hand compared with the afterlife.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#4/r4.anchor: هو حال من الضمير فى ورثوا والعرض المتاع أى حطام هذ الشئ الأدنى

NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#4/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#4/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#4/r5.claim: Calling it this lowly thing debases and belittles the worldly gain.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#4/r5.anchor: وفى قوله هذا الأدنى تخسيس وتحقير

NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#4/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#4/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#4/r6.claim: Taking the worldly offer is a circumstantial clause attached to the pronoun in ورثوا.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#4/r6.anchor: هو حال من الضمير فى ورثوا والعرض المتاع

NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#4/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#4/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#4/r7.claim: They assume God will not punish them for taking the bribes; the verb may refer to their taking or to the offer being taken.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#4/r7.anchor: لا يؤاخذه الله بما أخذنا والفعل مسند إلى الأخذ أو إلى الجار والمجرور

NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#4/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#4/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#4/r8.claim: If another similar offer comes, they take it again, hoping for forgiveness while persisting without repentance.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#4/r8.anchor: قوله تعالى يرجون المغفر وهم مصرون عائدون إلى مثل فعلهم غير تائبين

NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#4/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#4/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#4/r9.claim: The covenant is the pledge in their book to speak only the truth about God; this clause explains the covenant.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#4/r9.anchor: الميثاق فى مكتابهم إلا يقولوا على الله إلا الصدق وهو عطف بيان لميثاق الكتاب

NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#4/r10.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#4/r10.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#4/r10.claim: The clause means they read the book's contents and is coordinated with the question as a rhetorical affirmation.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#4/r10.anchor: وقرءوا ما فى الكتاب هو عطف على ألم يؤخذ عليهم لأنه تقرير

NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#4/r11.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#4/r11.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#4/r11.claim: The afterlife is better than that contemptible worldly gain for those who avoid bribes and forbidden acts.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#4/r11.anchor: من ذلك العرض الخسيس ﴿ للذين يتقون ﴾ الرشا والمحارم

NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#4/r12.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#4/r12.speaker: مدنى وحفص
NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#4/r12.claim: Medinan readers and Ḥafṣ read the verb with tāʾ.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:169/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169/r1.claim: The later khalaf means the children of those whom God dispersed through the land.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { فخلف من بعدهم خلف } يعني أولاد الذين فرقهم في الأرض

QURTUBI-FULL:7:169/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169/r2.speaker: أبو حاتم
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169/r2.claim: Abu Hatim says khalf with still lām means offspring, while khalaf with open lām means a replacement, child or stranger.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169/r2.anchor: قال أبو حاتم: «الخلف» بسكون اللام: الأولاد، الواحد والجميع فيه سواء. و «الخلف» بفتح اللام

QURTUBI-FULL:7:169/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169/r3.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169/r3.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrabi distinguishes righteous khalaf with fatḥ from blameworthy khalf with sukūn; Qurtubi says this is the common usage and the verse blames them.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169/r3.anchor: وقال ابن الأعرابي: «الخلف» بالفتح الصالح، وبالجزم الطالح

QURTUBI-FULL:7:169/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169/r4.speaker: لبيد
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169/r4.claim: Lubayd uses khalf for a deplorable successor, likening him to a scabrous skin.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169/r4.anchor:
قال لبيد:
ذهب الذين يعاش في أكنافهم

QURTUBI-FULL:7:169/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169/r5.claim: The Prophet says just people from every khalaf carry this knowledge, illustrating positive use.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169/r5.anchor:
قال صلى الله عليه وسلم:
" يحمل هذا العلم من كل خلف عدوله "

QURTUBI-FULL:7:169/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169/r6.claim: Although common usage distinguishes blameworthy khalf and praiseworthy khalaf, they can substitute for one another; Hassan's خلفنا is positive.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169/r6.anchor:
وقد يستعمل كل واحد منهما موضع الآخر. قال حسان بن ثابت:
لنا القدم الأولى إليك وخلفنا

QURTUBI-FULL:7:169/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169/r7.claim: An unattributed poem calls a khalaf bad; the text also reports خضف meaning a mound or embankment.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169/r7.anchor:
وقال آخر:
إنا وجدنا خلفا بئس الخلف
أغلق عنا بابه ثم حلف

QURTUBI-FULL:7:169/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169/r8.speaker: المفسرون
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169/r8.claim: The inheritors are Jews who read and learned God's Book but violated its rulings and prohibitions, so they are rebuked.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169/r8.anchor: قال المفسرون: هم اليهود، ورثوا كتاب الله فقرؤوه وعلموه، وخالفوا حكمه وأتوا محارمه

QURTUBI-FULL:7:169/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169/r9.claim: They eagerly take whatever worldly goods become available because of greed.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169/r9.anchor: ثم أخبر عنهم أنهم يأخذون ما يعرض لهم من متاع الدنيا لشدة حرصهم ونهمهم

QURTUBI-FULL:7:169/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169/r10.claim: With fatḥ rāʾ, ʿaraḍ means worldly goods; with sukūn, ʿirḍ means property other than coins.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169/r10.anchor: والعرض: متاع الدنيا بفتح الراء. وبإسكانها ما كان من المال سوى الدراهم والدنانير

QURTUBI-FULL:7:169/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169/r11.claim: The allusion is to bribes and illicit earnings.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169/r11.anchor: والإشارة في هذه الآية إلى الرشا والمكاسب الخبيثة

QURTUBI-FULL:7:169/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169/r12.claim: Their repeated taking shows they do not repent and will repeat the offense when able.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169/r12.anchor: ودل على أنهم لا يتوبون. قوله تعالى: { وإن يأتهم عرض مثله يأخذوه }

QURTUBI-FULL:7:169/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169/r13.claim: Only one who has stopped sinning and regrets it can properly expect forgiveness; they presume forgiveness while persisting.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169/r13.anchor: وأنهم بحال إذا أمكنتهم ثانية ارتكبوها، فقطعوا باغترارهم بالمغفرة وهم مصرون، وإنما يقول سيغفر لنا من أقلع وندم

QURTUBI-FULL:7:169/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169/r14.claim: Qurtubi says this condemned attitude also exists among people of his time.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169/r14.anchor: قلت: وهذا الوصف الذي ذم الله تعالى به هؤلاء موجود فينا

QURTUBI-FULL:7:169/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169/r15.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169/r15.claim: Muʿadh says people will recite a fading Quran without pleasure, wear sheep skins over wolf hearts, act from greed without fear, and persist while expecting forgiveness.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169/r15.anchor: عن معاذ بن جبل رضي الله عنه قال: سيبلى القرآن في صدور أقوام كما يبلى الثوب فيتهافت،

QURTUBI-FULL:7:169/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169/r16.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169/r16.claim: Another view identifies the pronoun with Jews of Yathrib in the Prophet's time, repeating their ancestors' conduct.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169/r16.anchor: وقيل: إن الضمير في «يأتهم» ليهود المدينة أي وإن يأت يهود يثرب

QURTUBI-FULL:7:169#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169#2/r1.claim: The covenant is the Torah and strictly requires truthful legal rulings, forbidding judges to take bribes or favor falsehood.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169#2/r1.anchor: يريد التوراة. وهذا تشديد في لزوم قول الحق في الشرع والأحكام، وألا يميل الحكام بالرشا إلى الباطل

QURTUBI-FULL:7:169#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169#2/r2.claim: The same duty binds Muslims through the Prophet and God's Book and applies across all revealed laws.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169#2/r2.anchor: وهذا الذي لزم هؤلاء وأخذ عليهم به الميثاق في قول الحق، لازم لنا على لسان نبينا

QURTUBI-FULL:7:169#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169#2/r3.claim: Here they read the Book while it was still recent to them.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169#2/r3.anchor: أي قرؤوه، وهم قريبو عهد به

QURTUBI-FULL:7:169#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169#2/r4.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169#2/r4.claim: Abu Abd al-Rahman reads وادارسوا, assimilating tāʾ into dāl.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169#2/r4.anchor: وقرأ أبو عبد الرحمن «وادارسوا ما فيه» فأدغم التاء في الدال

QURTUBI-FULL:7:169#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169#2/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169#2/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd says they used the Torah for a bribe-paying deserving claimant, but produced their own altered book for an unjust claimant.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169#2/r5.anchor: قال ابن زيد: كان يأتيهم المحق برشوة فيخرجون له كتاب الله فيحكمون له به،

QURTUBI-FULL:7:169#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169#2/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says they spoke falsely when claiming their sins were certainly forgiven.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169#2/r6.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: «ألا يقولوا على الله إلا الحق» وقد قالوا الباطل في غفران ذنوبهم

QURTUBI-FULL:7:169#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169#2/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169#2/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd instead applies their false speech to the rulings they issued.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169#2/r7.anchor: وقال ابن زيد يعني في الأحكام التي يحكمون بها كما ذكرنا

QURTUBI-FULL:7:169#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169#2/r8.speaker: بعض العلماء
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169#2/r8.claim: Some scholars take darasū to mean erasing the Book by failing to act on or understand it, like wind erasing traces.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169#2/r8.anchor: وقال بعض العلماء: إن معنى «ودرسوا ما فيه» أي محوه بترك العمل به والفهم له

QURTUBI-FULL:7:169#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169#2/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169#2/r9.claim: This sense fits the image of people of Scripture throwing God's Book behind their backs, including 3:187.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:169#2/r9.anchor: وهذا المعنى مواطىء أي موافق لقوله تعالى: { نبذ فريق من الذين أوتوا الكتاب كتاب الله ورآء ظهورهم }

RAZI-FULL:v15p36#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p36#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p36#2/r1.claim: The wording suggests the earlier generation was praiseworthy and the later one blameworthy, succeeding the righteous people previously described.
RAZI-FULL:v15p36#2/r1.anchor: ظاهره أن الأول ممدوح . والثاني مذموم ، وإذا كان كذلك ، فيجب أن يكون المراد : فخلف من بعد الصالحين

RAZI-FULL:v15p36#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p36#2/r2.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v15p36#2/r2.claim: Al-Zajjāj says khalaf is what replaces what was taken away, hence a generation succeeding another; both forms are used.
RAZI-FULL:v15p36#2/r2.anchor: قال الزجاج : الخلف ما أخلف عليك مما أخذ منك ، فلهذا السبب يقال للقرن الذي يجيء في إثر قرن خلف

RAZI-FULL:v15p36#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p36#2/r3.speaker: أحمد بن يحيى
RAZI-FULL:v15p36#2/r3.claim: Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā says people distinguish a good successor as khalaf ṣidq and a bad one as khalaf sūʾ, with khalaf reserved for blame.
RAZI-FULL:v15p36#2/r3.anchor: وقال أحمد بن يحيى : الناس كلهم يقولون خلف صدق وخلف سوء ، وخلف للسوء لا غير .

RAZI-FULL:v15p36#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p36#2/r4.speaker: لبيد
RAZI-FULL:v15p36#2/r4.claim: Some Arab authorities use both forms for good and bad; Labīd's verse is cited as evidence.
RAZI-FULL:v15p36#2/r4.anchor: وحاصل الكلام : أن من أهل العربية من قال الخلف والخلف قد يذكر في الصالح وفي الرديء ، ومنهم من يقول الخلف مخصوص بالذم قال لبيد .

RAZI-FULL:v15p36#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p36#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p36#2/r5.claim: Other grammarians derive blameworthy khalaf from corruption; bad speech is khalaf, as in the proverb about silence followed by a corrupt remark.
RAZI-FULL:v15p36#2/r5.anchor: ومنهم من يقول : الخلف المستعمل في الذم مأخوذ من الخلف ، وهو الفساد

RAZI-FULL:v15p36#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p36#2/r6.speaker: أبو عبيدة
RAZI-FULL:v15p36#2/r6.claim: Abū ʿUbayda distinguishes ʿaraḍ with fatḥa as worldly goods from ʿarḍ with sukūn as property other than gold and silver.
RAZI-FULL:v15p36#2/r6.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة جميع متاع الدنيا عرض بفتح الراء ، يقال الدنيا عرض حاضر يأكل منها البر والفاجر

RAZI-FULL:v15p36#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p36#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p36#2/r7.claim: The phrase means transient worldly goods; al-adnā belittles them as near at hand or low in rank and worth.
RAZI-FULL:v15p36#2/r7.anchor: والمراد بقوله : { عرض هاذا الادنى } أي حطام هذا الشيء الأدنى يريد الدنيا

RAZI-FULL:v15p36#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p36#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p36#2/r8.claim: The goods they accepted were bribes in legal judgments for distorting the revealed text.
RAZI-FULL:v15p36#2/r8.anchor: والمراد ما كانوا يأخذونه من الرشا في الأحكام على تحريف الكلام .

RAZI-FULL:v15p36#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p36#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p36#2/r9.claim: They minimized their sin and claimed God would forgive them, yet took another bribe whenever a similar offer arrived.
RAZI-FULL:v15p36#2/r9.anchor: ثم حكى تعالى عنهم أنهم يستحقرون ذلك الذنب ويقولون سيغفر لنا .

RAZI-FULL:v15p36#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p36#2/r10.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v15p36#2/r10.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads their repeated taking as evidence of greed for the world and unrestricted enjoyment of it.
RAZI-FULL:v15p36#2/r10.anchor: وقال الحسن هذا إخبار عن حرصهم على الدنيا وأنهم لا يستمتعون منها .

RAZI-FULL:v15p36#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p36#2/r11.speaker: غير مسمى
RAZI-FULL:v15p36#2/r11.claim: One explanation of the Torah covenant is that it barred altering scripture and religious laws to take bribes.
RAZI-FULL:v15p36#2/r11.anchor: قيل المراد منعهم عن تحريف الكتاب وتغيير الشرائع لأجل أخذ الرشوة

RAZI-FULL:v15p36#2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p36#2/r12.speaker: غير مسمى
RAZI-FULL:v15p36#2/r12.claim: Another explanation is that claiming forgiveness while persisting in sin was itself a false statement about God.
RAZI-FULL:v15p36#2/r12.anchor: وقيل : المراد أنهم قالوا سيغفر لنا هذا الذنب مع الإصرار ، وذلك قول باطل

RAZI-FULL:v15p37/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p37/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p37/r1.claim: Al-Rāzī rejects the inference that the Torah denies forgiveness for major sins: they claimed certain pardon, whereas Muslims hope for forgiveness and hold punishment ends.
RAZI-FULL:v15p37/r1.anchor: قلنا : أنهم كانوا يقطعون بأن هذه الكبيرة مغفورة ، ونحن لا نقطع بالغفران بل نرجو الغفران

RAZI-FULL:v15p37/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p37/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p37/r2.claim: They had studied the book and retained its teachings and covenant in memory.
RAZI-FULL:v15p37/r2.anchor: أي فهم ذاكرون لما أخذ عليهم لأنهم قد قرؤه ودرسوه .

RAZI-FULL:v15p37/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p37/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p37/r3.claim: The afterlife is better for the God-fearing than contemptible bribes; the verse asks whether they will reason.
RAZI-FULL:v15p37/r3.anchor: من تلك الرشوة الخبيثة المحقرة { أفلا يعقلون } .

QUSHAYRI:v1p364/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p364/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p364/r9.claim: The later heirs deserve blame because they preferred the low worldly gain and leaned toward transient life.
QUSHAYRI:v1p364/r9.anchor: استوجبوا الذم بقوله - سبحانه : { فخلف من بعدهم خلف } لأنهم آثروا العرض الأدنى ، وركنوا إلى عاجل الدنيا

QUSHAYRI:v1p364/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p364/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p364/r10.claim: They treated wishful expectation of the afterlife as their share while presuming they would be forgiven.
QUSHAYRI:v1p364/r10.anchor: وجعلوا نصيبهم من الآخرة المنى فقالوا : { سيغفر لنا }

QUSHAYRI:v1p364/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p364/r11.speaker: ويقال
QUSHAYRI:v1p364/r11.claim: A sign of gradual entrapment is committing sins, being deceived by the respite, and mistaking delayed punishment for proof of divine intimacy.
QUSHAYRI:v1p364/r11.anchor: ويقال من أمارات الاستدراج ارتكاب الزلة ، والاغترار بزمان المهلة ، وحمل تأخير العقوبة على استحقاق الوصلة

QUSHAYRI:v1p364/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p364/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p364/r12.claim: Their readiness to take another like gain reveals persistent self-delusion and preference for following desire.
QUSHAYRI:v1p364/r12.anchor: أخبر عن إصرارهم على الاغترار بالمنى ، وإيثار متابعة الهوى

QUSHAYRI:v1p364/r13.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p364/r13.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p364/r13.claim: The question about their covenant is a rhetorical confirmation that they were commanded to speak of God only with due reverence and perfection.
QUSHAYRI:v1p364/r13.anchor: استفهام في معنى التقرير ، أي أمروا ألا يصفوا الحق إلا بنعت الجلال ، واستحقاق صفات الكمال

QUSHAYRI:v1p364/r14.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p364/r14.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p364/r14.claim: One must not attribute to God a claim unsupported by revelation, proof, or sound reasoning.
QUSHAYRI:v1p364/r14.anchor: وألا يتحاكموا عليه بما لم يأت منه خبر ، ولم يشهد بصحته برهان ولا نظر

QUSHAYRI:v1p365/r17.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p365/r17.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p365/r17.claim: They had verified the Book’s contents and then denied them after clarification and proof appeared.
QUSHAYRI:v1p365/r17.anchor: يعني تحققوا بمضمون الكتاب ثم جحدوا بعد لوح البيان وظهور البرهان

QUSHAYRI:v1p365/r18.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p365/r18.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p365/r18.claim: For one hoping in God’s generosity, exposure to the breezes of His favor is better than exhausting oneself to obtain personal desires.
QUSHAYRI:v1p365/r18.anchor: يعني التعرض لنفحات فضله - سبحانه - خير لمن أمل جوده من مقاساة التعب ممن بذل - في تحصيل هواه - مجهوده

STUDYQURAN:7:169/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:169/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:169/r1.claim: The successors to Moses’ followers are understood as later Jews, especially religious leaders who corrupted Mosaic teaching and law by allowing commands and prohibitions to lapse.
STUDYQURAN:7:169/r1.anchor: The generation who succeeded the followers of Moses is understood by commentators to refer to some later Jews, and Jewish religious leaders in particular

STUDYQURAN:7:169/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:169/r2.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:7:169/r2.claim: Some commentators say Jewish leaders accepted bribes to ease legal requirements for certain people.
STUDYQURAN:7:169/r2.anchor: Some commentators suggest that certain Jewish leaders took bribery in exchange for easing the requirements of the law for certain people

STUDYQURAN:7:169/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:169/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:169/r3.claim: Quran 19:59 similarly describes Abraham’s and Israel’s descendants being succeeded by a generation that neglected prayer and followed base desires.
STUDYQURAN:7:169/r3.anchor: See also 19:59, regarding the descendants of Abraham and Israel: Then they were succeeded by a generation who neglected prayer and followed base desires

STUDYQURAN:7:169/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:169/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:169/r4.claim: They take whatever fleeting worldly goods they desire, lawful or unlawful and even sinful, while assuming they will be forgiven.
STUDYQURAN:7:169/r4.anchor: they take whatever they desire of fleeting, worldly things, whether they are lawful or unlawful, or even sinful, and assume they will be forgiven for it

STUDYQURAN:7:169/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:169/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:169/r5.claim: The claim that punishment will be brief reflects overconfidence in God’s leniency attributed to some Jews.
STUDYQURAN:7:169/r5.anchor: certain Jews were overly confident about God’s leniency in judgment toward them

STUDYQURAN:7:169/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:169/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:169/r6.claim: Their taking similar worldly gains again shows they are not repentant and intend to persist in disobedience.
STUDYQURAN:7:169/r6.anchor: indicating that they are not truly repentant, and that their intention is to persist in their acts of disobedience

STUDYQURAN:7:169/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:169/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:169/r7.claim: The Book’s covenant refers to Torah obligations, including speaking truthfully about God according to scripture.
STUDYQURAN:7:169/r7.anchor: the covenantal obligations imposed on the Jews by the Torah, one of which was to speak only truthfully about God in accordance with what is taught in the scripture

STUDYQURAN:7:169/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:169/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:169/r8.claim: Scripture teaches that forgiveness belongs to those who repent and amend their ways, not those persisting in error.
STUDYQURAN:7:169/r8.anchor: God’s forgiveness is only for those who are truly repentant and mend their ways, not for those who persist in their errors

STUDYQURAN:7:169/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:169/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:169/r9.claim: Other verses also say that the Hereafter is better for the reverent than this world.
STUDYQURAN:7:169/r9.anchor: That for the reverent the Hereafter is better than this world is also mentioned

TAB-FULL:v10p534#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p534#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p534#2/r1.claim: Khalaf here means a bad successor who came after and replaced the preceding people; Arabic says “good successor” and “bad successor.”
TAB-FULL:v10p534#2/r1.anchor: خلف سوء، يقول: حدث بعدهم وخلافهم، وتبدل منهم بدل سوء، يقال منه: هو خلف صدق، وخلف سوء

TAB-FULL:v10p534#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p534#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p534#2/r2.claim: The lām is usually open in praise and silent in blame, though usage can reverse; Ḥassān gives a blame-form with silent lām used approvingly.
TAB-FULL:v10p534#2/r2.anchor: وأكثر ما جاء في المدح بفتح اللام وفي الذم بتسكينها، وقد تحرك في الذم وتسكن في المدح

TAB-FULL:v10p534#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p534#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p534#2/r3.claim: Ḥassān's line shows the lām-sukūn form used approvingly for successors who follow their forebears in obedience.

TAB-FULL:v10p534#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p534#2/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p534#2/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabarī conjectures that blameworthy khalaf may derive from milk left until sour, or perhaps from the changed odor of a fasting person's mouth.
TAB-FULL:v10p534#2/r4.anchor: وأحسب أنه إذا وجه إلى الفساد مأخوذ من قولهم: خلف اللبن: إذا حمض من طول تركه في السقاء حتى يفسد

TAB-FULL:v10p534#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p534#2/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p534#2/r5.claim: Labīd's line supplies an example of khalaf with silent lām used disparagingly.
TAB-FULL:v10p534#2/r5.anchor: ذهب الذين يعاش في أكنافهم … وبقيت في خلف كجلد الأجرب

TAB-FULL:v10p534#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p534#2/r6.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v10p534#2/r6.claim: Mujāhid identifies the successors in this verse as Christians.
TAB-FULL:v10p534#2/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قول الله: " {فخلف من بعدهم خلف} [الأعراف: 169] قال: النصارى

TAB-FULL:v10p534#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p534#2/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p534#2/r7.claim: Al-Ṭabarī rejects a specific Christian identification: the text does not name them, the account fits Jews better, and context before and after concerns the Children of Israel.
TAB-FULL:v10p534#2/r7.anchor: ولم يذكر لنا أنهم نصارى في كتابه، وقصتهم بقصص اليهود أشبه منها بقصص النصارى

TAB-FULL:v10p534#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p534#2/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p534#2/r8.claim: They inherited and learned scripture but neglected to act by it, violated its rulings, and took bribes in God's judgments from fleeting worldly gain.
TAB-FULL:v10p534#2/r8.anchor: ورثوا كتاب الله: تعلموه، وضيعوا العمل به فخالفوا حكمه، يرشون في حكم الله

TAB-FULL:v10p534#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p534#2/r9.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p534#2/r9.claim: “The nearer present gain” is near in contrast to the more distant future life.
TAB-FULL:v10p534#2/r9.anchor: يعني بالأدنى: الأقرب من الآجل الأبعد

TAB-FULL:v10p534#2/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p534#2/r10.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p534#2/r10.claim: After taking the bribe, they presumptuously tell themselves God will forgive them, making false wishes about Him.
TAB-FULL:v10p534#2/r10.anchor: ويقولون إذا فعلوا ذلك: إن الله سيغفر لنا ذنوبنا، تمنيا على الله الأباطيل

TAB-FULL:v10p534#2/r11.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p534#2/r11.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p534#2/r11.claim: He connects their corrupt use of scripture for a little worldly gain with the warning about people who write scripture and sell it for a small price.
TAB-FULL:v10p534#2/r11.anchor: كما قال جل ثناؤه فيهم: {فويل للذين يكتبون الكتاب بأيديهم ثم يقولون هذا من عند الله ليشتروا به ثمنا قليلا

TAB-FULL:v10p534#2/r12.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p534#2/r12.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p534#2/r12.claim: Whenever a similar unlawful bribe or sin appears, they take it and deem it lawful; this persistence shows they do not repent.
TAB-FULL:v10p534#2/r12.anchor: وإن شرع لهم ذنب حرام مثله من الرشوة بعد ذلك أخذوه واستحلوه، ولم يرتدعوا عنه

TAB-FULL:v10p538/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p538/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v10p538/r1.claim: Saʿīd b. Jubayr explains that they commit sins, expect forgiveness, and repeat the sin if it presents itself again.
TAB-FULL:v10p538/r1.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير: " {وإن يأتهم عرض مثله يأخذوه} [الأعراف: 169] قال: من الذنوب

TAB-FULL:v10p538/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p538/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v10p538/r2.claim: Mujāhid says they seize whatever worldly gain attracts them, lawful or unlawful, hoping for forgiveness and taking it again when it appears.
TAB-FULL:v10p538/r2.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد: " {يأخذون عرض هذا الأدنى} [الأعراف: 169] قال: ما أشرف لهم من شيء في اليوم من الدنيا حلال أو حرام

TAB-FULL:v10p538/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p538/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v10p538/r3.claim: Mujāhid says they seek or merely wish for forgiveness after taking worldly gain, then repeat the behavior when more appears.
TAB-FULL:v10p538/r3.anchor: أبو سعد، عن مجاهد: " {يأخذون عرض هذا الأدنى} [الأعراف: 169] قال: لا يشرف لهم شيء من الدنيا إلا أخذوه حلالا كان أو حراما

TAB-FULL:v10p538/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p538/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v10p538/r4.claim: Qatāda calls them evil successors after their prophets and messengers, linking them to those who abandoned prayer and followed desires.
TAB-FULL:v10p538/r4.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: " {فخلف من بعدهم خلف} [الأعراف: 169] أي: والله لخلف سوء ورثوا الكتاب بعد أنبيائهم

TAB-FULL:v10p538/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p538/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v10p538/r5.claim: Qatāda says they indulge in false hopes of forgiveness and take each worldly temptation, lawful or unlawful, without being deterred by the earlier one.
TAB-FULL:v10p538/r5.anchor: قال: {يأخذون عرض هذا الأدنى ويقولون سيغفر لنا} [الأعراف: 169] تمنوا على الله أماني وغرة يغترون بها

TAB-FULL:v10p539/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p539/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v10p539/r1.claim: Qatāda says they take the offered gain whether lawful or unlawful, and repeat this when another such gain comes.
TAB-FULL:v10p539/r1.anchor: عن معمر، عن قتادة: " {يأخذون عرض هذا الأدنى} [الأعراف: 169] قال: يأخذونه إن كان حلالا وإن كان حراما

TAB-FULL:v10p539/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p539/r2.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v10p539/r2.claim: Al-Suddī recounts that Israelite judges pledged not to take bribes, yet each appointed judge did so, claimed forgiveness when rebuked, and was later replaced by another who repeated it.
TAB-FULL:v10p539/r2.anchor: عن السدي، قوله: " {فخلف من بعدهم خلف} [الأعراف: 169] إلى قوله: {ودرسوا ما فيه} [الأعراف: 169] قال: كانت بنو إسرائيل لا يستقضون

TAB-FULL:v10p539/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p539/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v10p539/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says they take whatever comes their way, lawful or unlawful, and say they will be forgiven.
TAB-FULL:v10p539/r3.anchor: عن أبيه، عن ابن عباس، قوله: " {فخلف من بعدهم خلف ورثوا الكتاب يأخذون عرض هذا الأدنى ويقولون سيغفر لنا} [الأعراف: 169] يقول: يأخذون ما أصابوا

TAB-FULL:v10p539/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p539/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v10p539/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd says their gain can be a book they authored; they use bribes to rule for claimants and invoke their invented text for an oppressor, though Torah condemns him.
TAB-FULL:v10p539/r4.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: " {يأخذون عرض هذا الأدنى} [الأعراف: 169] قال: الكتاب الذي كتبوه

TAB-FULL:v10p539#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p539#2/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v10p539#2/r1.claim: Saʿīd b. Jubayr glosses their taking the present worldly gain as committing sins.
TAB-FULL:v10p539#2/r1.anchor: عن منصور، عن سعيد بن جبير، قوله: " {فخلف من بعدهم خلف ورثوا الكتاب يأخذون عرض هذا الأدنى} [الأعراف: 169] قال: يعملون الذنوب

TAB-FULL:v10p540/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p540/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p540/r1.claim: The covenant on these bribing judges was God's covenant with Israelites to uphold the Torah and act by it; the verse reproaches them for breaking it.
TAB-FULL:v10p540/r1.anchor: وهو أخذ الله العهود على بني إسرائيل بإقامة التوراة والعمل بما فيها

TAB-FULL:v10p540/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p540/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p540/r2.claim: They were bound not to attribute to God anything beyond what He revealed to Moses in Torah or to lie about Him.
TAB-FULL:v10p540/r2.anchor: ولا يضيفوا إليه إلا ما أنزله على رسوله موسى صلى الله عليه وسلم في التوراة، وأن لا يكذبوا عليه

TAB-FULL:v10p540/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p540/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v10p540/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās applies the covenant against false claims about God to their presuming He must forgive sins they repeat without repentance.
TAB-FULL:v10p540/r3.anchor: عن ابن جريج، قال: قال ابن عباس: " {ألم يؤخذ عليهم ميثاق الكتاب أن لا يقولوا على الله إلا الحق} [الأعراف: 169] قال: فيما يوجبون على الله من غفران ذنوبهم

TAB-FULL:v10p540#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p540#2/r1.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v10p540#2/r1.claim: Ibn Zayd glosses “studied it” as knowing the Book and its contents, connecting it to the description of teaching and studying scripture.
TAB-FULL:v10p540#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: " { ودرسوا ما فيه} [الأعراف: 169] قال: علموه وعلموا ما في الكتاب

TAB-FULL:v10p540#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p540#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p540#2/r2.claim: The afterlife's reward is better for those who fear God, obey His commands, and preserve the limits He set in scripture.
TAB-FULL:v10p540#2/r2.anchor: مما أعد لأوليائه والعاملين بما أنزل في كتابه المحافظين على حدوده

TAB-FULL:v10p540#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p540#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p540#2/r3.claim: The rebuke asks bribing judges to recognize that the afterlife's reward for just, God-fearing conduct is better than a small worldly payment from unjust judgments.
TAB-FULL:v10p540#2/r3.anchor: إن ما عند الله في الدار الآخرة للمتقين العادلين بين الناس في أحكامهم، خير من هذا العرض القليل

SULAMI:v1p247#4/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p247#4/r1.speaker: قيل
SULAMI:v1p247#4/r1.claim: The revealed books conveyed through intermediaries had clarified that God should only be described in terms of His will and exalted power.
SULAMI:v1p247#4/r1.anchor: قيل : ألم يبين لهم على لسان الوسائط في الكتب المنزلة أن لا يصفوا الحق إلا بنفاد المشيئة وعلو القدرة

SULAMI:v1p247#4/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p247#4/r2.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v1p247#4/r2.claim: “They studied what was in it” means that they abandoned acting upon it.
SULAMI:v1p247#4/r2.anchor: قال سهل في قوله ﴿ ودرسوا ما فيه ﴾ تركوا العمل به

TABATABAI:7:169/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:169/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:169/r1.claim: The worldly العرض is what has no permanence in worldly affairs; عرض هذا الأدنى means the transient goods of this present life.
TABATABAI:7:169/r1.anchor: أي ما لا ثبات له من شؤونها، والمراد بعرض هذا الأدنى عرض هذه الحياة الدنيا والدار العاجلة

TABATABAI:7:169/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:169/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:169/r2.claim: The masculine demonstrative treats the worldly prize as an unspecified thing, ignoring its qualities to belittle it; Abraham's description of the sun as this is greater is a parallel.
TABATABAI:7:169/r2.anchor: أشير إليها بلفظ التذكير لأخذها شيئا ليس له من الخصوصيات إلا أن يشار إليه تجاهلا بخصوصياتها تحقيرا لشأنها

TABATABAI:7:169/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:169/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:169/r3.claim: Their claim that they will be forgiven is arbitrary self-deception, grounded in their conceit that they are God's chosen tribe, not in a stated condition of repentance.
TABATABAI:7:169/r3.anchor: قول جزافي لهم قالوه، ولا معول لهم فيه إلا الإغترار بشعبهم الذي سموه شعب الله

TABATABAI:7:169/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:169/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:169/r4.claim: This is not sincere hope: genuine hope entails fear of the opposite outcome and an inner balance of calm and anxiety, attraction and aversion, joy and sorrow.
TABATABAI:7:169/r4.anchor: فإن للرجاء آثارا لا تلائم هذه المشيئة إذ رجاء الخير لا ينفك عن خوف الشر الذي يقابله

TABATABAI:7:169/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:169/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:169/r5.claim: People immersed in worldly desire invoke God's forgiveness only to escape blame and return to pleasure; this is false wishful thinking and satanic temptation, unlike the call to righteous action in 18:110.
TABATABAI:7:169/r5.anchor: قال إن الله غفور رحيم يتخلص به من اللوم، ويخلص به إلى صافي لذائذه الدنية فليس ما يتظاهر به رجاء صادقا

TABATABAI:7:169#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:169#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:169#2/r1.claim: Taking every similar worldly gain shows that they did not repent after the first one; their claim of forgiveness is no true repentance or hope, and they intend to repeat the sin, like those who did not stop one another from evil.
TABATABAI:7:169#2/r1.anchor: كلما وجدوا شيئا من عرض الدنيا أخذوه من غير أن يراقبوا الله تعالى فيه

TABATABAI:7:169#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:169#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:169#2/r2.claim: He prefers taking the wāw in ودرسوا as circumstantial, with the clause describing عليهم; joining it to ورثوا الكتاب is possible but unlikely.
TABATABAI:7:169#2/r2.anchor: كأن الواو للحال، والجملة حال عن ضمير { عليهم } وقيل الجملة معطوفة

TABATABAI:7:169#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:169#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:169#2/r3.claim: A later generation inherited scripture with its knowledge, rulings, admonitions, and lessons, which should have led them to piety and the lasting afterlife; instead they pursued immediate pleasures and repeated sins.
TABATABAI:7:169#2/r3.anchor: وتحملوا ما فيه من المعارف والأحكام والمواعظ والعبر، وكان لازمه أن يتقوا ويختاروا الدار الآخرة

TABATABAI:7:169#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:169#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:169#2/r4.claim: The covenant was taken when they undertook the Book; because they had studied it, they knew their claim of assured forgiveness was false and that it emboldened sin and undermined religion.
TABATABAI:7:169#2/r4.anchor: وهو الميثاق المأخوذ عليهم عند حملهم إياه { أن لا يقولوا على الله إلا الحق } والحال أنهم

TABATABAI:7:169#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:169#2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:169#2/r5.claim: The afterlife is better for the God-fearing because its reward lasts and it is safe from every harm; the closing question rebukes their failure to reason.
TABATABAI:7:169#2/r5.anchor: لدوام ثوابها وأمنها من كل مكروه { أ فلا تعقلون }

TUSTARI:7:169/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:7:169/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:7:169/r1.claim: They studied what the Scripture contained by abandoning the practice of it.
TUSTARI:7:169/r1.anchor: ما فيه } [169] أي تركوا العمل به

TABRISI:7:169-170/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:169-170/r2.speaker: السلمي
TABRISI:7:169-170/r2.claim: Al-Sulamī’s noncanonical wādārasū is from tadārasū with assimilation.
TABRISI:7:169-170/r2.anchor: وفي الشواذ قراءة السلمي وادارسوا ما فيه أراد تدارسوا فأدغم

TABRISI:7:169-170/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:169-170/r3.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:7:169-170/r3.claim: Al-Zajjāj distinguishes khalaf, a generation following another, from khulf, what replaces something lost.
TABRISI:7:169-170/r3.anchor: قال الزجاج: يقال للقرن الذي يجيء في أثر قرن خلف

TABRISI:7:169-170/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:169-170/r4.speaker: الفراء
TABRISI:7:169-170/r4.claim: Al-Farrāʾ uses khalaf ṣidq for a good successor and khalaf sūʾ for a bad one; fatḥ is more often used for praise.
TABRISI:7:169-170/r4.anchor: قال الفراء: يقال هو خلف صدق وخلف سوء

TABRISI:7:169-170/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:169-170/r5.speaker: علي بن عيسى
TABRISI:7:169-170/r5.claim: ʿAlī b. ʿĪsā says khalaf and khulf can substitute for one another.
TABRISI:7:169-170/r5.anchor: قال علي بن عيسى: وقد يوضع أحدهما مكان الآخر

TABRISI:7:169-170/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:169-170/r6.speaker: لبيد
TABRISI:7:169-170/r6.claim: Labīd’s verse uses khalaf for a disfavored successor generation, comparing them to mange-ridden skin.
TABRISI:7:169-170/r6.anchor: ذهب الذين يعاش في أكنافهم وبقيت في خلف كجلد الأجرب

TABRISI:7:169-170/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:169-170/r7.speaker: حسان
TABRISI:7:169-170/r7.claim: Ḥassān’s verse uses khalaf for followers of earlier people in obedience to God.
TABRISI:7:169-170/r7.anchor: لنا القدم الأولى إليك وخلفنا لأولنا في طاعة الله تابع

TABRISI:7:169-170/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:169-170/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:169-170/r8.claim: ʿAraḍ is a transient thing with little duration; the philosophical term for an accident follows from its impermanence beside bodies.
TABRISI:7:169-170/r8.anchor: والعرض ما يعرض ويقل لبثه ومنه سمي العرض القائم بالجسم عرضا

TABRISI:7:169-170/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:169-170/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:169-170/r9.claim: Dars is repetition: rereading a book or repeated rain and wind erasing a house’s trace.
TABRISI:7:169-170/r9.anchor: والدرس تكرير الشيء ويقال درس الكتاب إذا كرر قراءته

TABRISI:7:169-170/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:169-170/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:169-170/r11.claim: Yaʾkhudhūna ʿaraḍa is a circumstantial accusative; wariṯū al-kitāb describes khalaf, and darasū is conjoined to wariṯū.
TABRISI:7:169-170/r11.anchor: يأخذون عرض هذا الأدنى في موضع النصب على الحال من الضمير في ورثوا

TABRISI:7:169-170/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:169-170/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:169-170/r12.claim: The covenant clause through illā al-ḥaqq is parenthetical between wariṯū and darasū; there is no pause before mā fīhi.
TABRISI:7:169-170/r12.anchor: اعتراض بين ورثوا ودرسوا ولا يجوز الوقف من أول الآية إلا على قوله ما فيه

TABRISI:7:169-170/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:169-170/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:169-170/r15.claim: The verse turns from earlier generations to successors; inheriting the Book means inheriting the Torah.
TABRISI:7:169-170/r15.anchor: معناه فذهب أولئك وقام مقامهم قوم آخرون ورثوا الكتاب يعني التوراة

TABRISI:7:169-170/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:169-170/r16.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:7:169-170/r16.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says worldly goods are present enjoyment consumed by both righteous and wicked people.
TABRISI:7:169-170/r16.anchor: عن ابن عباس يقال الدنيا عرض حاضر يأكل منه البر والفاجر

TABRISI:7:169-170/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:169-170/r17.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:169-170/r17.claim: One view says they took bribes and issued unjust judgments; another says they took bribes but judged rightly; either way it was paltry gain.
TABRISI:7:169-170/r17.anchor: وقيل: إنهم كانوا يرتشون ويحكمون بجور

TABRISI:7:169-170/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:169-170/r18.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:169-170/r18.claim: Al-adnā may mean immediate gain or this low, transient world.
TABRISI:7:169-170/r18.anchor: وأراد بقوله هذا الأدنى هذا العاجل

TABRISI:7:169-170/r19.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:169-170/r19.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:169-170/r19.claim: Their claim of forgiveness exposes greed and persistence: they take whatever appears, lawful or unlawful, while presuming God will forgive.
TABRISI:7:169-170/r19.anchor: وهذا إخبار عن حرصهم على الدنيا وإصرارهم على الذنوب

TABRISI:7:169-170/r20.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:169-170/r20.speaker: ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير ومجاهد
TABRISI:7:169-170/r20.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Saʿīd b. Jubayr, and Mujāhid say they take a later unlawful bribe and treat it as lawful, showing persistence.
TABRISI:7:169-170/r20.anchor: وقيل: معناه وإن جاءهم حرام من الرشوة وغيرها بعد ذلك أخذوه

TABRISI:7:169-170#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:169-170#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:169-170#2/r1.claim: The judges had covenanted in the Torah not to lie about God or attribute anything beyond what He revealed to Moses; it promises no forgiveness while sin persists.
TABRISI:7:169-170#2/r1.anchor: معناه ألم يؤخذ على هؤلاء المرتشين في الأحكام القائلين سيغفر لنا إذا عوتبوا

TABRISI:7:169-170#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:169-170#2/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:169-170#2/r2.claim: One gloss says they read the Torah and remembered its contents.
TABRISI:7:169-170#2/r2.anchor: أي وقرؤوا ما فيه فهم ذاكرون لذلك

TABRISI:7:169-170#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:169-170#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:169-170#2/r3.claim: Alternatively, darasū is conjoined to wariṯū: they inherited and studied the Book but neglected and failed to act on it.
TABRISI:7:169-170#2/r3.anchor: وقيل: إنه معطوف على قوله ورثوا الكتاب

TABRISI:7:169-170#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:169-170#2/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:169-170#2/r4.claim: The afterlife’s reward for people who obey God is better for those avoiding His disobedience.
TABRISI:7:169-170#2/r4.anchor: ما أعده الله لأوليائه في الدار الآخرة من النعيم والثواب

TABRISI:7:169-170#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:169-170#2/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:169-170#2/r5.claim: With yāʾ, the question asks whether this group understands; with tāʾ, Muhammad is told to ask them whether they understand.
TABRISI:7:169-170#2/r5.anchor: من قرأ بالياء فمعناه أفلا يعقل هذه الطائفة
