TABRISI:7:169-170#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:169-170#2/r8.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:7:169-170#2/r8.claim: Al-Ḥasan says no amount of gain satisfies them.

FARRA:v1p397/r15.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p397/r15.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p397/r15.claim: In the phrase about those who inherited the Book, خلف means a generation, with the lām quiescent.
FARRA:v1p397/r15.anchor: أضاعوا الصلاة أي قرن، بجزم اللام.

FARRA:v1p397/r16.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p397/r16.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p397/r16.claim: الخَلَف is what replaces something lost; one may pray for someone to receive a replacement, or call someone خلف سوء.
FARRA:v1p397/r16.anchor: والخلف: ما استخلفته، تقول: أعطاك الله خلفا مما ذهب لك، وأنت خلف سوء

THALABI:v4p299/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p299/r1.speaker: النضر بن شميل
THALABI:v4p299/r1.claim: Nadr distinguishes the bad form with a still lām from the Quranic good successor, whose lām is open.
THALABI:v4p299/r1.anchor: وقال النضر بن شميل: الخلف بجزم اللام وإسكانها في غير القرآن السوء واحد، فأما في القرآن الصالح [بفتح] اللام لا غير

THALABI:v4p299/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p299/r2.speaker: محمد بن جرير الطبري
THALABI:v4p299/r2.claim: Al-Tabari says praise usually has an open lām and blame a still one, though both forms sometimes occur in either use.
THALABI:v4p299/r2.anchor: قال محمد بن جرير الطبري: أكثر ما جاء في المدح بفتح اللام وفي الذم بتسكينها وقد تحرك في الذم وتسكن في المدح

THALABI:v4p299/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p299/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p299/r3.claim: The blameworthy sense may derive from spoiled milk left in a skin or the corrupted smell of a fasting mouth.
THALABI:v4p299/r3.anchor: إذا وجه إلى الفساد مأخوذ من قولهم: خلف اللبن وحمض من طول تركه في السقاء حتى تفسد، ومن قولهم: خلف فم الصائم

THALABI:v4p299/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p299/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p299/r4.claim: ʿAraḍ means all worldly goods; with a still rāʾ, al-ʿaraḍ means property other than dirhams and dinars.
THALABI:v4p299/r4.anchor: والعرض متاع الدنيا أجمع. والعرض بسكون الراء ما كان من المال سوى الدراهم والدنانير

THALABI:v4p299/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p299/r5.speaker: المفسرون
THALABI:v4p299/r5.claim: The exegetes say the Jews inherited and studied scripture but neglected its commands, took bribes in judgments, and altered the book and the Messenger's description.
THALABI:v4p299/r5.anchor: قال المفسرون: [إن] اليهود ورثوا كتاب الله فقرأوه وعلموه وضيعوا العمل به وخالفوا حكمه يرتشون في حكم الله وتبديل كتاب الله وتغيير صفة رسول الله

THALABI:v4p299/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p299/r6.speaker: المفسرون
THALABI:v4p299/r6.claim: They presumptuously imagined that sins done by night would be erased by day, and sins done by day by night.
THALABI:v4p299/r6.anchor: ويقولون سيغفر لنا ذنوبنا ما عملناه بالليل كفر عنا بالنهار، وما عملناه بالنهار كفر عنا بالليل تمنيا على الله الأباطيل

THALABI:v4p299/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p299/r7.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
THALABI:v4p299/r7.claim: Said ibn Jubayr reads the repeated taking as committing another sin when it presents itself.
THALABI:v4p299/r7.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير: وإن عرض لهم ذنب آخر عملوه

THALABI:v4p299/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p299/r8.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v4p299/r8.claim: Mujahid says they seize any desired worldly opportunity, lawful or unlawful, and keep hoping for forgiveness.
THALABI:v4p299/r8.anchor: وقال مجاهد: ما أشرف لهم في اليوم من شيء من الدنيا الحلال أو حرام يشتهونه أخذوه

THALABI:v4p299/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p299/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p299/r9.claim: The word وهف means that something was easy or readily available to them.
THALABI:v4p299/r9.anchor: وكلما وهف لهم شيء من الدنيا أكلوه وأخذوا من الدنيا، ما وهف أي ما سهل

THALABI:v4p299/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p299/r10.speaker: السدي
THALABI:v4p299/r10.claim: Al-Suddi reports that Israelite judges repeatedly took bribes despite a covenant and rebuke; later Jews of Yathrib likewise repeated their predecessors' conduct after covenanting with the Prophet.
THALABI:v4p299/r10.anchor: قال السدي: كانت بنو إسرائيل لا يستقضون قاضيا إلا ارتشى في الحكم. وإن خيارهم اجتمعوا فأخذوا منهم بعض العهود أن لا يفعلوا

THALABI:v4p299/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p299/r11.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p299/r11.claim: Al-adnā describes the worldly life with masculine agreement because the feminine noun dunyā is omitted and the wording is treated as masculine.
THALABI:v4p299/r11.anchor: والأدنى تذكير الدنيا وعرض هذه الدار الدنيا فلما ترك الاسم المؤنث ذكر النعت لتذكير اللفظ

THALABI:v4p301/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p301/r1.speaker: أبو بكر محمد بن عبد
THALABI:v4p301/r1.claim: An unnamed, partially identified authority says the phrase is reordered: they take the lowly worldly gain before the intervening covenant clause.
THALABI:v4p301/r1.anchor: سمعت أبا بكر محمد بن عبد [ ... ] يقول فيه تقديم وتأخير أي: يأخذون هذا العرض الأدنى

THALABI:v4p301/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p301/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p301/r2.claim: The phrase means that they studied and read what the scripture contains.
THALABI:v4p301/r2.anchor: أن لا يقولوا على الله إلا الحق ودرسوا ما فيه وقرءوا ما فيه

THALABI:v4p301/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p301/r3.speaker: السلمي
THALABI:v4p301/r3.claim: Al-Sulami reads ادارسوا, meaning تدارسوا: they studied it together and taught one another.
THALABI:v4p301/r3.anchor: وقرأ السلمي: ادارسوا أي تدارسوا مثل إذا زكوا أي قارأ بعضهم بعضا

THALABI:v4p301/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p301/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p301/r4.claim: Most readers use the third-person ya form as a statement; al-Hasan and Ibn al-Ashhab use the second-person address.
THALABI:v4p301/r4.anchor: أفلا تعقلون بالياء قرأ أكثر القراء على الخبر. وقرأ الحسن وابن الأشهب بالتاء على الخطاب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p428#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p428#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p428#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says a later generation of Jews came after the people God had dispersed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p428#2/r1.anchor: فخلف من بعد هؤلاء الذين قطعناهم خلف من اليهود

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p428#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p428#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس عن عطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p428#2/r2.claim: In Ata's report, Ibn Abbas explains the successors as descendants, the children of those dispersed across the lands.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p428#2/r2.anchor: وقال في رواية عطاء: (يريد: نسلا منهم)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p428#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p428#2/r3.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p428#2/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj says khalaf can mean a generation following another, or something that replaces what was taken; the replacement sense can also be spelled khalaf.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p428#2/r3.anchor: يقال للقرن الذي يجيء في أثر قرن: خلف، والخلف ما أخلف عليك بدلا مما أخذ منك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p428#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p428#2/r4.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p428#2/r4.claim: Al-Farra reads khalaf with a quiescent lām as a generation, and khalaf as what one appoints to replace what has gone.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p428#2/r4.anchor: وقال الفراء: {خلف} أي: قرن بجزم اللام، والخلف ما استخلفته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p428#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p428#2/r5.speaker: أحمد بن يحيى
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p428#2/r5.claim: Ahmad ibn Yahya says the common distinction is khalaf with fatḥa for a good successor and sukūn for a bad one; Abu Ubayda also held this, though he alone allowed sukūn for a good successor too.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p428#2/r5.anchor: وقال أحمد بن يحيى: (الناس كلهم يقولون: خلف صدق وخلف سوء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p428#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p428#2/r6.speaker: الأزهري عن الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p428#2/r6.claim: Al-Azhari reports al-Farra allowing khalaf with sukūn for both good and bad generations, explaining that it denotes a generation; he says this agrees with Abu Ubayda.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p428#2/r6.anchor: الخلف يذهب به إلى الذم، والخلف خلف صالح، وقد يكون في الرديء خلف وفي الصالح خلف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p428#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p428#2/r7.speaker: حسان
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p428#2/r7.claim: Hassan's verse uses khalaf with a quiescent lām for righteous successors, supporting the permissive usage.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p428#2/r7.anchor: ينشد لحسان: لنا القدم الأولى عليهم وخلفنا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p428#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p428#2/r8.speaker: ابن السكيت
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p428#2/r8.claim: Ibn al-Sikkit says one uses khalaf ṣidq and khalaf sūʾ, with the form unchanged for singular and plural, and cites poetry for the pejorative form.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p428#2/r8.anchor: يقال: هذا خلف صدق، وهذا خلف سوء، وهؤلاء خلف سوء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p428#2/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p428#2/r9.speaker: أصحاب العربية
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p428#2/r9.claim: The grammarians derive pejorative khalaf from corruption, citing the idiom nṭaqa khalfan for bad speech and khalafa for spoiled wine or a foul-smelling mouth.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p428#2/r9.anchor: الخلف المستعمل في الذم مأخوذ من الخلف، وهو الفساد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p428#2/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p428#2/r10.speaker: النضر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p428#2/r10.claim: Al-Nadr allows both vowelings for a bad generation but only fatḥa for a good one; most lexicographers agree, except al-Farra and Abu Ubayda, who allow sukūn for the good.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p428#2/r10.anchor: الخلف بتحريك اللام وإسكانها في القرن السوء واحد، فأما في القرن الصالح فتحريك اللام لا غير

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p431/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p431/r1.speaker: أبو عبيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p431/r1.claim: Abu Ubayd distinguishes ʿaraḍ with fatḥa as all worldly goods from ʿarḍ with sukūn as goods other than coined gold and silver; the latter is pluralized as ʿurūḍ.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p431/r1.anchor: جميع متاع الدنيا عرض بفتح الراء، يقال: إن الدنيا عرض حاضر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p431/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p431/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p431/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says they took whatever temptation appeared, lawful or unlawful, including bribes and similar gains.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p431/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬1): (يأخذون الطمع إذا عرض لهم حلالا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p431/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p431/r3.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p431/r3.claim: Ata's report from Ibn Abbas explains the phrase as whatever worldly benefit presented itself to them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p431/r3.anchor: وقال عطاء عنه: (يريد: ما أشرف لهم من الدنيا)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p431/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p431/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p431/r4.claim: Al-Adnā is a masculine adjective for al-dunyā: the feminine noun for this worldly abode is omitted, leaving its adjective masculine.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p431/r4.anchor: و {الأدنى} تذكير (الدنيا) وأراد عرض هذه الدار الدنيا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p431/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p431/r5.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p431/r5.claim: The commentators condemn Jews who inherited, read, and learned scripture but abandoned its practice and rulings, taking bribes in judgment and altering the Book and the Messenger's description.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p431/r5.anchor: المفسرون: (ذم الله تعالى بهذه الآية اليهود {ورثوا الكتاب} فقرؤوه، وعلموه، وضيعوا (¬6) العمل به

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p433/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p433/r1.speaker: ابن عباس والمفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p433/r1.claim: They wished for forgiveness, supposing sins committed by night would be erased by day and those committed by day by night.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p433/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬1) والمفسرون (¬2): (كانوا يتمنون على الله المغفرة، يقولون: ما عملنا بالليل كفر عنا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p433/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p433/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p433/r2.claim: He explains the repeated offer as another bribe like the one they accepted the previous day.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p433/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (إذا أصابوا عرضا مثل رشوتهم تلك التي أصابوا بالأمس قبلوه)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p433/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p433/r3.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p433/r3.claim: Mujahid says they take whatever worldly thing is offered, lawful or unlawful, hope for forgiveness, and take another like it the next day.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p433/r3.anchor: وقال مجاهد: {يأخذون عرض هذا الأدنى}، ما أشرت لهم اليوم شيء من الدنيا حلال أو حرام أخذوه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p433/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p433/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p433/r4.claim: On Mujahid's reading, al-adnā means the current, nearest day.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p433/r4.anchor: فالأدنى على هذا عبارة عن اليوم الأدنى، وهو اليوم الذي هم فيه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p433/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p433/r5.speaker: قتادة والسدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p433/r5.claim: Qatada and al-Suddi take the passage as reporting their persistence in sin.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p433/r5.anchor: ونحو هذا قال قتادة (¬7) والسدي (¬8) وقالوا: (هذا إخبار عن إصرارهم على الذنوب)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p433/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p433/r6.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p433/r6.claim: Al-Hasan reads the conduct as greed for worldly life: nothing satisfies them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p433/r6.anchor: وقال الحسن: (هذا إخبار عن حرصهم على الدنيا، وأنهم لا يشبعهم شيء)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p434/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p434/r1.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p434/r1.claim: Ataa reports from Ibn Abbas that the Torah firmly enjoined them to speak only truth about God, but they spoke falsely.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p434/r1.anchor: قال عطاء عن ابن عباس: (وكد الله في التوراة {أن لا يقولوا على الله إلا الحق}، فقالوا الباطن)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p434/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p434/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p434/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies their claim that they would be forgiven as their false statement about God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p434/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (يعني: قولهم: {سيغفر لنا}، فذلك قولهم على الله غير الحق)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p434/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p434/r3.speaker: ابن جريج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p434/r3.claim: Ibn Jurayj says they falsely expected forgiveness for sins they repeatedly committed without repenting.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p434/r3.anchor: وقال ابن جريج: (أي: فيما يرجون على الله من مغفرة ذنوبهم التي لا يزالون يعودون لها ولا يتوبون منها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p434/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p434/r4.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p434/r4.claim: Al-Zajjaj says repeated acceptance shows persistence; God's promise of forgiveness for grave sins that merit Hell is conditional on repentance.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p434/r4.anchor: وقال الزجاج: (قوله: {وإن يأتهم عرض} يدل على إصرارهم على الذنب، والله عز وجل وعد بالمغفرة في العظائم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p434/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p434/r5.speaker: بعض المفسرين
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p434/r5.claim: Some exegetes clarify that the Torah does not promise forgiveness while a person persists in sin.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p434/r5.anchor: قاله بعض المفسرين قال: (ليس في التوراة ميعاد المغفرة مع الإصرار)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p434/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p434/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p434/r6.claim: They remember the covenant imposed on them because they had read the scripture.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p434/r6.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {ودرسوا ما فيه} أي: فهم ذاكرون لما (¬5) أخذ عليهم

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p174#5/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p174#5/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p174#5/r1.claim: Khalf means inferior people or speech; an expression such as “this is khalf of speech” uses it for something bad.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p174#5/r1.anchor: فخلف من بعدهم خلف} والخلف: الرديء من الناس ومن الكلام،

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:169/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:169/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:169/r1.claim: The later generation were Jewish descendants of those previously destroyed and inherited scripture from their fathers.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:169/r1.anchor: { فخلف من بعدهم خلف } من بعد هؤلاء الذين قطعناهم خلف من اليهود. يعني: أولادهم { ورثوا الكتاب } أخذوه عن آبائهم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:169/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:169/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:169/r2.claim: They took whatever worldly gain came their way, lawful or unlawful.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:169/r2.anchor: { يأخذون عرض هذا الأدنى } يأخذون ما أشرف لهم من الدنيا حلالا أو حراما

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:169/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:169/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:169/r3.claim: Their expectation of forgiveness was wishful presumption about God.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:169/r3.anchor: { ويقولون سيغفر لنا } ويتمنون على الله المغفرة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:169/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:169/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:169/r4.claim: They accepted similar property again, showing their greed for worldly gain and repeated taking of bribes.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:169/r4.anchor: { وإن يأتهم عرض مثله يأخذوه } وإن أصابوا عرضا، أي: متاعا من الدنيا مثل رشوتهم تلك التي أصابوا بالأمس قبلوه.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:169/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:169/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:169/r5.claim: The Torah covenant forbade false claims about God; their claim of forgiveness was false because the Torah promises none while sin persists.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:169/r5.anchor: { ألم يؤخذ عليهم ميثاق الكتاب أن لا يقولوا على الله إلا الحق } وأكد الله عليهم في التوراة ألا يقولوا على الله إلا الحق فقالوا الباطل، وهو قولهم: { سيغفر لنا } وليس في التوراة ميعاد المغفرة مع الإصرار

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:169/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:169/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:169/r6.claim: They remembered the covenant because they had read the scripture.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:169/r6.anchor: { ودرسوا ما فيه } أي: فهم ذاكرون لما أخذ عليهم الميثاق؛ لأنهم قرؤوه.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:169/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:169/r1.speaker: Zemahşerî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:169/r1.claim: Zamakhshari identifies the new generation as Jews of the Prophet’s time and their inherited scripture as the Torah of that era.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:169/r1.anchor: Zemahşerî’ye göre buradaki “yeni kuşak”tan maksat, Hz. Peygamber dönemindeki yahudiler, vâris oldukları kitap ise o günkü Tevrat’tır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:169/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:169/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:169/r2.claim: The transient worldly benefit they took is understood to have been bribes received in court.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:169/r2.anchor: aldıkları geçici dünya menfaatinin de mahkemelerde aldıkları rüşvet olduğu söylenir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:169/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:169/r3.speaker: Taberî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:169/r3.claim: Tabari reports bribery was so widespread among Jews that people blamed those who refused it; a bribing judge excused himself by expecting forgiveness.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:169/r3.anchor: Taberî’nin kaydettiğine göre o dönemlerde yahudiler arasında rüşvet o kadar yaygındı ki, rüşvet almak istemeyenleri suçlarlardı.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:169/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:169/r4.speaker: bazı rivayetler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:169/r4.claim: Some reports identify the generation described in the verse as Christians.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:169/r4.anchor: Bazı rivayetlerde âyette sözü edilen bu kuşağın hıristiyanlar olduğu ileri sürülmüşse de

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:169/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:169/r5.speaker: Taberî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:169/r5.claim: Tabari rejects the Christian identification as unsupported by the Quran; the context concerns Jews and offers no evidence for another community.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:169/r5.anchor: bu rivayetleri aktaran Taberî’ye göre Kur’an’ın desteklemediği bu fikri kabul etmek mümkün değildir; âyetin bağlamı sadece yahudilerle ilgili

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:169/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:169/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:169/r6.claim: The Jews took unlawful wealth such as bribes, presumed they would be forgiven—perhaps because they falsely believed themselves God’s chosen nation—and continued sinning instead of repenting.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:169/r6.anchor: Yahudiler hem rüşvet ve benzeri yollarla haram malları alırlar, yiyip içerler hem de bu günahlarından dolayı tövbe edecekleri yerde

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:169/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:169/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:169/r7.claim: Their presumption of forgiveness is plausibly connected to the false belief that they were an elite nation before God.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:169/r7.anchor: muhtemelen Tanrı katında seçkin bir millet oldukları yolundaki bâtıl inançlarından dolayı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:169/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:169/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:169/r8.claim: Scripture repeatedly records their covenant to avoid sin and unlawful consumption, know God, and obey His commands; the commentary points to 2:40.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:169/r8.anchor: Allah ile bu şekilde ahidleşmişlerdi (ayrıntılı bilgi için bk. Bakara 2/40)

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:169/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:169/r9.speaker: Kurtubî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:169/r9.claim: Qurtubi rightly says presuming forgiveness after unlawful acts is a failing shared by Muslims, not a problem unique to Jews.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:169/r9.anchor: Kurtubî –haklı olarak– rüşvet almak gibi haramlar işleyip sonra da “Nasıl olsa Allah affeder” şeklinde boş ümitlere kapılmanın sadece yahudilere mahsus bir hastalık olmadığını

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:169/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:169/r10.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:169/r10.claim: The duties in these and similar verses also bind Muslims, since there is no religious difference in these matters.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:169/r10.anchor: bu ve benzeri âyetlerin müslümanları da bağladığını, çünkü bu konularda dinler arasında bir farklılık bulunmadığını

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:169/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:169/r11.speaker: M. Reşîd Rızâ
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:169/r11.claim: Rashid Rida deplores that Muslims, especially clergy, commit unlawful acts while relying on wishful thinking about forgiveness and intercession, which matter only for those pleasing to God.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:169/r11.anchor: M. Reşîd Rızâ da müslümanların, özellikle din adamlarının aynı illete müptelâ olmalarından yakınmakta

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:169/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:169/r12.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:169/r12.claim: God reminds people that the afterlife is better than transient worldly pleasure and that only the God-fearing, who honor His commands and avoid sin, grasp and act on this choice.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:169/r12.anchor: “geçici menfaat ve zevkler” anlamındaki dünya ile âhiret arasında bir tercih yapmak gerektiğinde âhireti tercih etmenin daha yararlı olduğunu

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:169/r13.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:169/r13.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:169/r13.claim: The closing appeal invites people to use reason to understand the wisdom and beneficial consequences of revealed information and reports.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:169/r13.anchor: insanların, kendilerine vahiyle bildirilen bu bilgi ve haberlerdeki hikmetleri ve yararlı sonuçları akıllarıyla da kavrayabileceklerine işaret etmektedir

BURHAN:v1p98/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p98/r1.speaker: أم سلمة
BURHAN:v1p98/r1.claim: Abū Dāwūd transmits from Umm Salama that the Prophet recited verse by verse and paused at each, including the basmala, to teach the verse endings.
BURHAN:v1p98/r1.anchor: روى أبو داود عن أم سلمة لما سئلت عن قراءة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قالت كان يقطع قراءته آية آية

BURHAN:v1p98/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p98/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p98/r2.claim: Zarkashī rejects calling this simply a Prophetic Sunnah pause: consistent pauses establish an ending and consistent linkage excludes one, while occasional pauses may teach endpoints, mark a full stop, or allow rest.
BURHAN:v1p98/r2.anchor: قال ووهم فيه من سماه وقف السنة

BURHAN:v1p98/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p98/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p98/r3.claim: A second method analogically assigns plausible verse boundaries not explicitly transmitted; it changes only pausing or linking, neither adding to nor subtracting from the Qur'an.
BURHAN:v1p98/r3.anchor: الثانى القياسى وهو ما ألحق من المحتمل غير المنصوص بالمنصوص لمناسب ولا محذور فى ذلك لأنه لا زيادة فيه ولا نقصان

BURHAN:v1p98/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p98/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p98/r4.claim: Verse endings resemble prose rhyme and poetic line endings: ordinary rhyme defects do not apply, and endings may shift rhyme types in Qur'an, rhymed prose, and rajaz unlike the ode.
BURHAN:v1p98/r4.anchor: فاصلة الآية كقرينة السجعة فى النثر وقافية البيت فى النظم وما يذكر من عيوب القافية من اختلاف الحذو والإشباع والتوجيه فليس بعيب فى الفاصلة

ITQAN:v1p270#3/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p270#3/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p270#3/r1.claim: Early readers completed a separate full recitation for each transmission; combining readings in one completion arose in the fifth century and became standard, restricted to experts.
ITQAN:v1p270#3/r1.anchor: الذي كان عليه السلف أخذ كل ختمة برواية لا يجمعون رواية إلى غيرها إلا أثناء المائة الخامسة فظهر جمع القراءات في الختمة الواحدة واستقر عليه العمل

ITQAN:v1p270#3/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p270#3/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p270#3/r2.claim: Combining required mastery of individual readings and their transmission routes; some permitted one completion per reader among the seven, but Nafiʿ and Ḥamza required separate completions for each transmitter.
ITQAN:v1p270#3/r2.anchor: ولم يكونوا يسمحون به إلا لمن أفرد القراءات وأتقن طرقها وقرأ لكل قارئ بختمة على حدة

ITQAN:v1p270#3/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p270#3/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p270#3/r3.claim: Once a student had completed both separate and combined readings with a recognised, authorising shaykh and reached mastery, he need not repeat separate completions.
ITQAN:v1p270#3/r3.anchor: إذا رأوا شخصا أفرد وجمع على شيخ معتبر وأجيز وتأهل وأراد أن يجمع القراءات في ختمة لا يكلفونه الإفراد

ITQAN:v1p270#3/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p270#3/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p270#3/r4.claim: Egyptians combine by repeating each disputed word’s forms before moving on; Syrians combine by reciting each reader to a pause in turn. The first is exact and easier but less graceful; the second strengthens recall and takes longer.
ITQAN:v1p270#3/r4.anchor: أحدهما الجمع بالحرف بأن يشرع في القراءة فإذا مر بكلمة فيها خلف أعادها بمفردها

ITQAN:v1p270#3/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p270#3/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p270#3/r5.claim: Some readers combined by verse using the stopping method.
ITQAN:v1p270#3/r5.anchor: وكان بعضهم يجمع بالآية على هذا الرسم

ITQAN:v1p270#3/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p270#3/r6.speaker: أبو الحسن القيجاطي
ITQAN:v1p270#3/r6.claim: Al-Qayjāṭī lists seven conditions, summarised as five: sound pause, sound beginning, good performance, and avoiding mixed readings; the shaykh prompts a student who combines incompatible forms.
ITQAN:v1p270#3/r6.anchor: وذكر أبو الحسن القيجاطي في قصيدته وشرحها الجامع القراءات شروطا سبعة حاصلها خمسة أحدها حسن الوقف ثانيها حسن الابتداء ثالثها حسن الأداء رابعها عدم التركيب

ITQAN:v4p457/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p457/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v4p457/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās disapproved taking payment for copying a muṣḥaf.
ITQAN:v4p457/r1.anchor: أخرج ابن أبي داود في كتاب المصاحف عن ابن عباس أنه كره أخذ الأجرة على كتابة المصحف

ITQAN:v4p457/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p457/r2.speaker: أيوب السختياني
ITQAN:v4p457/r2.claim: Ayyūb al-Sakhtiyānī is reported to share Ibn ʿAbbās’s disapproval of payment for copying a muṣḥaf.

ITQAN:v4p457/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p457/r3.speaker: ابن عمر وابن مسعود
ITQAN:v4p457/r3.claim: Ibn ʿUmar and Ibn Masʿūd disapproved of buying or selling muṣḥafs and hiring someone to copy them.
ITQAN:v4p457/r3.anchor: وأخرج عن ابن عمر وابن مسعود أنهما كرها بيع المصاحف وشراءها وأن يستأجر على كتابتها

ITQAN:v4p457/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p457/r4.speaker: مجاهد وابن المسيب والحسن
ITQAN:v4p457/r4.claim: Mujāhid, Ibn al-Musayyib, and al-Ḥasan permitted selling and buying muṣḥafs and being paid to write them.
ITQAN:v4p457/r4.anchor: وأخرج عن مجاهد وابن المسيب والحسن أنهم قالوا لا بأس بالثلاثة

ITQAN:v4p457/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p457/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
ITQAN:v4p457/r5.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr permitted sale, reasoning that sellers receive compensation for their handiwork.
ITQAN:v4p457/r5.anchor: وأخرج عن سعيد بن جبير أنه سئل عن بيع المصاحف فقال لا بأس إنما يأخذون أجور أيديهم

ITQAN:v4p457/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p457/r6.speaker: ابن الحنفية
ITQAN:v4p457/r6.claim: Ibn al-Ḥanafiyya permitted sale, explaining that what is sold is the paper.
ITQAN:v4p457/r6.anchor: وأخرج عن ابن الحنفية أنه سئل عن بيع المصحف قال لا بأس إنما تبيع الورق

ITQAN:v4p457/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p457/r7.speaker: عبد الله بن شقيق
ITQAN:v4p457/r7.claim: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shaqīq says the Prophet’s Companions were strict about selling muṣḥafs.
ITQAN:v4p457/r7.anchor: وأخرج عن عبد الله بن شقيق قال كان أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يشددون في بيع المصاحف

ITQAN:v4p457/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p457/r8.speaker: النخعي
ITQAN:v4p457/r8.claim: Al-Nakhaʿī says a muṣḥaf may neither be sold nor inherited.
ITQAN:v4p457/r8.anchor: وأخرج عن النخعي قال المصحف لا يباع ولا يورث

ITQAN:v4p457/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p457/r9.speaker: ابن المسيب
ITQAN:v4p457/r9.claim: Ibn al-Musayyib disliked selling muṣḥafs and urged people to help a fellow Muslim by lending or gifting one.
ITQAN:v4p457/r9.anchor: وأخرج عن ابن المسيب أنه كره بيع المصاحف وقال أعن أخاك بالكتاب أوهب له

ITQAN:v4p457/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p457/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v4p457/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, through ʿAṭāʾ, said one should buy muṣḥafs but not sell them.
ITQAN:v4p457/r10.anchor: وأخرج عن عطاء عن ابن عباس قال اشتر المصاحف ولا تبعها

ITQAN:v4p457/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p457/r11.speaker: مجاهد
ITQAN:v4p457/r11.claim: Mujāhid prohibited selling muṣḥafs while allowing their purchase.
ITQAN:v4p457/r11.anchor: وأخرج عن مجاهد أنه نهى عن بيع المصاحف ورخص في شرائها

ITQAN:v4p457/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p457/r12.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p457/r12.claim: The reports yield three early positions; the author prefers disliking sale while allowing purchase, calling it the strongest view and citing al-Shāfiʿī’s text.
ITQAN:v4p457/r12.anchor: وقد حصل من ذلك ثلاثة أقوال للسلف ثالثها كراهة البيع دون الشراء وهو أصح الأوجه عندنا

ITQAN:v4p457/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p457/r13.speaker: الرافعي
ITQAN:v4p457/r13.claim: Al-Rāfiʿī reports two explanations of the price: it pays for the covers because God’s speech is not sold, or compensates the copying work.
ITQAN:v4p457/r13.anchor: قال الرافعي وقد قيل إن الثمن متوجه إلى الدفتين لأن كلام الله لا يباع وقيل إنه بدل من أجرة النسخ

ITQAN:v4p457/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p457/r14.speaker: الشعبي
ITQAN:v4p457/r14.claim: Al-Shaʿbī permits sale because the payment is for both paper and the seller’s labor.
ITQAN:v4p457/r14.anchor: أخرج ابن أبي داود عن الشعبي قال لا بأس ببيع المصاحف إنما يبيع الورق وعمل يديه

ITQAN:v1p169/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p169/r1.speaker: ابن حجر
ITQAN:v1p169/r1.claim: Ibn Ḥajar takes the wording to suggest that Companions arranged sūra verses by their own judgment; the author says other reports show they acted only by prophetic instruction.
ITQAN:v1p169/r1.anchor: قال ابن حجر ظاهر هذا أنهم كانوا يؤلفون آيات السور باجتهادهم وسائر الأخبار تدل على أنهم لم يفعلوا شيئا من ذلك إلا بتوقيف

ITQAN:v1p169/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p169/r4.speaker: مكي وغيره
ITQAN:v1p169/r4.claim: Makkī and others say verse order within sūras was set by the Prophet; al-Tawba lacks an opening basmala because he gave no instruction to place one.
ITQAN:v1p169/r4.anchor: وقال مكي وغيره ترتيب الآيات في السور بأمر من النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ولما لم يأمر بذلك في أول براءة تركت بلا بسملة

ITQAN:v1p169/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p169/r5.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر
ITQAN:v1p169/r5.claim: Al-Qāḍī Abū Bakr says arranging verses is obligatory: Gabriel instructed where each verse should be placed.
ITQAN:v1p169/r5.anchor: وقال القاضي أبو بكر في الانتصار ترتيب الآيات أمر واجب وحكم لازم فقد كان جبريل يقول ضعوا آية كذا في موضع كذا

ITQAN:v1p169/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p169/r6.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر
ITQAN:v1p169/r6.claim: Al-Qāḍī Abū Bakr holds that the Uthmanic codex contains all unretracted revelation, with verse order preserved from God and His Messenger; whether the Prophet ordered sūras himself or entrusted them to the community, the latter seems likelier.
ITQAN:v1p169/r6.anchor: وقال القاضي أبو بكر في الانتصار ترتيب الآيات أمر واجب وحكم لازم

ITQAN:v1p169/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p169/r7.speaker: مالك
ITQAN:v1p169/r7.claim: Mālik, as transmitted by Ibn Wahb, says the Qurʾān was arranged according to what people heard from the Prophet.
ITQAN:v1p169/r7.anchor: عن ابن وهب قال سمعت مالكا يقول إنما ألف القرآن على ما كانوا يسمعون من النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

ITQAN:v1p169/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p169/r8.speaker: البغوي
ITQAN:v1p169/r8.claim: Al-Baghawī says the Companions gathered the Qurʾān without adding, subtracting, or rearranging it; their task was collection in one place, while Gabriel taught the order now in the codices. Revelation order differs from recitation order.
ITQAN:v1p169/r8.anchor: وقال البغوي في شرح السنة الصحابة رضي الله عنهم جمعوا بين الدفتين القرآن الذي أنزله الله على رسوله

TABATABAI:7:167-169/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:167-169/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:167-169/r8.claim: Al-'arad means something without permanence, which is why worldly gain is described as a transient offering.

ELMALILI:7:164-170#2/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:164-170#2/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:164-170#2/r12.claim: A corrupt later generation inherited the Torah, learned to read and write, and entered teaching, legal-religious, and judicial offices, yet did not uphold its rulings.
ELMALILI:7:164-170#2/r12.anchor: Tevrat seleflerinden bunların ellerine intikal etmiş, okumasını yazmasını öğrenmişler, neşr ü tâlim, iftâ ve hüküm mevki‘lerine geçmişler

ELMALILI:7:164-170#2/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:164-170#2/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:164-170#2/r13.claim: They took fleeting worldly goods and bribes, altered or concealed truth, presumed they would be forgiven, and accepted further bribes without repenting.
ELMALILI:7:164-170#2/r13.anchor: bir rüşvet daha arz olunursa yine alıyorlar, tevbe etmiyorlar

ELMALILI:7:164-170#2/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:164-170#2/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:164-170#2/r14.claim: Their covenant under the Book required them to say nothing about God except the truth.
ELMALILI:7:164-170#2/r14.anchor: Vaktiyle kendilerinden Allah’a karşı haktan başka bir şey söylemeyeceklerine dair o kitabın mîsâkı alınmadı mı?

ELMALILI:7:164-170#2/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:164-170#2/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:164-170#2/r15.claim: They had repeatedly studied the covenant and the truths they now conceal, including the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet, and the matters of piety.
ELMALILI:7:164-170#2/r15.anchor: O mîsâkı ve bugün ketm ü tahrif ettikleri hakikatleri, o Resûl, o Nebiyy-i Ümmî, o ittikā meselelerini vaktiyle tekrar tekrar okudular

ELMALILI:7:164-170#2/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:164-170#2/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:164-170#2/r16.claim: Elmalılı explains the pious as those who avoid injustice, bribery, and illicit gain, and asks whether the offenders will not reason that the afterlife is better for them.
ELMALILI:7:164-170#2/r16.anchor: âhiret evi müttakī olanlar -yani öyle haksızlıktan, rüşvet ü irtikâbdan sakınıp korunanlar- için ayn-ı hayrdır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:167/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:167/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:167/r9.claim: Condemning an entire people is irrational and unethical, conflicts with Qur'anic justice, and ignores Israel's hope of mercy in 17:4–8 if they do not return to evil; verses 168–170 affirm justice for Jews and all people.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:167/r9.anchor: bir toplumu bu şekilde toptan mahkûm etmek hem aklen ve ahlâken doğru değildir hem de bizzat Kur’an-ı Kerîm’in herkese ve her topluma hak ettiği şekilde muamele edileceğini ve hiçbir kimseye hiçbir şekilde haksızlık yapılmayacağını belirten açıklamalarına

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:167/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:167/r12.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:167/r12.claim: The author finds the Moses-era identification implausible because dispersion began later; 7:169's opening points to Jewish groups living before Islam.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:167/r12.anchor: Zira dağılma süreci Hz. Mûsâ’dan sonra başlamıştır.

AKHFASH:v1p341/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p341/r2.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p341/r2.claim: Khalf may mean any generation after a prior one, whether a replacement or not; khalaf can mean a substitute that takes the predecessor's place and fills its role.
AKHFASH:v1p341/r2.anchor: و"الخلف" الذي هو بدل مما كان قبله قد قام مقامه

AKHFASH:v1p341/r3.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p341/r3.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p341/r3.claim: ʿAraḍ is property other than dirhams and dinars, which are ʿayn; more broadly it is anything that comes across a person, including trouble or opportunity.
AKHFASH:v1p341/r3.anchor: وقال {يأخذون عرض هذاالأدنى} فأضاف "العرض" إلى "هذا" وفسر "هذا" ب"الأدنى"

AKHFASH:v1p341/r4.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p341/r4.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p341/r4.claim: The related expressions ʿaraḍa lahu and aʿraḍa laka describe something coming across one's path; the cited poem uses muʿriḍan for facing the spears.
AKHFASH:v1p341/r4.anchor: وتقول: "أعرض لك الخير" و"عرض لك الخير"

AKHFASH:v1p341/r5.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p341/r5.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p341/r5.claim: Al-ʿāriḍ of a cloud is what faces you; the passage also says al-ḥabī is what comes from every direction.
AKHFASH:v1p341/r5.anchor: و"العارض" من السحاب: ما استقبلك وهو قول الله عز وجل {فلما رأوه عارضا}

AKHFASH:v1p341/r6.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p341/r6.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p341/r6.claim: Min ʿarḍ al-nās means what is toward you, as in ḍrib bihi ʿarḍ al-ḥāʾiṭ.
AKHFASH:v1p341/r6.anchor: وأما "الحبي": فما كان من كل ناحية وتقول: "خذوه من عرض الناس"

AKHFASH:v1p341/r7.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p341/r7.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p341/r7.claim: The dimension term ʿarḍ, paired with ṭūl, is still-voweled; other uses include the verbal noun ʿarḍan for presenting a house or an affair appearing.

AKHFASH:v1p341/r8.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p341/r8.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p341/r8.claim: The verbs ʿaraḍa and aʿraḍa are explained through the verbal noun ʿarḍan, including presenting a house or an affair appearing.
AKHFASH:v1p341/r8.anchor: و: "عرضت عليه المنزل عرضا" و"عرض لي أمر عرضا" هذا مصدره

AKHFASH:v1p341/r9.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p341/r9.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p341/r9.claim: A line he cites uses ʿaraḍū al-khaṭṭī; he explains ʿaraḍū and aʿraḍū from the root ʿaraḍa.

AKHFASH:v1p341/r10.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p341/r10.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p341/r10.claim: What comes across a person of worldly good can be a benefit; ʿaraḍ min al-khayr wa-l-sharr describes what one encounters and profits from, with bad occurrences also named.
AKHFASH:v1p341/r10.anchor: و"العرض من الخير والشر": ما أصبت عرضا من الدنيا فانتفعت به

DAMGHANI:v1p322/r1.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p322/r1.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p322/r1.claim: ʿArḍ means perishable worldly goods, as in the worldly gain people seek and the transient goods they take.
DAMGHANI:v1p322/r1.anchor: تريدون عرض الدنيا اي ما لا يبقى قال تعالى في سورة الاعراف ياخذون عرض هذا الادنى

ZAJJAJ:v2p387/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p387/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p387/r4.claim: خلف names one who comes after a generation; الخلف can also mean a replacement for what was taken or lost, with fatḥa on the lām in الخلف.
ZAJJAJ:v2p387/r4.anchor: يقال للذي يجيء في أثر قرن خلف. والخلف ما أخلف عليك بدلا مما أخذ منك

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p120/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p120/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p120/r1.claim: Omission can broaden meaning to more than two possibilities; 7:169 exemplifies this through several possible omitted prepositions.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p120/r1.anchor: مثال آخر من الحذف وقد يكون الحذف للتوسع في المعنى يعطي أكثر من احتمالين كما في قوله تعالى

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p120/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p120/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p120/r4.claim: If the omitted preposition is bi, the phrase means that the covenant was taken on this matter; the author calls this a regular deletion.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p120/r4.anchor: محتمل أن يكون المحذوف حرف الباء (بأن يقولوا على الله) بمعنى ألم يؤخذ عليهم ميثاق الكتاب بهذا الأمر وهذا حذف قياسي

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p120/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p120/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p120/r5.claim: A possible omitted fī gives the reading, “the covenant of the Book concerning their saying only the truth about God.”
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p120/r5.anchor: ومحتمل أن يكون المحذوف حرف في (ألم يؤخذ عليهم ميثاق الكتاب في أن يقولوا على الله)

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p120/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p120/r6.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p120/r6.claim: An omitted ʿalā frames the wording as a pact or stipulation, stressing agreement and commitment not to say anything but truth about God.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p120/r6.anchor: حرف على (ألم يؤخذ عليهم ميثاق الكتاب على أن لا يقولوا على الله) وهذا من باب التوافق والتعاهد

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p120/r7.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p120/r7.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p120/r7.claim: An omitted lām gives a purposive sense: the covenant was taken so that they would not say anything about God except the truth.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p120/r7.anchor: ومحتمل أن يكون المحذوف حرف اللام (لئلا يقولوا على الله) وهنا للتعليل

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p120/r8.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p120/r8.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p120/r8.claim: The author allows all these senses together: if God had intended only one, He would have stated the preposition and fixed the meaning.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p120/r8.anchor: فيمكن أن تكون كل هذه المعاني مرادة وكلها مرادة لأنه لو أراد سبحانه معنى منها لذكر أي حرف وحدد المعنى

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p569/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p569/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p569/r3.claim: The covenant phrase allows nine constructions: omitted باء, في, على, or لام; no deletion with البيان or بدل; أن may be explanatory or verbal-noun; and لا may be prohibitive or negative, leaving a broad range of intended senses.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p569/r3.anchor: إذن هناك تسعة احتمالات في هذه الآية الواحدة إحتمال حذف حرف الجر (الباء، في، على، اللام)

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210/r8.speaker: الزجاج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210/r8.claim: Al-Zajjāj says khalaf is a generation that comes after another generation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210/r8.anchor: قال الزجاج: يقال للقرن الذي يجيء بعد القرن خلف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210/r9.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210/r9.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says khalaf can mean the succeeding generation, while khulf means the one installed as a successor; elsewhere he associates khalaf with blame and khulf with a righteous successor.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210/r9.anchor: وقال الفراء: الخلف القرن والخلف من استخلفه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210/r10.speaker: ثعلب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210/r10.claim: Thaʿlab reports the common distinction: “good successor” is khulf ṣidq and “bad successor” is khalaf sūʾ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210/r10.anchor: وقال ثعلب: الناس كلهم يقولون خلف صدق للصالح وخلف سوء للطالح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210/r11.claim: A poem uses khalaf negatively for people who remain after those once cherished, likening them to a scabby hide.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210/r11.anchor: ومنه قول الشاعر: ذهب الذين يعاش في أكنافهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210/r12.claim: The proverb “he was silent for a thousand, then spoke a khalaf” uses khalaf for a long-awaited but bad utterance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210/r12.anchor: والمثل: سكت ألفا ونطق خلفا أي سكت طويلا ثم تكلم بكلام فاسد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210/r13.claim: A line calls a successor blameworthy, while Ḥassān’s verse is cited for the praiseworthy sense; the latter text is cut off here.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210/r13.anchor: وفي الصالح خلف وعلى هذا بيت حسان:

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:168-170/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:168-170/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:168-170/r6.claim: Khalf means a bad successor; as a verbal noun used adjectivally it can refer to one or many, though it is also treated as a collective noun.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:168-170/r6.anchor: خلف } بدل سوء مصدر نعت به ولذلك يقع على الواحد

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:168-170/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:168-170/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:168-170/r7.claim: They inherited the Torah from their ancestors, reading it and knowing what it contained.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:168-170/r7.anchor: التوراة من أسلافهم يقرؤونها ويقفون على ما فيها

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:168-170/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:168-170/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:168-170/r8.claim: This lowly worldly gain may be called near or base; it refers to bribes in judgment and payment for distorting words.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:168-170/r8.anchor: حطام هذا الشيء الأدنى يعني الدنيا، وهو من الدنو أو الدناءة

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:168-170/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:168-170/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:168-170/r9.claim: “They say, ‘We will be forgiven’” may coordinate with the prior verb or be circumstantial; the verb may be construed with the prepositional phrase or as a verbal noun of their taking.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:168-170/r9.anchor: سيغفر لنا } لا يؤاخذنا الله بذلك ويتجاوز عنه

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:168-170/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:168-170/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:168-170/r10.claim: They expect forgiveness while persisting in sin and returning to the same conduct without repentance.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:168-170/r10.anchor: يرجون المغفرة مصرين على الذنب عائدين إلى مثله غير تائبين عنه

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:168-170/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:168-170/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:168-170/r11.claim: The covenant was in the Book; its truth requirement rebukes their certainty of forgiveness without repentance as a lie and breach of the covenant.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:168-170/r11.anchor: المراد توبيخهم على البت بالمغفرة مع عدم التوبة

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:168-170/r12.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:168-170/r12.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:168-170/r12.claim: “They studied what it contained” may coordinate semantically with the covenant question, or with inheriting the Book as an aside.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:168-170/r12.anchor: عطف على { ألم يؤخذ } من حيث المعنى فإنه تقرير

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:168-170/r13.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:168-170/r13.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:168-170/r13.claim: The afterlife is better for the pious than these people’s gains; they should not exchange a base worldly prize that brings punishment for lasting bliss.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:168-170/r13.anchor: ولا يستبدلوا الأدنى الدنيء المؤدي إلى العقاب

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:168-170/r14.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:168-170/r14.speaker: نافع وابن عامر وحفص ويعقوب
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:168-170/r14.claim: They read the verb with tāʾ, shifting the grammatical person.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:168-170/r14.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن عامر وحفص ويعقوب بالتاء

BIQAI-FULL:v3p145/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p145/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p145/r1.claim: The lowly, near display is worldly life; they persist without repentance and confidently assume they will be forgiven.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p145/r1.anchor: أي دائما من غير توبة . ولما كان النافع الغفران من غير نظر إلى معين

BIQAI-FULL:v3p145/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p145/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p145/r2.claim: If another equally base and illicit gain, such as a bribe, comes to them, they take it again.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p145/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p145/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p145/r3.claim: They use the passive form because they seek assurance of forgiveness without naming or considering a particular forgiver.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p145/r3.anchor: من غير نظر إلى معين , بنوا للمفعول قولهم

BIQAI-FULL:v3p145/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p145/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p145/r4.claim: The binding covenant in the Torah requires them to speak only truth about God; asserting certain forgiveness without repentance is not established truth and violates it.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p145/r4.anchor: { ميثاق الكتاب } اي الميثاق المؤكد في التوارة { أن لا يقولوا } أي قولا من الأقوال وإن قل

BIQAI-FULL:v3p145/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p145/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p145/r5.claim: They repeatedly read and memorized the covenant, so they could not excuse their conduct by claiming ignorance of what their forebears received.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p145/r5.anchor: أي ما في ذلك الميثاق بتكرير القراءة للحفظ

BIQAI-FULL:v3p145/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p145/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p145/r6.claim: Their scripture teaches that the afterlife is better than the worldly gains they take; they choose what harms and vanishes over lasting good.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p145/r6.anchor: أي فعلوا ما تقدم من مجانبة التقوى والحال أن الآخرة { خير } أي مما يأخذون { للذين يتقون } أي هم يعملون ذلك بإخبار كتابهم

BIQAI-FULL:v3p145/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p145/r7.speaker: نافع وابن عامر وحفص
BIQAI-FULL:v3p145/r7.claim: On the address-form reading, the question directly addresses them and signals the extremity of divine anger.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p145/r7.anchor: وعلى قراءة نافع وابن عامر وحفص بالخطاب يكون المارد الإعلام بتناهي الغضب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p159/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p159/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p159/r1.claim: If the preceding division means exile among enemy lands, “a successor came after them” follows that account and points to the Jews' return under Cyrus around 530 BCE.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p159/r1.anchor: تفريع على قوله : { وقطعناهم } ( الأعراف : 168 ) إن كان المراد تقطيعهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p159/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p159/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p159/r2.claim: Cyrus permitted Jews captured by Nebuchadnezzar to return; they rebuilt Jerusalem's temple through Nehemiah and Ezra and revived public reading of Moses' law.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p159/r2.anchor: فإنه لما فتح بلاد أشور أذن لليهود الذين أسرهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p159/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p159/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p159/r3.claim: On this reading, inheriting the book means renewing Torah practice through the scroll Ezra produced, Ezra being known in Muslim tradition as ʿUzayr.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p159/r3.anchor: والمراد بإرث الكتاب إعادة مزاولتهم التوراة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p159/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p159/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p159/r4.claim: Taking worldly gain describes only some of the returned successor group, since its first members repented and included prophets and righteous people.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p159/r4.anchor: ويكون أخذهم عرض الأدنى أخذ بعض الخلف لا جميعه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p159/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p159/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p159/r5.claim: If the earlier division means multiplication and favor, the successors are descendants scattered after their ancestors' era, including the Jews in Medina at the rise of Islam; commentators incline to this reading.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p159/r5.anchor: وإلى هذا المعنى في ( الخلف ) نحا المفسرون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p159/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p159/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p159/r6.claim: With a silent lām, khalaf means one who comes after another in place, work, or lineage, as context shows; it does not inherently denote an evil successor.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p159/r6.anchor: والخلف بسكون اللام من يأتي بعد غيره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p159/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p159/r7.speaker: النضر بن شميل
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p159/r7.claim: Al-Naḍr ibn Shumayl says silent-lām khalaf is not mostly used for an evil successor, contrary to many linguists.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p159/r7.anchor: قاله النضر بن شميل ، خلافا لكثير من أهل اللغة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p159/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p159/r8.speaker: كثير من أهل اللغة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p159/r8.claim: Many linguists say silent-lām khalaf most often denotes a bad successor, while open-lām khalaf denotes a good one.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p159/r8.anchor: إذ قالوا : الأكثر استعمال الخلف بسكون اللام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p159/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p159/r9.speaker: البصريون
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p159/r9.claim: The Basran grammarians allow both pronunciations for a bad successor, but use only the open-lām form for a good successor.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p159/r9.anchor: وقال البصريون : يجوز التحريك والإسكان في الرديء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p498/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p498/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p498/r4.claim: A later, bad generation inherited study of the Torah after the mixed earlier generation; Mujāhid identifies them as Christians, though Ibn Kathīr allows that the description may be broader.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p498/r4.anchor: فخلف من بعد ذلك الجيل الذين فيهم الصالح والطالح، خلف آخر لا خير فيهم، وقد ورثوا دراسة [هذا] (2) الكتاب وهو التوراة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p498/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p498/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p498/r5.claim: They traded conveying the truth for worldly gain, indulged themselves, and promised themselves repentance, then repeated the same wrongdoing when an equivalent opportunity came.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p498/r5.anchor: يعتاضون عن بذل الحق ونشره بعرض الحياة الدنيا، ويسرفون أنفسهم ويعدونها بالتوبة،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p498/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p498/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p498/r6.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says they commit a sin, ask God to forgive it, then commit it again when the same opportunity presents itself.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p498/r6.anchor: كما قال سعيد بن جبير: يعملون الذنب، ثم يستغفرون الله منه، فإن عرض ذلك الذنب أخذوه.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p498/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p498/r7.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p498/r7.claim: Mujāhid says they took any worldly gain that came their way, lawful or unlawful, while hoping for forgiveness, and took it again if offered another time.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p498/r7.anchor: وقول مجاهد في قوله: {يأخذون عرض هذا الأدنى} قال: لا يشرف لهم شيء من الدنيا إلا أخذوه،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p498/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p498/r8.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p498/r8.claim: Qatāda calls them a wicked generation that inherited scripture after the prophets and messengers, although God entrusted it to them; he links them to those who neglected prayer and followed desires.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p498/r8.anchor: وقال قتادة في: {فخلف من بعدهم خلف} أي: والله، لخلف سوء،

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r7.claim: The later generation consists of people in the Prophet’s time who inherited the Torah, read its commands, prohibitions, and rulings, but did not act on them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r7.anchor: من بعد المذكورين { خلف } وهم الذين كانوا في زمن رسول الله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r8.claim: عرض هذا الأدنى is the perishable goods of this near or lowly world; the phrasing belittles it, and the people took bribes in judgments to alter wording for commoners.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r8.anchor: أي حطام هذا الشيء الأدنى ، يريد الدنيا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r9.claim: الأدنى can derive from nearness, since worldly gain is immediate, or from low rank, baseness, and smallness.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r9.anchor: الأدنى : إما من الدنو بمعنى القرب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r10.claim: They assume God will not hold them to account for what they took and will forgive them.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r11.claim: The prepositional phrase لنا is the grammatical subject of يغفر; it may alternatively be the verbal noun of يأخذون, ‘the taking.’

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r12.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r12.claim: The wāw is circumstantial: they welcome forgiveness while persisting and returning to the same act without repentance.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r12.anchor: مصرون عائدون إلى مثل فعلهم ، غير تائبين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r13.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r13.claim: Forgiveness of sins requires repentance; a person persisting in sin is not forgiven.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r13.anchor: وغفران الذنوب لا يصح إلا بالتوبة ، والمصر لا غفران له

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r14.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r14.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r14.claim: The covenant refers to the Torah’s rule that a grave sin is forgiven only through repentance.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r14.anchor: من ارتكب ذنبا عظيما فإنه لا يغفر له إلا بالتوبة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r15.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r15.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r15.claim: They had studied the Book’s condition that forgiveness requires repentance.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r15.anchor: في الكتاب من اشتراط التوبة في غفران الذنوب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r16.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r16.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r16.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī polemically says the doctrine of the determinists is exactly the Jews’ doctrine described here.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r16.anchor: والذي عليه المجبرة هو مذهب اليهود بعينه كما ترى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r17.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r17.speaker: مالك بن دينار
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r17.claim: Mālik b. Dīnār warns of people who fall short then presume forgiveness because they avoided polytheism; he calls their attitude wishful thinking and says even their best are complacent, like the people in this verse.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r17.anchor: وعن مالك بن دينار رحمه الله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r18.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r18.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r18.claim: The afterlife is better than that paltry worldly gain for those who avoid bribes and God’s prohibitions.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r18.anchor: والدار الاخرة خير } من ذلك العرض الخسيس

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r19.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r19.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r19.claim: The source lists variants including ورثوا الكتاب, a tāʾ form for إلا تقولوا, وادارسوا meaning تدارسوا, and أفلا تعقلون with yāʾ or tāʾ.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r20.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r20.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r20.claim: أن لا يقولوا على الله إلا الحق can explain ميثاق الكتاب as an apposition: the covenant stated in the Book; claiming forgiveness without repentance then violates it and invents against God.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r21.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r21.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r21.claim: If the covenant means the earlier stipulation, أن لا يقولوا may be its purpose, ‘so they would not say,’ or أن may explain a prohibition: ‘Do not say about God except the truth.’
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r21.anchor: وإن فسر ميثاق الكتاب بما تقدم ذكره كان { أن لا يقولوا } مفعولا له

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r22.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r22.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r22.claim: ودرسوا ما فيه coordinates with ألم يؤخذ عليهم: the covenant was taken from them and they studied its contents.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r22.anchor: على { ألم يؤخذ عليهم } ، لأنه تقرير

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p273#2/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p273#2/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p273#2/r4.claim: Khalaf means successors; with a still lām it is used for blame, with fatḥa for praise. Abu Ubayda says the forms are synonymous, but al-Mawardi prefers the distinction as stronger and more common in poetry.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p273#2/r4.anchor: والخلف بتسكين اللام مستعمل في الذم . وبفتح اللام مستعمل في الحمد . وقال أبو عبيدة . معناها [ واحد ] مثل الأثر والإثر , والأول أظهر وهو في قول الشعراء أشهر

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p273#2/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p273#2/r5.speaker: الفراء
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p273#2/r5.claim: Khalaf may mean a generation, according to al-Farra, or a collective noun for those who succeed, a plural of khālif.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p273#2/r5.anchor: وفي الخلف وجهان : أحدهما : القرن , قاله الفراء . والثاني : أنه جمع خالف .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p273#2/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p273#2/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p273#2/r6.claim: A poet's verse uses khalaf in the blameworthy sense, wishing that the successors had perished instead of the addressee.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p273#2/r6.anchor: قال بعضهم : خلفت خلفا ليت بهم … كان , لا بك التلف

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p273#2/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p273#2/r7.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p273#2/r7.claim: The inheritors may be later generations of Jews who received the Torah from their predecessors, or Christians succeeding the Jews and possessing the Gospel, according to Mujahid.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p273#2/r7.anchor: وفيهم قولان : أحدهما : أنهم من خلف اليهود من أبنائهم . والكتاب الذي ورثوه التوراة لانتقالها لهم . والثاني : أنهم النصارى

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p273#2/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p273#2/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p273#2/r8.claim: “The goods of this lower life” means bribes for judgments, according to all; called goods because they do not last. “Lower” may refer to nearby worldly life or to the moral baseness of forbidden things.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p273#2/r8.anchor: يعني الرشوة على الحكم في قول الجميع وسماه عرضا لقلة بقائه . وفي وصفه بالأدنى وجهان : أحدهما : لأخذه في الدنيا الدانية

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p273#2/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p273#2/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p273#2/r9.claim: They may say they will not be held accountable because the act is forgiven, or acknowledge it as sin while presuming God may forgive it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p273#2/r9.anchor: يحتمل وجهين : أحدهما : أنه مغفور , لا نؤاخذ به . والثاني : أنه ذنب لكن الله قد يغفره لنا تأميلا منهم لرحمته .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p273#2/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p273#2/r10.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p273#2/r10.claim: Mujahid, Qatada, and al-Suddi say taking another bribe shows that they persist in sin.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p273#2/r10.anchor: أحدهما : أنهم أهل إصرار على الذنوب , قاله مجاهد وقتادة والسدي .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p273#2/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p273#2/r11.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p273#2/r11.claim: Al-Hasan says they are insatiable and take more not from need, but because nothing satisfies them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p273#2/r11.anchor: والثاني : أنهم لا يشبعهم شيء , فهم لا يأخذونه لحاجة , قاله الحسن .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p273#2/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p273#2/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p273#2/r12.claim: The covenant may prohibit false judgments about bribery, or may encompass all commands, prohibitions, obedience, and sins.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p273#2/r12.anchor: يحتمل وجهين : أحدهما : ألا يقولوا على الله إلا الحق في تحريم الحكم بالرشا . والثاني : في جميع الطاعات والمعاصي والأوامر والنواهي .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p273#2/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p273#2/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p273#2/r13.claim: The phrase may mean they abandoned the book's teachings until they faded, or studied it, knew its contents, and knowingly persisted in disobeying it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p273#2/r13.anchor: فيه تأويلان : أحدهما : تركوا ما فيه أن يعملوا به حتى صار دارسا . والثاني : أنهم قد تلوه ودرسوه فهم لا يجهلون ما فيه

MUQATIL:7:167-170/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:7:167-170/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:7:167-170/r6.claim: The bad successors who came after the Children of Israel are the Jews, who inherited the Torah from their forebears.
MUQATIL:7:167-170/r6.anchor: { فخلف من بعدهم } ، يعنى من بعد بنى إسرائيل، { خلف } السوء وهم اليهود، { ورثوا الكتاب } ، يعنى ورثوا التوراة عن أوائلهم وآبائهم

MUQATIL:7:167-170/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:7:167-170/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:7:167-170/r7.claim: The near worldly gain is a bribe in judgment; they took bribes by day and claimed forgiveness at night, and took a matching bribe at night while claiming forgiveness by day.
MUQATIL:7:167-170/r7.anchor: { يأخذون عرض هذا الأدنى } ، وهي الدنيا؛ لأنها أدنى من الآخرة، يعنى الرشوة فى الحكم، { ويقولون سيغفر لنا } ، فكانوا يرشون بالنهار

MUQATIL:7:167-170/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:7:167-170/r8.speaker: author
MUQATIL:7:167-170/r8.claim: The Torah covenant forbade them to make the prohibited lawful or speak of God except truth, even though they had read the Torah.
MUQATIL:7:167-170/r8.anchor: يقول الله: { ألم يؤخذ عليهم ميثاق الكتاب } ، يعنى بغير ما يقولون: لقد أخذ عليهم فى التوراة أن لا يستحلوا محرما

MUQATIL:7:167-170/r9.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:7:167-170/r9.speaker: author
MUQATIL:7:167-170/r9.claim: The Hereafter, meaning Paradise, is better for those who avoid declaring forbidden things lawful; the verse asks whether they will reason.
MUQATIL:7:167-170/r9.anchor: { والدار الآخرة } ، يعنى الجنة، { خير للذين يتقون } ، استحلال المحارم، { أفلا تعقلون }
